instructions.instruction: Grease a shallow baking dish with the remaining butter. Arrange a layer of potato slices across the base, season lightly with salt and pepper, then add some of the onions and thyme. Repeat until the ingredients are used, finishing with an overlapping layer of potatoes.
instructions.tip: Keep the layers fairly even so the potatoes cook at the same rate.

instructions.title: Add stock and herbs
instructions.instruction: Pour the hot stock carefully around the edges of the dish until it reaches nearly to the top layer without completely submerging it. Add the bay leaf and remaining thyme.
instructions.tip: Hot stock helps the dish begin cooking evenly in the oven.

instructions.title: Bake until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover the dish loosely with foil and bake for 35 minutes. Remove the foil and continue baking for another 25–35 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden with crisp edges.
instructions.tip: If the top browns before the potatoes are tender, cover loosely and continue baking.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf and allow the potatoes to rest for 5–10 minutes so the stock settles into the layers. Serve hot alongside roast chicken, beef, fish or vegetables.
instructions.tip: Check the centre with a small knife before serving; it should pass through easily.

tips: Waxy potatoes hold their shape, while floury potatoes create a softer, more rustic texture.
Use vegetable stock to keep the dish vegetarian.
Fresh thyme can be replaced with rosemary, but use a smaller amount because its flavour is stronger.

alternatives: Dried thyme, using about one-third the amount

title: Brazilian cheese bread (pão de queijo)
description: Pão de queijo is a beloved Brazilian cheese bread made with tapioca starch, eggs, milk, oil and cheese. The small rolls bake into golden puffs with a crisp shell and a chewy, stretchy centre.

instructions.title: Preheat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper or lightly grease a mini-muffin tin.
instructions.tip: A hot oven helps the rolls puff and develop a lightly crisp exterior.

instructions.title: Heat the liquid ingredients
instructions.instruction: Combine the milk, water, oil and salt in a small saucepan. Heat until just simmering, then remove from the heat.
instructions.tip: Do not boil the mixture for a long time; it only needs to be hot enough to scald the starch.

instructions.title: Scald the tapioca starch
instructions.instruction: Place the tapioca starch in a heatproof bowl. Pour the hot liquid over it and stir firmly with a wooden spoon until the mixture becomes clumpy. Leave to cool for 10–15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Let the mixture cool enough before adding the eggs so they do not cook on contact.

instructions.title: Add eggs and cheese
instructions.instruction: Beat in the eggs one at a time until incorporated. Add the Parmesan and mozzarella and mix until a sticky, elastic dough forms.
instructions.tip: If the dough is too sticky to shape, chill it for 15–20 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the rolls
instructions.instruction: Lightly oil your hands and roll the dough into 18–20 small balls. Arrange them on the prepared tray with space between each.
instructions.tip: Lightly oiled hands make shaping easier without adding excess flour.

instructions.title: Bake until puffed
instructions.instruction: Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the rolls have puffed and their surfaces are lightly golden. Avoid opening the oven repeatedly during baking.
instructions.tip: The rolls should feel set on the outside while remaining chewy inside.

instructions.title: Serve warm
instructions.instruction: Cool the rolls for 3–5 minutes before serving. Enjoy them warm with coffee, tea or as a savoury accompaniment to soup.
instructions.tip: Pão de queijo is at its best shortly after baking, while the centre remains soft and stretchy.

tips: Tapioca starch is essential for the characteristic chewy texture; wheat flour is not an equivalent replacement.
Freeze shaped, unbaked rolls on a tray, then store in a sealed bag and bake from frozen with a few extra minutes.
A little sharp cheese adds flavour and balances the mild mozzarella.

alternatives: Mild cheddar, for a different flavour
Unsweetened plant milk, though texture may vary

title: Breadfruit in Butter Sauce
description: Tender breadfruit simmered and finished in a rich butter sauce with garlic, herbs and a touch of black pepper. This Caribbean-inspired preparation highlights breadfruit's potato-like texture and mildly nutty flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the breadfruit
instructions.instruction: Wash the breadfruit and cut it into quarters. Remove the tough core and peel away the thick skin. Cut the flesh into large, even chunks.
instructions.tip: A firm, mature breadfruit works best for this dish; very ripe fruit will become much softer.

instructions.title: Boil until tender
instructions.instruction: Place the breadfruit chunks in a saucepan and cover with water or vegetable stock. Add a little salt and the thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–30 minutes until a knife passes easily through the flesh.
instructions.tip: Cooking time varies with the size and maturity of the fruit.

instructions.title: Drain the breadfruit
instructions.instruction: Drain the cooked breadfruit thoroughly and remove the thyme stems. Allow the pieces to steam-dry for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.tip: Drying the surface helps the butter sauce cling rather than become watery.

instructions.title: Prepare the butter sauce
instructions.instruction: Melt the butter in a wide skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, taking care not to brown it.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic pale to preserve its sweet, aromatic flavour.

instructions.title: Coat the breadfruit
instructions.instruction: Add the cooked breadfruit to the skillet and gently turn the pieces in the garlic butter. Season with black pepper and additional salt if needed. Cook for 3–5 minutes until heated through.
instructions.tip: Turn the pieces gently because cooked breadfruit can break apart.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in the spring onions and lime juice. Transfer to a serving dish and spoon any remaining butter sauce over the top. Serve warm as a side or light main dish.
instructions.tip: A small amount of lime juice brightens the rich butter without overpowering the breadfruit.

tips: Choose a firm breadfruit with greenish skin for a savoury preparation.
For extra depth, add a little coconut milk to the butter sauce near the end.
Serve alongside grilled fish, roasted chicken or stewed beans.

alternatives: Green plantain, for a different but starchy result
Potatoes, though the flavour will be different
A small pinch of dried thyme

title: Brie wrapped in prosciutto & brioche
description: A festive baked Brie wrapped in savoury prosciutto and buttery brioche, creating a golden exterior around a warm, molten cheese centre. Serve it as a party starter with fruit preserves or crisp apple slices.

ingredients.item: Brioche dough or brioche pastry sheet

instructions.title: Prepare the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Pat the Brie dry and keep it chilled until ready to wrap.
instructions.tip: Cold Brie is easier to wrap and less likely to leak before the pastry sets.

instructions.title: Season the cheese
instructions.instruction: Mix the Dijon mustard, thyme leaves and black pepper. Spread a thin layer over the top and sides of the Brie.
instructions.tip: Use mustard sparingly so it complements rather than overwhelms the cheese.

instructions.title: Wrap with prosciutto
instructions.instruction: Arrange the prosciutto slices slightly overlapping on a board. Place the Brie in the centre and fold the prosciutto around it, covering the sides and top as evenly as possible.
instructions.tip: Overlap the slices to help hold the cheese together as it softens.

instructions.title: Enclose in brioche
instructions.instruction: Roll or flatten the brioche dough into a sheet large enough to enclose the cheese. Place the wrapped Brie in the centre, bring the dough around it and pinch the seams firmly underneath. Place seam-side down on the tray.
instructions.tip: Avoid leaving holes or very thin patches in the dough, which can allow cheese to escape.

instructions.title: Apply the egg wash
instructions.instruction: Brush the exposed brioche evenly with beaten egg. If the dough is very soft, chill the wrapped cheese for 10 minutes before baking.
instructions.tip: Egg wash encourages a glossy, golden crust.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Bake for 25–35 minutes, until the brioche is deeply golden and cooked through. If the crust browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil for the remaining baking time.
instructions.tip: Let the brioche brown fully; underbaked dough will remain heavy around the cheese.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest for 8–10 minutes before cutting. Transfer to a serving board and accompany with fig jam, apple slices or toasted bread.
instructions.tip: The brief rest allows the molten cheese to settle slightly while remaining soft.

tips: Chill the wrapped cheese briefly before baking if the brioche dough becomes difficult to handle.
Serve with a sharp fruit preserve to balance the richness of the cheese.
For even portions, use a sharp knife and cut gently after resting.

title: Bulgarian Green Salad
description: A fresh Bulgarian-style green salad featuring crisp lettuce, cucumber, spring onions, radishes and herbs in a simple lemon and sunflower oil dressing. It is a light, refreshing side dish for grilled meats, cheese or vegetable mains.

instructions.title: Wash and dry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Wash the lettuce, cucumber, radishes, spring onions and green pepper thoroughly. Dry the lettuce and herbs well so the dressing does not become diluted.
instructions.tip: A salad spinner helps remove excess water from the leaves.

instructions.title: Prepare the salad ingredients
instructions.instruction: Chop the lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Slice the cucumber, radishes, spring onions and green pepper, then place everything in a large salad bowl.
instructions.tip: Keep the slices relatively uniform for an even mix of textures.

instructions.title: Add fresh herbs
instructions.instruction: Finely chop the parsley and dill and scatter them over the vegetables. Toss gently to distribute the herbs without bruising the lettuce.
instructions.tip: Fresh dill gives the salad a distinctive aromatic note.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the sunflower oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper in a small bowl until combined.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing before adding it; adjust the acidity with a little more oil if necessary.

instructions.title: Dress the salad
instructions.instruction: Pour the dressing over the vegetables just before serving and toss lightly until the leaves are coated. Add the crumbled sirene cheese if using.
instructions.tip: Dress the salad at the last moment to keep the vegetables crisp.

instructions.title: Serve fresh
instructions.instruction: Transfer to a serving bowl and serve immediately alongside grilled meat, baked vegetables or a savoury pastry.
instructions.tip: Keep any leftovers undressed to preserve their texture.

tips: Use crisp, fresh vegetables for the best texture.
Sirene cheese adds a salty, tangy finish but can be omitted for a dairy-free salad.
Add sliced tomatoes if you want a variation closer to the popular Bulgarian shopska salad.

alternatives: Fresh mint in a smaller quantity

title: Baked brie with sorrel jam
description: Warm baked Brie paired with bright, tangy sorrel jam creates an elegant appetiser that balances creamy cheese with a fruity, gently tart topping. Serve with toasted baguette slices or crisp crackers.

instructions.title: Prepare the sorrel
instructions.instruction: Rinse the sorrel calyces thoroughly and remove any tough stems or unwanted seed pods. Place the cleaned calyces in a saucepan with the water.
instructions.tip: Roselle sorrel is naturally tart; taste the finished jam before adding extra lemon juice.

instructions.title: Cook the jam
instructions.instruction: Add the sugar, optional cinnamon and ginger to the saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the calyces soften and the liquid becomes syrupy.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat gentle to prevent the sugar from scorching.

instructions.title: Finish the jam
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lemon juice and cook for another 2–3 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick. Mash lightly for a rustic jam or blend carefully for a smoother texture, then allow it to cool slightly.
instructions.tip: The jam thickens further as it cools, so it can remain a little loose while hot.

instructions.title: Prepare the Brie
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the Brie wheel in a small ovenproof dish lined with parchment paper. Score the top rind lightly with a sharp knife if desired.
instructions.tip: Use a snug baking dish to contain the cheese as it softens.

instructions.title: Bake the cheese
instructions.instruction: Bake the Brie for 12–18 minutes, until the centre feels soft and molten when gently pressed. Avoid baking so long that the cheese completely collapses.
instructions.tip: The exact time depends on the size and ripeness of the cheese.

instructions.title: Toast the baguette
instructions.instruction: Brush the baguette slices lightly with olive oil and toast in the oven for 5–7 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.
instructions.tip: Toast the bread while the Brie bakes to save time.

instructions.title: Top and serve
instructions.instruction: Spoon some sorrel jam over the warm Brie and serve the remaining jam on the side with the toasted baguette slices.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately while the cheese is soft and easy to spread.

tips: Roselle sorrel is different from the leafy green herb also called sorrel; use the tart red calyces for the jam.
Prepare the jam ahead of time and refrigerate it in a clean sealed jar.
Serve with walnuts or sliced pears for added texture and sweetness.

title: Black Bean soup
description: A hearty black bean soup inspired by Latin American home cooking, simmered with onion, garlic, bell pepper, cumin and smoked paprika. Partially blending the beans creates a thick, satisfying texture, finished with lime and fresh coriander.

instructions.title: Soak the beans
instructions.instruction: Rinse the dried black beans and soak them in plenty of cold water for 8–12 hours. Drain and rinse before cooking.
instructions.tip: Discard the soaking water and use fresh water or stock for the soup.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and oregano and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Cooking the spices briefly in oil helps release their aroma.

instructions.title: Add beans and stock
instructions.instruction: Stir in the drained beans, diced tomatoes, vegetable stock and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 60–90 minutes, until the beans are completely tender.
instructions.tip: Cooking time depends on the age of the beans; add hot water if the soup becomes too thick before they soften.

instructions.title: Season the soup
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf. Add salt and black pepper to taste once the beans are tender, then simmer for another 5 minutes.
instructions.tip: Waiting until the beans soften before final seasoning makes it easier to judge the salt level.

instructions.title: Thicken the soup
instructions.instruction: Use an immersion blender to blend a portion of the soup, leaving plenty of whole beans for texture. Alternatively, transfer two cups to a blender, blend carefully and return to the pot.
instructions.tip: Allow hot soup to cool slightly before blending in a countertop blender, and vent the lid safely.

instructions.title: Finish with lime and herbs
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lime juice and chopped coriander. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding a little more stock or water if the soup is too thick.
instructions.tip: Lime juice added at the end brightens the earthy flavour of the beans.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle the soup into warm bowls. Garnish with extra coriander, diced avocado or a spoonful of yoghurt if desired.
instructions.tip: Serve with warm tortillas, crusty bread or rice for a more substantial meal.

tips: For a faster version, use about 700 g of drained canned black beans and reduce the simmering time to 20–25 minutes.
Add chopped jalapeño with the onions if you prefer a spicier soup.
The soup thickens in the refrigerator; loosen leftovers with stock when reheating.

alternatives: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed
Water with a little extra seasoning

title: Colombian style Stuffed Potatoes
description: Colombian-style stuffed potatoes, inspired by papas rellenas, feature a crisp golden exterior surrounding a savoury filling of seasoned ground beef, onion, tomatoes and spices. They are delicious served hot with ají sauce or a squeeze of lime.

instructions.title: Cook the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Place the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with salted water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain thoroughly and mash until smooth. Let the mash cool.
instructions.tip: Dry potatoes produce a firmer shell that is easier to shape.

instructions.title: Prepare the meat filling
instructions.instruction: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a skillet. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and ground beef. Cook until the beef is browned, breaking it into small pieces.
instructions.tip: Break the beef up finely so the filling can be enclosed evenly.

instructions.title: Season the filling
instructions.instruction: Stir in the tomato, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook for 5–7 minutes until the tomato softens and excess liquid evaporates. Mix in the coriander and let the filling cool.
instructions.tip: A relatively dry filling prevents the potato shells from splitting.

instructions.title: Shape the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Divide the cooled mash into eight portions. Flatten each portion in your palm, place a spoonful of filling in the centre, and carefully close the potato around it. Shape into oval balls.
instructions.tip: Lightly wet or oil your hands if the mash sticks.

instructions.title: Coat the potato balls
instructions.instruction: Set out the flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs in separate shallow bowls. Dust each stuffed potato with flour, dip it in egg, then roll it in breadcrumbs until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: For a sturdier crust, chill the coated potatoes for 15 minutes before frying.

instructions.title: Fry until golden
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep, heavy saucepan. Fry the potatoes in small batches for 4–6 minutes until crisp and golden, turning as needed. Drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan, which lowers the oil temperature.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Allow the potatoes to cool for a few minutes, then serve warm with Colombian-style ají sauce, lime wedges or a fresh salad.
instructions.tip: The filling will be very hot immediately after frying, so let the potatoes rest briefly.

tips: Cool the filling before assembling so the potato shells stay firm.
For a vegetarian filling, use cooked lentils or finely chopped mushrooms instead of beef.
Serve with a fresh chilli and coriander sauce to balance the fried exterior.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup
description: A comforting tomato soup made with ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic and vegetable stock, blended until silky and finished with cream. A little basil and black pepper bring out the sweetness and acidity of the tomatoes.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Wash and chop the tomatoes. Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
instructions.tip: Ripe, flavourful tomatoes give the soup its best taste.

instructions.title: Soften the onion and garlic
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5–7 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic from browning, as burnt garlic can make the soup bitter.

instructions.title: Cook the tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for one minute. Add the chopped tomatoes, oregano, stock and optional sugar. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20–25 minutes until the tomatoes are very soft.
instructions.tip: The optional sugar can balance very acidic tomatoes, but taste before adding it.

instructions.title: Blend the soup
instructions.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat and add the basil leaves. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth. If using a countertop blender, work in batches and vent the lid carefully.
instructions.tip: Blend thoroughly for a velvety texture, or leave a few small pieces if preferred.

instructions.title: Add the cream
instructions.instruction: Return the soup to low heat and stir in the cream. Warm gently for 2–3 minutes without boiling. Season with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Adding cream after blending gives the soup a smoother finish.

instructions.title: Taste and serve
instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust the seasoning. Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with basil leaves or a small swirl of cream. Serve with toasted bread or a grilled cheese sandwich.
instructions.tip: If the soup is too thick, add a splash of stock until it reaches your preferred consistency.

tips: Canned whole tomatoes can replace fresh tomatoes when they are out of season.
Roast the tomatoes first for a deeper, sweeter flavour.
Reheat gently and avoid boiling after adding the cream.

alternatives: A small amount of dried basil

title: Mantu Afghan Dumpling
description: Afghan mantu are delicate steamed dumplings filled with spiced ground beef and onion, served over a garlic yoghurt sauce and topped with a savoury split-pea and tomato sauce. Fresh mint adds a fragrant finish to this traditional dish.

ingredients.amount: 500 ml for the split peas, plus as needed

instructions.title: Cook the split peas
instructions.instruction: Rinse the split peas and place them in a saucepan with 500 ml water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30–40 minutes until tender. Drain any excess liquid.
instructions.tip: Start the split peas first because they take longer than the dumplings to cook.

instructions.title: Prepare the dumpling filling
instructions.instruction: Mix the ground beef with one diced onion, half the minced garlic, ground coriander, cumin, black pepper and salt. Combine thoroughly so the seasoning is evenly distributed.
instructions.tip: Finely diced onion helps the filling cook evenly inside the dumplings.

instructions.title: Shape the mantu
instructions.instruction: Place a small spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper. Moisten the edges with water, fold opposite corners together and press to seal, then bring the remaining corners together to form a compact parcel.
instructions.tip: Keep the unused wrappers covered with a damp towel so they do not dry out.

instructions.title: Make the tomato and split-pea sauce
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan. Add the remaining onion and cook until soft. Stir in the remaining garlic, turmeric and tomato paste, then add the cooked split peas and about 150 ml water. Simmer for 10 minutes until saucy, seasoning to taste.
instructions.tip: Add a little more water if the sauce becomes too thick.

instructions.title: Prepare the yoghurt sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the plain yoghurt with a small pinch of salt, a little water to loosen it and the dried mint. Add a little minced garlic if you prefer a stronger flavour.
instructions.tip: Use thick, unsweetened yoghurt for a creamy base that stays on the plate.

instructions.title: Steam the dumplings
instructions.instruction: Lightly oil a steamer basket and arrange the dumplings in a single layer with space between them. Steam over boiling water for 25–30 minutes, until the wrappers are tender and the beef filling is cooked through.
instructions.tip: Do not let the dumplings touch, as they may stick together during steaming.

instructions.title: Assemble and serve
instructions.instruction: Spread the yoghurt sauce across a serving platter. Arrange the steamed mantu on top, spoon over the split-pea and tomato sauce and finish with dried mint. Serve hot.
instructions.tip: Assemble just before serving so the dumpling wrappers retain their texture.

tips: Prepare and freeze uncooked mantu on a tray before transferring them to a sealed container.
For a milder version, replace part of the beef with finely chopped mushrooms.
Keep the yoghurt sauce cool and add it to the platter immediately before serving.

title: Oyster Mushroom Soup
description: A comforting mushroom soup made with tender oyster mushrooms, onion, garlic and thyme in a savoury stock. A splash of cream adds richness while the mushrooms provide a delicate, earthy flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the mushrooms
instructions.instruction: Brush the oyster mushrooms clean and tear them into bite-sized strips. Dice the onion, mince the garlic and remove the thyme leaves from their stems.
instructions.tip: Avoid soaking mushrooms in water; they can absorb moisture and brown less effectively.

instructions.title: Brown the mushrooms
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in batches and cook for 5–7 minutes until they release their moisture and develop golden edges. Remove and set aside.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches so the mushrooms brown rather than steam.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining butter to the saucepan. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Scrape up the browned mushroom residue to build flavour into the soup.

instructions.title: Thicken the base
instructions.instruction: Stir in the flour and cook for one minute. Gradually whisk in the vegetable stock until smooth, then bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Add the stock slowly to help prevent flour lumps.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Return the mushrooms to the pot, reserving a small handful for garnish if desired. Add the soy sauce and simmer for 10–12 minutes to blend the flavours.
instructions.tip: The soy sauce adds savouriness, so taste before adding extra salt.

instructions.title: Add the cream
instructions.instruction: Stir in the double cream and warm gently for 2–3 minutes without boiling. For a thicker texture, blend a portion of the soup and return it to the pot.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat low after adding cream to maintain a smooth texture.

instructions.title: Season and serve
instructions.instruction: Season with black pepper and salt as needed. Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped parsley and the reserved mushrooms.
instructions.tip: Serve with toasted sourdough or crusty bread.

tips: For a deeper flavour, roast some of the mushrooms before adding them to the soup.
Use vegetable stock and check the soy sauce label for a vegetarian version.
Add a small squeeze of lemon juice just before serving if the soup tastes too rich.

alternatives: A mix of shiitake and button mushrooms

title: Paracuca (Roasted Peanuts)
description: Paracuca is a popular Angolan sweet peanut snack made by coating peanuts in a lightly spiced sugar syrup and allowing the coating to crystallise or set. The result is crunchy, sweet and nutty, with optional cinnamon or vanilla for extra aroma.

ingredients.amount: 300 g, shelled and skin-on or blanched

instructions.title: Prepare the peanuts
instructions.instruction: Inspect the peanuts and remove any damaged pieces. Line a baking tray with parchment paper and set it near the stove for cooling the finished snack.
instructions.tip: Use fresh peanuts with no stale or rancid smell.

instructions.title: Dissolve the sugar
instructions.instruction: Combine the sugar, water and salt in a heavy saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the liquid begins to simmer.
instructions.tip: Use a saucepan large enough to stir the peanuts without spilling.

instructions.title: Cook the peanuts
instructions.instruction: Add the peanuts and stir continuously as the syrup bubbles. Continue cooking for 8–12 minutes, until the liquid reduces and begins to look sandy and crystallised around the nuts.
instructions.tip: Keep stirring as the syrup thickens to prevent scorching.

instructions.title: Develop the coating
instructions.instruction: Lower the heat and continue stirring until the sugar coating clings to the peanuts. If you prefer a glossier caramel-style coating, cook a little longer while watching carefully; add cinnamon or vanilla near the end if using.
instructions.tip: Hot sugar can cause serious burns, so avoid touching or tasting the coating while it is hot.

instructions.title: Spread and cool
instructions.instruction: Immediately spread the coated peanuts over the prepared tray. Separate clusters carefully with a heatproof spatula while the coating is still workable.
instructions.tip: Work quickly because the sugar coating hardens as it cools.

instructions.title: Cool completely
instructions.instruction: Allow the peanuts to cool completely for 20–30 minutes until the coating is firm and crunchy. Break apart any remaining clusters.
instructions.tip: Do not package the peanuts while warm, as trapped moisture can soften the coating.

instructions.title: Store and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the cooled paracuca to an airtight container and serve as a snack or sweet treat.
instructions.tip: Store in a cool, dry place to preserve the crunch.

tips: Stir continuously once the syrup thickens to prevent the sugar from burning.
Add a small pinch of chilli powder for a sweet-and-spicy variation.
Keep the finished peanuts sealed away from humidity.

alternatives: Brown sugar, for a deeper flavour and slightly different coating
Omit for a plain sugar coating

title: Simple heart of palm & tomato salad
description: A fresh, simple salad combining tender hearts of palm with ripe tomatoes, red onion and parsley in a bright lemon and olive oil dressing. Its clean flavours and crisp texture make it a refreshing starter or side dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the hearts of palm
instructions.instruction: Drain the hearts of palm and pat them dry. Slice into rounds about 1 cm thick and place in a salad bowl.
instructions.tip: Handle the slices gently because they can be delicate.

instructions.title: Cut the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and thinly slice the red onion. Chop the parsley and halve the olives if using.
instructions.tip: Use ripe but firm tomatoes so the salad does not become watery.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, optional Dijon mustard, salt and black pepper in a small bowl until combined.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing before mixing it with the vegetables and adjust the acidity to your preference.

instructions.title: Combine the salad
instructions.instruction: Add the tomatoes, red onion, parsley and optional olives to the hearts of palm. Pour over the dressing and toss gently until everything is lightly coated.
instructions.tip: Fold the salad carefully to keep the hearts of palm intact.

instructions.title: Rest briefly
instructions.instruction: Let the salad stand for 5–10 minutes so the flavours combine, without leaving it at room temperature for an extended period.
instructions.tip: If preparing ahead, keep the dressing separate until just before serving.

instructions.title: Serve fresh
instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve chilled or at room temperature as a light starter or accompaniment to grilled fish, chicken or beans.
instructions.tip: A little extra parsley and freshly ground pepper make a simple finishing garnish.

tips: Choose hearts of palm packed in water or brine and rinse them if they taste overly salty.
Add cucumber or avocado for extra freshness and texture.
Serve soon after dressing to keep the tomatoes firm.

title: Algerian Flafla (Bell Pepper Salad)
description: Algerian flafla, also known in related North African preparations as felfel or hmiss, is a smoky cooked pepper salad made with roasted bell peppers, tomatoes, garlic and olive oil. It is served warm or at room temperature with bread as a side or starter.

instructions.title: Roast the peppers
instructions.instruction: Heat the oven grill or broiler to high. Place the peppers on a tray and roast, turning occasionally, until their skins are blistered and blackened in places, about 15–20 minutes.
instructions.tip: Alternatively, roast the peppers over a gas flame or on a hot grill.

instructions.title: Steam and peel
instructions.instruction: Transfer the hot peppers to a covered bowl and leave for 10 minutes. Peel away the loosened skins, remove the stems and seeds, and chop the flesh roughly.
instructions.tip: A little char can remain for a smoky flavour, but remove any excessively burnt skin.

instructions.title: Prepare the tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Score the tomatoes lightly and blanch them in boiling water for 30–45 seconds, then transfer to cold water. Peel and chop them, discarding excess watery seeds if desired.
instructions.tip: Removing the skins helps create a smoother salad texture.

instructions.title: Cook the garlic and spices
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then stir in the cumin, paprika and optional cayenne.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic from browning to avoid bitterness.

instructions.title: Simmer the salad
instructions.instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 8–10 minutes until they soften and release their juices. Stir in the roasted peppers and simmer for another 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is thick.
instructions.tip: Cook until excess liquid evaporates so the salad can be scooped up with bread.

instructions.title: Season and serve
instructions.instruction: Season with salt, stir in the lemon juice and chopped parsley, and remove from the heat. Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.
instructions.tip: Allowing the salad to rest for a short time helps the roasted flavours blend.

tips: Use a mix of red and green peppers for a more complex flavour.
For a heartier variation, fold in a cooked egg near the end.
Keep refrigerated in a sealed container and use within 3 days.

title: Aubergine couscous salad
description: A colourful Mediterranean-inspired couscous salad featuring roasted aubergine, juicy tomatoes, cucumber, fresh herbs and a lemon dressing. Fluffy couscous absorbs the smoky vegetable juices, creating a satisfying salad suitable for lunch or a light dinner.

instructions.title: Roast the aubergine
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Toss the diced aubergine with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, cumin, salt and black pepper. Spread on a lined baking tray and roast for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and browned.
instructions.tip: Spread the aubergine in a single layer so it roasts instead of steaming.

instructions.title: Prepare the couscous
instructions.instruction: Place the couscous in a heatproof bowl. Pour over the hot vegetable stock, cover and leave for 5–8 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff the grains with a fork.
instructions.tip: Avoid stirring the couscous while it absorbs the stock, as this can make it clump.

instructions.title: Chop the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber and finely chop the red onion. Place them in a large mixing bowl.
instructions.tip: Remove excess cucumber seeds if they are particularly watery.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and pepper. Taste and adjust the acidity as needed.
instructions.tip: A little extra lemon juice helps balance the sweetness of roasted aubergine.

instructions.title: Combine the salad
instructions.instruction: Add the fluffed couscous and roasted aubergine to the vegetables. Pour over the dressing, then add the parsley and mint. Toss gently until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Let the aubergine cool slightly before mixing so the cucumber remains crisp.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Leave the salad for 5–10 minutes to allow the flavours to combine. Taste once more, adjust the seasoning and serve at room temperature.
instructions.tip: Add a little olive oil or lemon juice just before serving if the couscous has absorbed all the dressing.

tips: Add chickpeas or crumbled feta for extra protein.
The salad can be prepared ahead, but add cucumber shortly before serving for the freshest texture.
For a gluten-free variation, replace couscous with cooked quinoa.

alternatives: Hot water with a pinch of salt

title: Avocado dip with new potatoes
description: Tender new potatoes served with a creamy avocado dip flavoured with lime, garlic, coriander and yoghurt. This fresh, tangy combination makes an easy appetiser, picnic dish or light lunch.

instructions.title: Wash the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Scrub the new potatoes thoroughly under running water. Leave the skins on and cut any large potatoes in half so the pieces are similar in size.
instructions.tip: Keeping the skins on preserves their delicate texture and flavour.

instructions.title: Boil until tender
instructions.instruction: Place the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the centre.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking, which can cause the potatoes to split.

instructions.title: Drain and season
instructions.instruction: Drain the potatoes thoroughly and let them steam-dry for 2–3 minutes. Toss with the olive oil, a little salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: The warm potatoes absorb seasoning more readily than cold ones.

instructions.title: Prepare the avocados
instructions.instruction: Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a few small pieces if you prefer a chunky dip.
instructions.tip: Choose ripe avocados that yield gently when pressed.

instructions.title: Make the dip
instructions.instruction: Mix the mashed avocado with the yoghurt, lime juice, garlic and chopped coriander. Season with salt, pepper and optional chilli flakes. Stir until creamy.
instructions.tip: Add the lime juice immediately to help slow browning and brighten the flavour.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Arrange the potatoes on a platter and serve warm or at room temperature with the avocado dip alongside. Garnish with extra coriander if desired.
instructions.tip: Keep the dip covered and chilled until serving.

tips: For a dairy-free dip, replace yoghurt with a spoonful of olive oil and a little extra lime juice.
Roast the potatoes instead of boiling them for crisp edges.
Prepare the dip shortly before serving for the best colour and flavour.

title: Beetroot Soup (Borscht)
description: A classic Eastern European-style borscht made with beetroot, cabbage, carrots, potatoes and vegetable stock. The soup has a deep ruby colour and a balance of earthy sweetness and gentle acidity, traditionally served with sour cream and fresh dill.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Peel and grate the beetroot and carrot. Dice the onion and potatoes, shred the cabbage and mince the garlic.
instructions.tip: Wear gloves if desired, as beetroot can stain your hands.

instructions.title: Cook the onion and carrot
instructions.instruction: Heat the sunflower oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5–7 minutes until softened.
instructions.tip: Gentle cooking brings out the sweetness of the vegetables.

instructions.title: Cook the beetroot
instructions.instruction: Add the grated beetroot and tomato paste. Stir well and cook for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Cooking the beetroot briefly in oil helps develop its flavour before the stock is added.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Pour in the vegetable stock and add the potatoes, cabbage and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 25–35 minutes, until the beetroot and potatoes are tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the pot partially covered and add a little water if the soup reduces too much.

instructions.title: Balance the flavour
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust the acidity, adding a little more vinegar if the soup tastes too sweet.
instructions.tip: Acidity helps preserve borscht's bright flavour and balances the earthy beetroot.

instructions.title: Add the dill
instructions.instruction: Stir in most of the chopped dill and simmer for one minute. Remove from the heat and allow the soup to rest for 5 minutes.
instructions.tip: Add fresh herbs near the end so their flavour remains bright.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle into bowls and top each serving with sour cream and the remaining dill. Serve with rye bread or crusty bread.
instructions.tip: Borscht is also delicious chilled, depending on the regional style and season.

tips: For a richer flavour, use vegetable stock with a roasted vegetable base.
A small amount of sugar may be added if the beetroot is unusually earthy, but taste first.
The soup keeps well in the refrigerator and often tastes even better the next day.

title: Black Beans Hotpot
description: A warming black bean hotpot simmered with tomatoes, peppers, onions and smoky spices. The beans create a hearty, protein-rich dish with a thick sauce, ideal for serving with rice, crusty bread or baked potatoes.

ingredients.amount: 700 g, drained and rinsed if canned

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Dice the onion, bell pepper and carrot. Mince the garlic and drain the black beans if using canned beans.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables into similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Soften the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a heavy casserole or saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and carrot and cook for 7–8 minutes until softened.
instructions.tip: Allow the vegetables to soften gradually rather than browning too quickly.

instructions.title: Add the spices
instructions.instruction: Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and optional chilli powder. Cook for one minute until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of stock if the tomato paste begins sticking to the pan.

instructions.title: Build the hotpot
instructions.instruction: Add the diced tomatoes, black beans and vegetable stock. Stir well and bring to a gentle boil.
instructions.tip: Use low-sodium stock if you want more control over the final seasoning.

instructions.title: Simmer until thick
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce has thickened.
instructions.tip: Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to naturally thicken the sauce.

instructions.title: Season and finish
instructions.instruction: Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in the chopped coriander and simmer for another minute.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lime juice can brighten the smoky flavours.

instructions.title: Serve hot
instructions.instruction: Ladle the hotpot into bowls and serve with rice, bread or baked potatoes. Add extra coriander or sliced chilli if desired.
instructions.tip: Allow leftovers to cool promptly and refrigerate in a covered container.

tips: Add sweetcorn or diced courgette for extra vegetables.
For a smoky meat version, stir in cooked chorizo or smoked sausage.
The hotpot thickens after chilling, so add a little stock when reheating.

alternatives: Water with extra herbs and seasoning

title: Braised stuffed cabbage
description: Tender cabbage leaves wrapped around a savoury filling of ground meat, rice, onion and herbs, slowly braised in a tomato-based sauce. This comforting dish appears in many Central and Eastern European cuisines and is excellent served warm with sour cream.

instructions.title: Soften the cabbage leaves
instructions.instruction: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Remove any damaged outer cabbage leaves and carefully cut around the core. Lower the cabbage into the water and cook for 5–8 minutes, peeling away softened leaves as they loosen. Drain and cool.
instructions.tip: If a leaf remains stiff, return it to the boiling water for another minute or two.

instructions.title: Prepare the filling
instructions.instruction: Mix the ground beef, rinsed rice, half the onion, garlic, egg, thyme, paprika, salt and black pepper in a bowl until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Use uncooked rice because it will finish cooking inside the cabbage rolls.

instructions.title: Shape the rolls
instructions.instruction: Trim the thick central rib of each cabbage leaf so it folds easily. Place a portion of filling near the base, fold the sides inward and roll tightly. Repeat until the filling is used.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill the leaves; rice expands as it cooks.

instructions.title: Prepare the tomato sauce
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot. Cook the remaining onion for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the tomato paste and crushed tomatoes, then add the stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Choose a pot wide enough to fit the rolls snugly in one or two layers.

instructions.title: Arrange and braise
instructions.instruction: Place the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the sauce. Spoon a little sauce over the top, cover and simmer gently for 60–75 minutes, until the cabbage is tender, the rice is cooked and the filling reaches a safe internal temperature of 71°C.
instructions.tip: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer rather than a vigorous boil to prevent the rolls from breaking apart.

instructions.title: Check the sauce
instructions.instruction: Carefully remove one roll to check that the rice and meat are fully cooked. Taste the sauce and adjust the salt and pepper. If it is too thin, simmer uncovered for a few minutes.
instructions.tip: Handle the rolls gently when checking because the leaves become delicate after braising.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Serve the stuffed cabbage hot with plenty of tomato sauce and a spoonful of sour cream if desired. Accompany with bread or boiled potatoes.
instructions.tip: Let the rolls rest for 5 minutes before serving so the filling settles.

tips: Prepare the rolls a day ahead and reheat them gently in the sauce.
For a lighter filling, replace half the beef with ground turkey or cooked lentils.
If a cabbage leaf tears, overlap it with another small leaf before filling.

title: Cabbage Soup (Shchi)
description: Shchi is a traditional Russian cabbage soup made with cabbage, potatoes, carrots, onions and stock. This comforting version uses tomatoes for gentle acidity and bay leaf and dill for aroma, with sour cream added at the table.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Shred the cabbage, dice the potatoes and onion, grate the carrot and chop the tomatoes. Mince the garlic.
instructions.tip: Cut the potatoes into similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Soften the onion and carrot
instructions.instruction: Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5–7 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetables lightly coloured rather than deeply browned for a clean soup flavour.

instructions.title: Add the cabbage and stock
instructions.instruction: Stir in the shredded cabbage and cook for 3–4 minutes until it begins to soften. Add the stock, bay leaves and chopped tomatoes, then bring to a boil.
instructions.tip: If the pot seems crowded, add the cabbage in batches as it wilts.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Add the potatoes, reduce the heat and simmer for 25–30 minutes until the cabbage is tender and the potatoes are cooked through.
instructions.tip: Keep the soup at a gentle simmer to preserve the shape of the vegetables.

instructions.title: Season the shchi
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the dried dill, salt and black pepper, then simmer for another 2 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
instructions.tip: If the tomatoes are very acidic, a small pinch of sugar can balance the flavour.

instructions.title: Rest and garnish
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and allow the soup to rest for 5 minutes. Stir in some of the fresh dill, reserving a little for garnish.
instructions.tip: Resting briefly helps the cabbage and broth flavours come together.

instructions.title: Serve hot
instructions.instruction: Ladle into bowls and top each portion with sour cream and fresh dill. Serve with rye bread or crusty bread.
instructions.tip: Shchi often tastes even better the next day after the flavours have developed.

tips: For a heartier version, add cooked beef, chicken or white beans.
Use sauerkraut instead of some fresh cabbage for a tangier variation, adjusting the salt.
Add sour cream at the table rather than boiling it into the soup.

alternatives: A mixture of green cabbage and a little sauerkraut

title: Carrot and Bean Fritters
description: Crispy carrot and bean fritters made with mashed beans, grated carrot, herbs and warming spices. These golden patties are an easy vegetarian snack or lunch option, served with a yoghurt dip, salad or flatbread.

instructions.title: Prepare the beans
instructions.instruction: Drain and rinse the beans thoroughly. Place them in a bowl and mash with a fork until mostly broken down, leaving a few whole pieces for texture.
instructions.tip: Drain the beans well so the fritter mixture is not too wet.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Grate the carrots, finely chop the red onion and mince the garlic. If the grated carrot releases a lot of moisture, squeeze it gently in a clean towel.
instructions.tip: Removing excess moisture helps the patties hold their shape.

instructions.title: Mix the batter
instructions.instruction: Add the carrot, onion, garlic, egg, flour, cumin, coriander, parsley, lemon zest, salt and pepper to the mashed beans. Stir until a thick mixture forms.
instructions.tip: If the mixture feels too loose, add one extra tablespoon of flour.

instructions.title: Shape the fritters
instructions.instruction: Divide the mixture into eight portions and shape into patties about 1.5 cm thick. Place them on a plate and chill for 10 minutes if the mixture feels delicate.
instructions.tip: Use slightly damp hands to make shaping easier.

instructions.title: Fry until golden
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp, working in batches if needed.
instructions.tip: Turn the fritters only once the first side has formed a firm crust.

instructions.title: Drain and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the cooked fritters to a paper towel-lined plate. Serve warm with lemon wedges, yoghurt dip or a fresh green salad.
instructions.tip: Keep cooked fritters warm in a low oven while finishing the remaining batches.

tips: For a gluten-free version, use chickpea flour or a suitable gluten-free flour blend.
Add crumbled feta or grated Parmesan for a saltier, richer fritter.
Reheat leftovers in an oven or air fryer to restore crispness.

alternatives: 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water, rested until gelled

title: Chtitha Batata (Algerian Potato Stew)
description: A comforting Algerian potato stew simmered in a fragrant garlic, tomato, paprika, and cumin sauce. This rustic dish is hearty, warming, and perfect served with crusty bread.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Peel the potatoes and cut them into evenly sized 3 cm cubes. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
instructions.tip: Keep the potato pieces similar in size so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatic base
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Avoid browning the garlic too much, as it can become bitter.

instructions.title: Toast the spices
instructions.instruction: Add the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, coriander, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant and the tomato paste darkens slightly.
instructions.tip: Briefly frying the spices deepens their flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Add the potatoes and vegetable stock. Stir to coat the potatoes, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and cover partially.
instructions.tip: The liquid should mostly surround the potatoes without completely drowning them.

instructions.title: Cook until tender
instructions.instruction: Simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened. Add a splash of water if the pan becomes too dry.
instructions.tip: Mash a few potato pieces into the sauce for a naturally thicker consistency.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot with bread or couscous.
instructions.tip: A little lemon juice balances the rich, spicy sauce.

tips: For a richer stew, replace some vegetable stock with chicken stock.
Adjust the cayenne pepper to control the heat.
The stew thickens as it rests, so add a little water when reheating if necessary.

alternatives: Water with a small amount of stock powder

title: Cottage Cheese And Feta Stuffed Peppers
description: Sweet bell peppers filled with creamy cottage cheese, tangy feta, herbs, and garlic, then baked until tender with a lightly golden filling. These colorful stuffed peppers work as a vegetarian main or a satisfying side dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the peppers
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve the bell peppers lengthwise and remove the seeds and membranes. Arrange them cut-side up in a lightly oiled baking dish.
instructions.tip: Choose peppers with flat bottoms or trim a tiny piece from the underside so they sit securely.

instructions.title: Make the cheese filling
instructions.instruction: In a bowl, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled feta, egg, garlic, oregano, black pepper, and lemon zest. Mix until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: If your cottage cheese is very watery, drain it briefly to keep the filling from becoming loose.

instructions.title: Add the greens
instructions.instruction: Fold the chopped spinach and parsley into the cheese mixture. Taste before adding salt because feta is already salty.
instructions.tip: Thoroughly dry the spinach after washing to avoid excess moisture.

instructions.title: Fill the peppers
instructions.instruction: Divide the filling evenly among the pepper halves, mounding it gently without packing it too tightly.
instructions.tip: Leave a little room at the top so the filling can set without spilling.

instructions.title: Bake until tender
instructions.instruction: Drizzle the peppers with olive oil and bake for 30–35 minutes, until the peppers soften and the filling is set with lightly golden edges.
instructions.tip: Cover loosely with foil if the filling browns before the peppers are tender.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Let the peppers rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve warm with a green salad, rice, or toasted bread.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lemon just before serving brightens the cheese filling.

tips: Use red, yellow, or orange peppers for a sweeter flavor.
For a heartier meal, add cooked quinoa or rice to the filling.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

alternatives: Chopped kale with tough stems removed

title: Creamy Aji green sauce
description: A bright, creamy Peruvian-inspired green sauce made with cilantro, jalapeño, lime, and mayonnaise. It is zesty, herbaceous, and delicious with grilled chicken, roasted vegetables, potatoes, or sandwiches.

ingredients.item: Fresh cilantro, leaves and tender stems

instructions.title: Prepare the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Wash and thoroughly dry the cilantro. Roughly chop the jalapeño and peel the garlic. For a milder sauce, remove the jalapeño seeds and membranes.
instructions.tip: Keep some seeds if you prefer a noticeably spicy sauce.

instructions.title: Blend the herbs
instructions.instruction: Place the cilantro, jalapeño, garlic, lime juice, olive oil, mayonnaise, and sour cream in a blender or food processor.
instructions.tip: A small blender works best for achieving a smooth, creamy texture.

instructions.title: Blend until creamy
instructions.instruction: Blend until the sauce is mostly smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed. Add water one tablespoon at a time until it reaches your preferred consistency.
instructions.tip: Use less water for a thick dip and more for a pourable dressing.

instructions.title: Season to taste
instructions.instruction: Add the salt and black pepper, then blend briefly. Taste and adjust with extra lime juice or salt if needed.
instructions.tip: The sauce should taste fresh and tangy, with the cilantro remaining prominent.

instructions.title: Chill before serving
instructions.instruction: Transfer the sauce to a covered container and refrigerate for at least 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
instructions.tip: The flavor often becomes more balanced after chilling.

instructions.title: Serve and store
instructions.instruction: Serve as a dip or drizzle over grilled meat, roasted potatoes, vegetables, or sandwiches. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
instructions.tip: Use a clean spoon each time and consume within 3–4 days.

tips: For extra heat, add a small piece of serrano pepper.
Blend in a little avocado for a thicker, richer variation.
Keep the sauce refrigerated and do not leave it at room temperature for extended periods.

alternatives: Plain Greek yogurt for a lighter sauce
Mild green chilli for a gentler flavour

title: Creamy Corn Soup Recipe
description: A silky, comforting corn soup made with sweet corn, onion, potato, and stock, finished with cream for a smooth texture. It is easy to prepare and works well as a light lunch or starter.

ingredients.item: Sweet corn kernels, fresh or frozen

instructions.title: Soften the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate so the onion softens without browning heavily.

instructions.title: Add corn and potato
instructions.instruction: Stir in the sweet corn and diced potato. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the vegetables in the butter.
instructions.tip: Reserve a small spoonful of corn for garnish if desired.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Pour in the vegetable stock and add the salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the potato is tender.
instructions.tip: The potato helps thicken the soup without needing flour.

instructions.title: Blend until smooth
instructions.instruction: Remove the saucepan from the heat and blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth. For a very silky result, carefully blend in batches in a countertop blender.
instructions.tip: If using a countertop blender, allow steam to escape safely and never seal hot liquid in a full blender.

instructions.title: Add the dairy
instructions.instruction: Return the blended soup to low heat. Stir in the milk and cream and warm gently for 3–4 minutes without allowing it to boil vigorously.
instructions.tip: Gentle heating helps preserve the creamy texture.

instructions.title: Adjust and serve
instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust the seasoning. Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped chives and the reserved corn, if using.
instructions.tip: Serve with toasted bread or a simple green salad.

tips: For a chunkier soup, blend only half of the mixture.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes if you enjoy a little heat.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.

alternatives: Coconut milk for a dairy-free variation

title: Barramundi with Moroccan spices
description: Barramundi fillets seasoned with cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, and lemon, then roasted until flaky and tender. The warm Moroccan-inspired spice blend complements the fish without overpowering its delicate flavour.

ingredients.item: Barramundi fillets, skin on or off

instructions.title: Heat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Pat the barramundi fillets dry with paper towels and place them in a lightly oiled baking dish.
instructions.tip: Dry fish develops a better surface and allows the spice mixture to adhere.

instructions.title: Mix the spice paste
instructions.instruction: In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, garlic, lemon zest, salt, and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Use only a small amount of cinnamon; it should add warmth rather than dominate.

instructions.title: Season the fish
instructions.instruction: Rub the spice mixture evenly over both sides of the fillets, taking care to coat the thicker sections well. Drizzle with half of the lemon juice.
instructions.tip: Let the fish sit for 10 minutes while the oven finishes heating, but do not marinate for hours in the lemon juice.

instructions.title: Roast until flaky
instructions.instruction: Bake for 12–16 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Cook to an internal temperature of 63°C.
instructions.tip: Check early because thin fillets cook quickly and can dry out.

instructions.title: Finish with lemon
instructions.instruction: Remove the fish from the oven and drizzle with the remaining lemon juice. Scatter the chopped coriander over the top.
instructions.tip: A little extra olive oil can be added just before serving for a glossy finish.

instructions.title: Plate and serve
instructions.instruction: Serve immediately with couscous, roasted vegetables, or a chickpea salad. Spoon any spiced juices from the baking dish over the fish.
instructions.tip: A side of lemony yogurt sauce works well with the warm spices.

tips: The same spice mixture works with cod, haddock, or firm white fish.
Serve with couscous and toasted almonds for a fuller Moroccan-inspired meal.
Avoid overcooking; the fish should remain moist and separate into large flakes.

title: Blueberry & lemon friands
description: Small French-inspired almond cakes with a delicate golden crust, soft buttery crumb, juicy blueberries, and bright lemon zest. Friands are naturally tender thanks to ground almonds and are perfect with tea or coffee.

ingredients.item: Extra butter or baking spray for the tin

instructions.title: Prepare the tin and oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a 10–12-hole friand or muffin tin thoroughly with butter or baking spray.
instructions.tip: Friands can stick because of their high butter and sugar content, so grease the corners carefully.

instructions.title: Combine the dry ingredients
instructions.instruction: Sift the icing sugar and plain flour into a bowl. Stir in the ground almonds, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt.
instructions.tip: Sifting removes lumps and helps create an even cake texture.

instructions.title: Add the egg whites
instructions.instruction: Lightly whisk the egg whites with a fork until frothy but not stiff. Pour them into the dry ingredients and mix gently until combined.
instructions.tip: There is no need to whip the egg whites to peaks; friands rely on a simple batter.

instructions.title: Finish the batter
instructions.instruction: Stir in the melted, cooled butter and vanilla extract until the batter is smooth. Fold in half of the blueberries.
instructions.tip: Allow hot butter to cool slightly so it does not cook the egg whites.

instructions.title: Fill and bake
instructions.instruction: Divide the batter among the prepared moulds, filling each about three-quarters full. Scatter the remaining blueberries over the tops and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
instructions.tip: If using a deep muffin tin, the cakes may need a few extra minutes.

instructions.title: Cool and serve
instructions.instruction: Let the friands rest in the tin for 5–10 minutes, then carefully turn them out onto a wire rack. Dust with icing sugar once cool, if desired.
instructions.tip: The cakes are delicate when hot but firm up as they cool.

tips: Use frozen blueberries straight from the freezer if fresh ones are unavailable.
Do not overmix the batter after adding the flour.
Store cooled friands in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

alternatives: A finely ground nut-free baking blend, noting the texture will differ

title: Chocolate Coconut Squares
description: Rich chocolate coconut squares with a fudgy cocoa base and a chewy coconut layer. These easy traybake treats are cut into small portions and make a satisfying dessert for chocolate and coconut lovers.

instructions.title: Prepare the baking tin
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Line a 20 cm square baking tin with baking paper, leaving some overhang to lift out the finished squares.
instructions.tip: A metal tin helps the base bake evenly and develop clean edges.

instructions.title: Make the chocolate base
instructions.instruction: Whisk the melted butter and sugar together. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then sift in the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt. Stir just until no dry patches remain.
instructions.tip: Avoid overmixing once the flour is added to keep the base tender.

instructions.title: Bake the base
instructions.instruction: Spread the chocolate mixture evenly into the prepared tin. Bake for 12–15 minutes until the surface is set but the centre remains slightly soft.
instructions.tip: The base will bake again with the coconut layer, so it should not be completely dried out.

instructions.title: Prepare the coconut topping
instructions.instruction: Mix the desiccated coconut with the condensed milk in a bowl until evenly moistened. Gently spread the mixture over the warm chocolate base.
instructions.tip: Use the back of a spoon lightly dampened with water to spread the sticky topping.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Return the tin to the oven for 15–20 minutes, until the coconut topping is lightly golden and set. Cool completely in the tin.
instructions.tip: Watch the edges closely near the end, as coconut can brown quickly.

instructions.title: Add chocolate and cut
instructions.instruction: Melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil in short microwave bursts or over a bowl set above gently simmering water. Drizzle over the cooled slab, allow to set, then cut into 16 squares.
instructions.tip: Chill briefly before cutting for neater portions.

tips: For a stronger chocolate flavour, use Dutch-process cocoa powder.
Let the slab cool completely before cutting to keep the coconut layer intact.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or refrigerate for a firmer texture.

title: Mini chilli beef pies
description: Golden individual beef pies filled with minced beef, tomatoes, beans, and warming chilli spices. The rich, savoury filling is wrapped in crisp pastry, making these mini pies ideal for parties, lunchboxes, or a hearty snack.

instructions.title: Prepare the filling
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Dice the vegetables finely so the mini pies are easy to fill.

instructions.title: Brown the beef
instructions.instruction: Add the minced beef and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon until browned and no longer pink. Drain excess fat if necessary.
instructions.tip: Let the beef brown in places rather than stirring constantly for better flavour.

instructions.title: Season and simmer
instructions.instruction: Stir in the tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, beef stock, kidney beans, chilli powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until thick, then cool completely.
instructions.tip: The filling must be fairly dry and cool before it goes into the pastry, otherwise the pastry can turn soggy.

instructions.title: Cut the pastry
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Cut pastry circles large enough to line the muffin cups and smaller circles for the lids, re-rolling scraps as needed.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry cool while working; warm pastry is harder to handle.

instructions.title: Fill and seal the pies
instructions.instruction: Press the larger pastry circles into the muffin cups. Divide the cooled beef filling among them, brush the pastry edges with beaten egg, and place the smaller circles on top. Press the edges together and cut a small steam vent in each lid.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill, as the filling can bubble out during baking.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Brush the tops with the remaining beaten egg and bake for 22–28 minutes until the pastry is crisp and deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before carefully removing the pies.
instructions.tip: If the tops brown too quickly, move the tin to a lower oven rack.

tips: Make the filling a day ahead and refrigerate it until ready to use.
For a milder version, reduce the chilli powder and use sweet paprika.
The baked pies can be frozen once cooled and reheated in the oven until piping hot.

alternatives: Puff pastry for a lighter, flaky top

title: Quick salt & pepper squid
description: Crispy squid tossed with a fragrant salt-and-pepper seasoning, garlic, chilli, and spring onions. This quick Chinese-inspired dish has a light crunchy coating and tender squid, making it an excellent starter or sharing plate.

ingredients.amount: 500 ml, or enough for shallow frying

instructions.title: Prepare the squid
instructions.instruction: Pat the squid completely dry with paper towels. Slice the tubes into rings about 1 cm wide and leave small tentacles whole or cut large ones in half.
instructions.tip: Dry squid fries more crisply and reduces oil splatter.

instructions.title: Make the coating
instructions.instruction: Mix the cornflour, plain flour, salt, white pepper, and five-spice powder in a shallow bowl. Toss the squid in the mixture until lightly and evenly coated, shaking off excess flour.
instructions.tip: A thin coating gives a crisp result without making the squid heavy.

instructions.title: Heat the oil
instructions.instruction: Pour the oil into a deep, heavy pan to a safe depth for frying and heat to 180°C. If you do not have a thermometer, a small pinch of coating should sizzle immediately without burning.
instructions.tip: Never fill the pan more than halfway with oil, and keep water away from hot oil.

instructions.title: Fry in batches
instructions.instruction: Fry the squid in small batches for about 1–2 minutes until the coating is crisp and pale golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towels.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan because it lowers the oil temperature and makes the coating greasy.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Carefully pour off most of the frying oil, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan. Add the garlic, chilli, and spring onions and stir-fry for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the aromatics moving so the garlic does not burn.

instructions.title: Toss and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the fried squid to the pan and toss quickly with the garlic and chilli mixture. Serve immediately with lime wedges and an extra pinch of salt and pepper if needed.
instructions.tip: Serve straight away to keep the coating crunchy.

tips: Cook squid quickly over high heat; prolonged frying can make it tough.
For a less oily version, cook in an air fryer at 200°C until crisp, shaking halfway through and lightly spraying with oil.
Serve with chilli sauce, lemon or lime wedges, or a simple soy dipping sauce.

alternatives: Thin strips of firm white fish
A small pinch of ground cumin and ground coriander

title: Spiced smoky barbecued chicken
description: Juicy barbecue chicken coated in a smoky paprika, cumin, garlic, and chilli marinade, then grilled until caramelized with a tangy barbecue glaze. Perfect for outdoor grilling or a stovetop grill pan.

instructions.title: Prepare the marinade
instructions.instruction: In a bowl, combine the olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic, onion powder, chilli powder, brown sugar, salt, pepper, and apple cider vinegar.
instructions.tip: Smoked paprika gives the chicken a deep barbecue flavour even when cooking indoors.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry and coat thoroughly with the spice mixture. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours.
instructions.tip: Allowing time for the marinade to penetrate improves flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the grill
instructions.instruction: Preheat a barbecue or grill pan to medium-high heat and lightly oil the cooking surface. Remove the chicken from the refrigerator about 15 minutes before cooking.
instructions.tip: Avoid excessively high heat because the sugar in the marinade can burn.

instructions.title: Grill the chicken
instructions.instruction: Grill the chicken for approximately 6–8 minutes per side for boneless thighs, or longer for bone-in pieces, turning as needed until browned and nearly cooked through.
instructions.tip: Cooking time depends on thickness and whether the chicken contains bones.

instructions.title: Apply the barbecue glaze
instructions.instruction: Brush the chicken with barbecue sauce during the final 3–5 minutes of cooking, turning once and applying another thin layer. Cook until the thickest part reaches 74°C.
instructions.tip: Add sugary sauce near the end to prevent it from scorching.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the chicken to a clean plate and rest for 5 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges, corn, coleslaw, or grilled vegetables.
instructions.tip: Resting helps the juices redistribute before serving.

tips: For deeper flavour, marinate the chicken overnight.
Keep a portion of barbecue sauce separate for serving rather than reusing sauce that has touched raw chicken.
Use indirect heat to finish larger bone-in pieces without burning the outside.

alternatives: Boneless chicken breast, adjusted for cooking time
Tomato ketchup mixed with a little honey and vinegar

title: Squid, chickpea & chorizo salad
description: A Mediterranean-inspired warm salad combining tender squid, smoky chorizo, creamy chickpeas, lemon, and fresh parsley. The paprika-rich cooking juices become a simple dressing for this hearty dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Pat the squid dry and cut it into rings. Drain the chickpeas, slice the chorizo and red onion, and dice the bell pepper.
instructions.tip: Dry squid well so it sears instead of releasing too much moisture.

instructions.title: Render the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the chorizo and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring until it releases its paprika-coloured oil and begins to crisp.
instructions.tip: The chorizo usually releases enough fat to cook the vegetables without much extra oil.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the red onion and bell pepper to the pan and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Lower the heat if the garlic starts to brown too quickly.

instructions.title: Warm the chickpeas
instructions.instruction: Add the chickpeas and toss them in the chorizo mixture for 2–3 minutes until warmed through. Transfer the mixture to a large serving bowl.
instructions.tip: A tablespoon of water can loosen the pan juices if the mixture looks dry.

instructions.title: Sear the squid
instructions.instruction: Increase the heat to high and add the olive oil if the pan is dry. Cook the squid in a single layer for about 1–2 minutes, turning once, until opaque and just tender. Cook in batches if necessary.
instructions.tip: Squid becomes tough if it is cooked slowly for too long; keep this step quick.

instructions.title: Dress and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the squid to the bowl with the chickpeas and chorizo. Add lemon juice, red wine vinegar, parsley, black pepper, and salt to taste. Toss with the spinach or rocket and serve warm.
instructions.tip: Taste before adding much salt because chorizo can already be quite salty.

tips: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the smoky dressing.
For a fresher finish, add a little lemon zest just before serving.
Cook the squid just before serving for the best texture.

alternatives: Smoked tofu for a meat-free variation
Firm white fish cut into bite-sized pieces

title: Sticky Chicken
description: Tender chicken pieces glazed in a glossy sweet-and-savoury sauce made with soy, honey, garlic, and ginger. The sauce reduces into a sticky coating that pairs beautifully with rice and crisp vegetables.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces

instructions.title: Mix the sticky sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the soy sauce, honey, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and black pepper in a bowl. In a separate small cup, mix the cornflour with the water until smooth.
