instructions.tip: Mix the cornflour slurry immediately before using so it does not settle.

instructions.title: Brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add the chicken in a single layer. Cook for 5–7 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned on most sides.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if the pan is crowded, otherwise the chicken will steam.

instructions.title: Add the sauce
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium and pour the prepared sauce over the chicken. Stir to coat all the pieces and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate because honey and sugar can burn quickly.

instructions.title: Simmer until cooked
instructions.instruction: Cook for 6–10 minutes, stirring regularly, until the chicken is cooked through and reaches 74°C in the thickest pieces.
instructions.tip: The cooking time depends on the size of the chicken pieces.

instructions.title: Thicken the glaze
instructions.instruction: Stir the cornflour slurry again and pour it into the pan. Simmer for 1–2 minutes until the sauce becomes glossy and clings to the chicken.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if the glaze becomes too thick before the chicken is fully cooked.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove from the heat and scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds. Serve hot with steamed rice, noodles, or stir-fried vegetables.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lime can balance the sweetness of the glaze.

tips: Use low-sodium soy sauce if you prefer a less salty glaze.
For extra heat, add chilli flakes or a teaspoon of chilli sauce.
Serve immediately for the glossiest sauce, or loosen leftovers with a little water when reheating.

title: Warm roast asparagus salad
description: A fresh warm salad of roasted asparagus, cherry tomatoes, leafy greens, and a lemon-mustard dressing. Toasted almonds and shaved Parmesan add crunch and savoury richness to this simple seasonal dish.

ingredients.item: Baby spinach or mixed salad leaves

instructions.title: Preheat the oven
instructions.instruction: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper and trim the woody ends from the asparagus.
instructions.tip: Bend a spear gently near the base; it will naturally break where the woody section begins.

instructions.title: Season the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Arrange the asparagus and cherry tomatoes on the tray. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss lightly.
instructions.tip: Spread the vegetables out so they roast instead of steaming.

instructions.title: Roast until tender
instructions.instruction: Roast for 10–15 minutes, turning the asparagus once, until it is tender with lightly browned tips and the tomatoes have softened.
instructions.tip: Thin asparagus cooks quickly, so begin checking after 8–10 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, Dijon mustard, honey, and grated garlic until emulsified. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
instructions.tip: If the dressing is too sharp, add a little more honey; if too thick, add a teaspoon of water.

instructions.title: Toast the almonds
instructions.instruction: Place the flaked almonds in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat and toast for 2–3 minutes, stirring often, until lightly golden. Remove immediately from the pan.
instructions.tip: Almonds can burn quickly, so do not leave them unattended.

instructions.title: Assemble the salad
instructions.instruction: Place the spinach or salad leaves in a large bowl. Add the warm asparagus and tomatoes, drizzle with the dressing, and toss gently. Finish with Parmesan shavings and toasted almonds.
instructions.tip: Add the leaves just before serving so they soften slightly without becoming wilted.

tips: Add cooked lentils or chickpeas to make the salad more filling.
For a vegan version, omit Parmesan and use a little nutritional yeast.
Serve alongside grilled fish, roast chicken, or warm crusty bread.

title: BeaverTails
description: A Canadian fairground favourite, BeaverTails are hand-stretched pieces of yeast dough fried until golden and topped with cinnamon sugar. Serve them warm with lemon, chocolate spread, or other sweet toppings.

ingredients.amount: 1 litre, or enough for deep frying

instructions.title: Activate the yeast
instructions.instruction: Combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of the sugar in a bowl. Leave for 5–10 minutes until foamy. If using instant yeast, it can be mixed directly with the flour.
instructions.tip: The liquid should feel warm, not hot, or it may damage the yeast.

instructions.title: Make the dough
instructions.instruction: In a large bowl, mix the flour, remaining sugar, and salt. Add the yeast mixture, milk, melted butter, and egg. Mix until a soft dough forms.
instructions.tip: Add a little extra flour only if the dough is extremely sticky; too much flour can make the fried dough dense.

instructions.title: Knead and rise
instructions.instruction: Knead for 8–10 minutes by hand, or 5–6 minutes in a mixer, until smooth and elastic. Place in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and leave in a warm place for 60–90 minutes until doubled in size.
instructions.tip: A slow rise in a cool room is fine; allow extra time until the dough visibly expands.

instructions.title: Shape the tails
instructions.instruction: Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Roll or stretch each piece into an elongated oval about 5 mm thick, tapering the ends slightly.
instructions.tip: Do not make the dough too thick, as it will puff while frying.

instructions.title: Fry until golden
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 175°C. Fry one or two pieces at a time for about 1–2 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain briefly on a wire rack or paper towels.
instructions.tip: Keep the oil temperature steady and never leave hot oil unattended.

instructions.title: Coat and serve
instructions.instruction: Mix the coating sugar with the cinnamon in a shallow dish. While the fried dough is still warm, toss each piece in the cinnamon sugar and serve immediately with lemon or your favourite sweet topping.
instructions.tip: For a classic finish, squeeze a little lemon juice over the cinnamon sugar just before eating.

tips: For a chocolate version, spread chocolate hazelnut spread over the warm dough.
Use a thermometer to maintain the oil temperature for even frying.
BeaverTails are best eaten immediately while warm and crisp.

alternatives: Cinnamon mixed with a pinch of nutmeg

title: Breakfast Potatoes
description: Crispy-edged breakfast potatoes with tender centres, seasoned with paprika, garlic, onion, and black pepper. These golden potatoes are easy to prepare in a skillet and pair well with eggs or a hearty breakfast plate.

instructions.title: Cut the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into even 1.5 cm cubes. Rinse briefly under cold water and dry very thoroughly with a clean towel.
instructions.tip: Removing surface starch and moisture helps the potatoes brown more evenly.

instructions.title: Parboil the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Bring a saucepan of salted water to a boil. Add the potatoes and simmer for 5–6 minutes until the edges begin to soften but the centres remain firm. Drain well and let them steam-dry for several minutes.
instructions.tip: Do not cook them until fully tender, or they may break apart in the skillet.

instructions.title: Season the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Toss the dried potatoes with the olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, thyme, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Seasoning after drying helps the spices stick without forming a wet paste.

instructions.title: Brown in the skillet
instructions.instruction: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and add the butter. Add the potatoes in a single layer and cook for 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp on several sides.
instructions.tip: Avoid stirring too often; letting the potatoes sit helps them form a crust.

instructions.title: Add the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Stir in the diced onion and red pepper. Cook for another 5–7 minutes until the vegetables soften and the potatoes are fully tender.
instructions.tip: If the potatoes brown too quickly before softening, lower the heat and cover briefly.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust the seasoning, then scatter over the chopped parsley. Serve hot with eggs, breakfast sausages, or sautéed greens.
instructions.tip: A dash of hot sauce or a squeeze of lemon can brighten the finished dish.

tips: Use a wide skillet so the potatoes have room to crisp.
For a quicker version, use leftover cooked potatoes and skip the parboiling step.
Add diced cooked bacon or smoked paprika-seasoned tofu for extra savoury flavour.

alternatives: Diced courgette added near the end

title: Canadian Butter Tarts
description: Classic Canadian butter tarts made with crisp pastry shells and a rich, sweet filling of butter, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla. The centres bake into a soft, syrupy custard, with raisins or pecans added according to preference.

instructions.title: Make the pastry
instructions.instruction: Combine the flour and salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time until the dough just comes together.
instructions.tip: Handle the dough lightly to keep the pastry tender.

instructions.title: Chill and roll
instructions.instruction: Shape the dough into a flat disc, wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Roll it out on a lightly floured surface to about 3 mm thick.
instructions.tip: If the dough cracks, let it rest at room temperature for a few minutes before rolling again.

instructions.title: Line the tart tin
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Cut 12 pastry rounds and press them gently into the cups of a muffin tin, forming small shells. Chill the lined tin while making the filling.
instructions.tip: Avoid stretching the pastry, as it can shrink during baking.

instructions.title: Mix the filling
instructions.instruction: Whisk the melted butter and brown sugar together. Add the syrup, eggs, vanilla, and vinegar and whisk until smooth. Stir in the raisins, pecans, or both if using.
instructions.tip: Let the melted butter cool before mixing it with the eggs.

instructions.title: Fill the shells
instructions.instruction: Divide the filling among the pastry shells, filling each no more than two-thirds full to allow room for bubbling. Place the tin on a baking tray to catch any drips.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill, as the syrup can bubble over and stick to the tin.

instructions.title: Bake and cool
instructions.instruction: Bake for 18–22 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is set around the edges but still slightly soft in the centre. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then carefully transfer to a rack.
instructions.tip: The filling firms as it cools, so avoid baking until the centres are completely hard.

tips: For a runnier traditional-style filling, bake toward the lower end of the time range.
For a firmer filling, bake a little longer while watching the pastry colour.
Cool the tarts before storing them in an airtight container.

alternatives: Maple syrup, which gives a more pronounced flavour

title: Classic Tourtière
description: A traditional French-Canadian meat pie filled with seasoned minced pork and beef, onion, and warming spices, enclosed in flaky pastry. This savoury pie is especially popular during the winter holidays but makes a comforting meal year-round.

ingredients.item: Shortcrust pastry, enough for a double-crust 23 cm pie

instructions.title: Cook the onion and garlic
instructions.instruction: Heat the butter or oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Finely chopped onion blends into the filling and distributes its flavour evenly.

instructions.title: Brown the meat
instructions.instruction: Add the minced pork and beef. Cook for 7–9 minutes, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and no pink remains.
instructions.tip: Drain excess fat if the mixture looks very greasy, leaving a little for flavour.

instructions.title: Simmer with spices
instructions.instruction: Add the diced potato, beef stock, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
instructions.tip: The potato helps bind the filling, while the spices give the pie its traditional warm aroma.

instructions.title: Cool the filling
instructions.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat and let the filling cool completely. Preheat the oven to 200°C and place a baking tray inside to heat.
instructions.tip: A cool filling prevents the pastry from softening before it reaches the oven.

instructions.title: Assemble the pie
instructions.instruction: Line a 23 cm pie dish with one sheet of pastry, leaving a little overhang. Spoon in the cooled filling, cover with the second sheet, and press the edges together to seal. Trim and crimp the edges, then cut a small steam vent in the top.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry cold and avoid stretching it while fitting the dish.

instructions.title: Glaze and bake
instructions.instruction: Brush the top with beaten egg and place the pie on the hot baking tray. Bake for 35–45 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden and crisp. Rest for 10–15 minutes before slicing.
instructions.tip: If the edges brown too quickly, cover them loosely with strips of foil.

tips: Prepare the filling a day ahead and refrigerate it to make assembly easier.
Serve with pickles, mustard, or a crisp green salad to balance the rich pie.
Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheated until piping hot.

alternatives: Puff pastry for the top crust

title: Jam jam cookies
description: Tender, buttery sandwich cookies filled with sweet raspberry or strawberry jam and finished with a light dusting of icing sugar. These classic-style jam cookies are delicate, fruity, and perfect alongside tea.

instructions.title: Cream the butter and sugar
instructions.instruction: Beat the softened butter and granulated sugar together for 2–3 minutes until pale and fluffy. Add the egg and vanilla extract and beat until combined.
instructions.tip: Use room-temperature butter so it creams smoothly without becoming oily.

instructions.title: Add the dry ingredients
instructions.instruction: Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl. Add to the butter mixture in two batches and mix gently until a soft dough forms.
instructions.tip: Stop mixing as soon as the flour is incorporated to keep the cookies tender.

instructions.title: Chill the dough
instructions.instruction: Shape the dough into a disc, wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
instructions.tip: Chilling makes the dough easier to roll and helps the cookies keep their shape.

instructions.title: Cut the cookies
instructions.instruction: Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface to about 4 mm thick. Cut out 40–48 rounds, re-rolling the scraps gently. If desired, cut a small window from the centre of half the rounds.
instructions.tip: Dip the cutter in flour occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Bake until lightly golden
instructions.instruction: Arrange the rounds on the trays with space between them. Bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges are just beginning to turn pale golden. Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
instructions.tip: Do not wait for the cookies to become dark; they will firm up as they cool.

instructions.title: Fill and sandwich
instructions.instruction: Spread a small amount of jam on the flat side of each whole cookie. Top with a second cookie, using windowed cookies if desired. Dust with icing sugar and let the filling settle before serving.
instructions.tip: If the jam is very runny, warm it briefly and let it cool until thick enough to spread.

tips: Use a thick jam to help the sandwiches hold together.
For a citrus variation, add finely grated lemon zest to the dough.
Store assembled cookies in an airtight container and eat within 3 days for the best texture.

title: Molasses Baked Beans
description: Slow-baked beans in a rich, dark sauce of molasses, brown sugar, mustard, and tomato, with optional smoky bacon. This comforting North American-style side dish has a sweet-savoury flavour and tender beans in a thick sauce.

ingredients.amount: To taste, added after the beans soften

instructions.title: Soak the beans
instructions.instruction: Rinse the dried beans and place them in a large bowl covered with plenty of cold water. Soak for 8–12 hours, then drain and rinse. Alternatively, use a quick-soak method by boiling for 2 minutes and resting covered for 1 hour.
instructions.tip: Discard the soaking water and use fresh water for cooking.

instructions.title: Parboil the beans
instructions.instruction: Place the drained beans in a large saucepan, cover with fresh water, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 30–45 minutes until they begin to soften but are not fully cooked. Drain, reserving a little cooking liquid if desired.
instructions.tip: Cooking time varies with the age of the beans; they should be partly tender before baking.

instructions.title: Prepare the flavour base
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 150°C. In a large ovenproof casserole, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until lightly browned, if using. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened.
instructions.tip: For a vegetarian version, sauté the onion in a tablespoon of oil instead.

instructions.title: Make the molasses sauce
instructions.instruction: Stir in the molasses, brown sugar, tomato paste, mustard, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, smoked paprika, black pepper, and bay leaf. Add the partly cooked beans and stir to coat.
instructions.tip: Taste the sauce before adding salt, especially if using bacon or stock.

instructions.title: Bake slowly
instructions.instruction: Add enough water or unsalted stock to just cover the beans. Cover the casserole and bake for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally and checking the liquid level. Add more hot water if needed, until the beans are tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the casserole covered for most of the cooking time so the beans soften without drying out.

instructions.title: Thicken and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the lid for the final 20–30 minutes to thicken the sauce. Remove the bay leaf, season with salt to taste, and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
instructions.tip: The sauce thickens further as it cools; add a splash of water when reheating if necessary.

tips: For the most tender result, soak the beans overnight and cook them until almost tender before adding acidic ingredients.
For a smokier flavour, add a little extra smoked paprika.
Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate for up to 3–4 days, and reheat until piping hot.

alternatives: A mixture of dark brown sugar and a little maple syrup, with a less intense flavour
A small amount of soy sauce

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
description: A Montreal deli classic featuring beef brisket cured with a fragrant blend of pepper, coriander, mustard, and garlic, then slowly smoked and steamed until tender. Serve thinly sliced on rye bread with mustard and pickles.

instructions.title: Prepare the brisket
instructions.instruction: Trim excess surface fat from the brisket, leaving a thin layer. Pat the meat dry with paper towels.
instructions.tip: Choose a brisket with some marbling to help it remain moist during the long cooking process.

instructions.title: Mix the spice cure
instructions.instruction: Combine the salt, brown sugar, black pepper, coriander, mustard seeds, garlic powder, paprika, cloves, and ground bay leaf. Rub the mixture evenly over all sides of the brisket.
instructions.tip: Press the spices firmly onto the meat so the seasoning adheres.

instructions.title: Cure the beef
instructions.instruction: Place the seasoned brisket in a covered non-reactive container and refrigerate for 5–7 days, turning it once daily. For a traditional cured deli-style result, use a validated curing recipe with correctly measured curing salt rather than relying on ordinary salt alone.
instructions.tip: Keep the meat refrigerated at 4°C or below throughout curing.

instructions.title: Smoke the brisket
instructions.instruction: Rinse off excess surface seasoning and pat dry. Smoke the brisket at approximately 110–120°C until it develops a dark, fragrant crust and reaches around 70–75°C internally, allowing several hours depending on thickness.
instructions.tip: Use a food-safe smoker and monitor the internal temperature with a reliable thermometer.

instructions.title: Steam until tender
instructions.instruction: Transfer the smoked brisket to a covered roasting pan with a little hot water. Steam in an oven at approximately 150°C until a probe slides into the thickest section with little resistance, often another 2–3 hours.
instructions.tip: Tenderness matters more than a precise finishing time; keep the pan covered to prevent drying.

instructions.title: Slice and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest the brisket briefly, then slice thinly across the grain. Pile the warm slices onto rye bread, spread with yellow mustard, and serve with dill pickles.
instructions.tip: For the most tender slices, identify the grain direction before cutting and slice across it.

tips: Traditional Montreal smoked meat requires curing, smoking, and steaming, so plan several days ahead.
For easier serving, prepare the brisket in advance and reheat slices gently with a little steaming liquid.
The listed nutrition is an approximate estimate for a sandwich portion.

alternatives: Beef chuck roast, although the texture will differ

title: Split Pea Soup
description: A hearty soup of green split peas simmered with carrots, celery, onion, and herbs until creamy and thick. Smoked ham adds traditional savoury depth, while the vegetable-only version is equally comforting.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Rinse the split peas under cold water and check for any debris. Dice the onion, carrots, and celery, and mince the garlic.
instructions.tip: Split peas usually do not need soaking, although rinsing them helps remove surface starch and dust.

instructions.title: Soften the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook for 5–7 minutes until beginning to soften. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: A gentle sauté builds flavour before the peas are added.

instructions.title: Add peas and stock
instructions.instruction: Stir in the split peas, stock, bay leaf, thyme, black pepper, and diced ham if using. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Choose low-sodium stock so you can control the final salt level.

instructions.title: Simmer until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover partially and simmer for 60–75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peas have broken down and the vegetables are tender. Add hot water if the soup becomes too thick.
instructions.tip: Older split peas can take longer to soften, so continue simmering as needed.

instructions.title: Adjust the texture
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf. For a smoother soup, blend a portion with an immersion blender; for a rustic texture, simply stir vigorously to break down the peas.
instructions.tip: The soup thickens considerably as it rests, so adjust with stock or water before serving.

instructions.title: Season and serve
instructions.instruction: Taste and add salt if needed. Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with crusty bread or toast.
instructions.tip: If using ham, taste before salting because the meat and stock may already provide enough seasoning.

tips: For a vegetarian soup, omit the ham and use vegetable stock.
Add a pinch of smoked paprika if you want a smoky flavour without meat.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3–4 days.

alternatives: Water with a suitable stock cube

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: A quick Chinese-American stir-fry of tender beef strips and bright green broccoli coated in a savoury garlic-soy sauce. Serve over steamed rice for a satisfying weeknight dinner.

ingredients.item: Flank steak or sirloin, thinly sliced against the grain

instructions.title: Marinate the beef
instructions.instruction: Slice the beef thinly against the grain. Toss it with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1 teaspoon of cornflour, and the black pepper. Leave for 10–15 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
instructions.tip: Partially chilling the beef makes it easier to slice thinly.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, water or stock, brown sugar, and remaining cornflour until smooth.
instructions.tip: Mix the cornflour thoroughly so the finished sauce thickens without lumps.

instructions.title: Blanch the broccoli
instructions.instruction: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Add the broccoli and cook for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse briefly with cool water. Alternatively, steam until just tender.
instructions.tip: Brief blanching helps the broccoli cook quickly while retaining its colour.

instructions.title: Sear the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of neutral oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer and sear for 1–2 minutes per side until browned. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if necessary to avoid steaming the beef.

instructions.title: Stir-fry aromatics and broccoli
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for about 20 seconds, then add the broccoli and toss for 1–2 minutes.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic moving so it does not burn over the high heat.

instructions.title: Combine and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the beef and any juices to the wok. Stir the sauce again and pour it in. Toss for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and broccoli. Finish with sesame oil and sesame seeds if using, then serve with rice.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick before the broccoli is heated through.

tips: Slice the beef against the grain for a more tender result.
Serve with steamed rice or noodles to make the meal more substantial.
For a lower-sodium dish, use reduced-sodium soy sauce and unsalted stock.

title: Beef Lo Mein
description: Chinese-American stir-fried noodles tossed with tender beef, crunchy vegetables, and a savoury soy-based sauce. This quick noodle dish is colourful, comforting, and easy to customise with vegetables you have on hand.

ingredients.item: Lo mein noodles or egg noodles

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook the noodles according to the package instructions until just tender. Drain, rinse briefly if the package recommends it, and toss with 1 teaspoon of sesame oil to prevent sticking.
instructions.tip: Slightly undercook the noodles because they will finish cooking in the wok.

instructions.title: Season the beef
instructions.instruction: Toss the sliced beef with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, the cornflour, and black pepper. Leave for 10 minutes while preparing the vegetables.
instructions.tip: Thin, evenly cut strips cook quickly and remain tender.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Combine the remaining soy sauce with the oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, remaining sesame oil, and water. Stir until well mixed.
instructions.tip: Dark soy sauce mainly adds colour, so use it sparingly if you prefer a lighter noodle dish.

instructions.title: Sear the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of neutral oil in a wok over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until browned and nearly cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the wok; cook the beef in batches if needed.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining neutral oil. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then add the carrot, bell pepper, and cabbage. Cook for 3–4 minutes until just tender but still crisp.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetables moving so they cook evenly over the high heat.

instructions.title: Toss the noodles
instructions.instruction: Return the beef to the wok and add the noodles and sauce. Toss for 2–3 minutes until everything is hot and evenly coated. Add a splash of water if needed, then finish with spring onions and serve.
instructions.tip: Use tongs to lift and turn the noodles without breaking them.

tips: Prepare all the vegetables and sauce before heating the wok, as stir-frying moves quickly.
Add mushrooms or bean sprouts for more texture.
If using dried noodles, cook them according to their package instructions before stir-frying.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
description: A quick, savoury fried rice made with cooked rice, chicken, eggs, peas, carrots, and spring onions. High heat and cold rice help create separate grains coated in a light soy and sesame seasoning.

instructions.title: Prepare the rice and chicken
instructions.instruction: Break up the chilled rice with clean hands or a fork so there are no large clumps. Pat the diced chicken dry and season lightly with pepper.
instructions.tip: Use rice that was cooked earlier, cooled quickly, and refrigerated; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for extended periods.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of neutral oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until golden and cooked through to 74°C internally. Transfer to a clean plate.
instructions.tip: Cut the chicken into similar-sized pieces so it cooks evenly.

instructions.title: Scramble the eggs
instructions.instruction: Add a little more oil if needed. Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently until softly scrambled and fully set. Transfer to the plate with the chicken.
instructions.tip: Cook the eggs separately so they remain in distinct, tender pieces.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and peas and cook for another minute until fragrant and heated through.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat high enough to cook the vegetables quickly without making them soggy.

instructions.title: Fry the rice
instructions.instruction: Add the chilled rice and toss vigorously for 3–4 minutes, breaking apart any remaining clumps. Drizzle the soy sauce around the hot sides of the wok and toss to coat the grains.
instructions.tip: Fry in batches if your pan is small; too much rice at once traps steam.

instructions.title: Combine and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the chicken and eggs to the wok. Add the spring onions, sesame oil, and pepper, then toss for 1–2 minutes until evenly mixed and piping hot. Taste and add salt only if needed.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately for the best texture.

tips: Day-old refrigerated rice gives the best results because it is drier and less sticky.
Add diced bell pepper, corn, or chopped cabbage to vary the vegetables.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat thoroughly; avoid reheating rice more than once.

title: Chinese Orange Chicken
description: Crisp chicken pieces coated in a glossy orange sauce made with fresh orange juice, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and a touch of sugar. This Chinese-American favourite balances sweet citrus flavour with savoury seasoning.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.amount: 500 ml, or enough for shallow frying

instructions.title: Prepare the chicken coating
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry. Whisk the egg in a bowl. In another bowl, combine the 80 g cornflour and plain flour. Dip the chicken pieces in egg, then coat thoroughly in the flour mixture.
instructions.tip: Shake off excess coating to help the chicken become crisp rather than clumpy.

instructions.title: Fry the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pan to 175°C. Fry the chicken in batches for 4–6 minutes, depending on piece size, until crisp, golden, and cooked through to 74°C internally. Drain on a wire rack.
instructions.tip: Do not overcrowd the pan or the oil temperature will drop.

instructions.title: Start the orange sauce
instructions.instruction: In a clean skillet, combine the orange juice, orange zest, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and chilli flakes if using. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
instructions.tip: Fresh orange juice gives the sauce a brighter citrus flavour.

instructions.title: Thicken the sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the 2 teaspoons of cornflour with the water until smooth. Slowly stir the slurry into the simmering sauce and cook for 1–2 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened.
instructions.tip: Add the slurry gradually; the sauce will thicken further as it cools.

instructions.title: Coat the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the fried chicken to the skillet and toss quickly until every piece is coated with orange sauce. Keep the heat moderate and remove the pan from the heat as soon as the chicken is glazed.
instructions.tip: Toss just before serving so the coating stays as crisp as possible.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds, if using. Serve immediately with steamed rice and stir-fried vegetables.
instructions.tip: Add extra orange zest at the end for a stronger citrus aroma.

tips: For a lighter version, air-fry the coated chicken with a light spray of oil until cooked and crisp.
Adjust the sugar depending on how sweet your oranges are.
Keep the chicken and sauce separate until just before serving if preparing ahead.

title: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir Fry
description: A simple Chinese home-style dish of soft scrambled eggs simmered briefly with juicy tomatoes, spring onions, and a lightly sweet-savoury sauce. It is comforting, quick to prepare, and delicious over steamed rice.

instructions.title: Prepare the eggs
instructions.instruction: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and white pepper, and whisk until the yolks and whites are evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Whisking just before cooking helps the eggs remain tender.

instructions.title: Scramble the eggs
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and gently push them around until softly set but still moist. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Remove the eggs while slightly soft because they will be returned to the pan later.

instructions.title: Cook the tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the pan. Add the garlic and half the spring onions and stir for 20 seconds. Add the tomato wedges and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring gently until they soften and release their juices.
instructions.tip: Use ripe tomatoes for a naturally sweeter, juicier sauce.

instructions.title: Season the tomato sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the soy sauce, sugar, and remaining salt. If the tomatoes are not releasing enough liquid, add 1–2 tablespoons of water and simmer briefly.
instructions.tip: The sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes; adjust it to taste.

instructions.title: Combine with eggs
instructions.instruction: Return the scrambled eggs to the pan and gently fold them through the tomatoes for 30–60 seconds until warmed through and fully set.
instructions.tip: Fold gently to keep the eggs in soft, distinct curds.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat, drizzle with sesame oil if using, and scatter over the remaining spring onions. Serve hot with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Avoid simmering for too long after adding the eggs or they may become firm and rubbery.

tips: Add a little ketchup for a sweeter, more familiar home-style variation.
Serve with rice or noodles to make a more substantial meal.
Do not overcook the eggs; soft curds are the hallmark of this dish.

title: Egg Drop Soup
description: A light Chinese soup made with seasoned chicken stock and delicate ribbons of beaten egg. White pepper, spring onions, and a little sesame oil add flavour to this quick, soothing starter.

instructions.title: Prepare the stock
instructions.instruction: Pour the chicken stock into a saucepan. Add the grated ginger, soy sauce, and white pepper, then bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
instructions.tip: Use a good-quality stock with moderate salt so the soup does not become too salty.

instructions.title: Make the thickening slurry
instructions.instruction: In a small bowl, whisk the cornflour with the cold water until smooth. Stir the slurry into the simmering stock and cook for 1–2 minutes until the liquid is slightly thickened.
instructions.tip: The soup should be lightly silky rather than thick like gravy.

instructions.title: Beat the eggs
instructions.instruction: Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk until the yolks and whites are evenly combined, without creating too much foam.
instructions.tip: Pouring from a small jug or measuring cup makes the egg easier to control.

instructions.title: Create egg ribbons
instructions.instruction: Lower the heat so the stock is gently simmering. Stir the soup slowly in one direction to create movement, then drizzle in the beaten egg in a thin stream. Let the ribbons set for several seconds before stirring gently.
instructions.tip: A slow, steady pour creates delicate ribbons; pouring too quickly produces large clumps.

instructions.title: Season the soup
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Taste and add salt if needed.
instructions.tip: Sesame oil is potent, so a small amount is enough.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle into warmed bowls and garnish with sliced spring onions. Serve immediately as a starter or alongside rice and stir-fried dishes.
instructions.tip: Egg drop soup is best served freshly made, while the egg ribbons are delicate.

tips: For a vegetarian version, use vegetable stock and check that the soy sauce is suitable for your diet.
Add sweetcorn, finely sliced mushrooms, or soft tofu for extra texture.
For a clearer soup, use less cornflour or omit it entirely.

alternatives: A few drops of neutral oil

title: Egg Foo Young
description: A Chinese-American omelette made with beaten eggs, bean sprouts, spring onions, and mushrooms, cooked until golden and served with a savoury soy-based gravy. It is a flexible dish that works as a main meal with rice.

ingredients.item: Cooked chicken or cooked prawns, chopped, optional

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Rinse and drain the bean sprouts thoroughly. Slice the spring onions and mushrooms. If using cooked chicken or prawns, chop them into small pieces.
instructions.tip: Drain the bean sprouts well so they do not release excess liquid into the omelette.

instructions.title: Mix the egg mixture
instructions.instruction: Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with the soy sauce and white pepper. Fold in the bean sprouts, spring onions, mushrooms, and optional cooked chicken or prawns.
instructions.tip: Mix just before cooking for the freshest texture.

instructions.title: Cook the omelettes
instructions.instruction: Heat a little neutral oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Spoon in a portion of the egg mixture, shaping it into a thick round. Cook for 3–4 minutes until the underside is golden and the edges are set.
instructions.tip: Make several smaller omelettes rather than one very large one so they are easier to flip.

instructions.title: Flip and finish cooking
instructions.instruction: Carefully flip each omelette and cook for another 2–3 minutes until the centre is fully set. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining mixture, adding more oil as needed.
instructions.tip: Use a wide spatula and wait until the base is firm before flipping.

instructions.title: Prepare the gravy
instructions.instruction: In a small saucepan, bring the stock and oyster sauce to a gentle simmer. Mix the cornflour with the cold water, then stir it into the saucepan. Cook for 1–2 minutes until the gravy thickens, then stir in the sesame oil.
instructions.tip: For a vegetarian version, use vegetable stock and vegetarian mushroom sauce instead of oyster sauce.

instructions.title: Serve with gravy
instructions.instruction: Arrange the egg foo young on plates and spoon the hot gravy over or alongside them. Serve with steamed rice and extra spring onions if desired.
instructions.tip: Pour the gravy on just before eating to preserve the browned edges of the omelette.

tips: Use leftover cooked chicken or prawns to make preparation faster.
Add finely shredded cabbage, carrots, or water chestnuts for extra crunch.
Serve with rice to turn the omelette into a complete meal.

title: General Tsos Chicken
description: Crispy chicken pieces tossed in a glossy, tangy-sweet Chinese-American sauce made with soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and dried chillies. Serve with steamed rice and vegetables for a satisfying takeaway-style meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces

ingredients.amount: 500 ml, or enough for shallow frying

instructions.title: Prepare the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry and cut it into evenly sized pieces. Beat the egg in a bowl, then toss the chicken in it until coated. Mix the 100 g cornflour with the plain flour in a separate bowl.
instructions.tip: Uniform chicken pieces cook more evenly and are easier to coat.

instructions.title: Coat and fry
instructions.instruction: Dredge the chicken pieces in the flour mixture, shaking off the excess. Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep, heavy pan and fry the chicken in batches for 4–6 minutes, until crisp, golden, and cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C. Drain on a wire rack.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan because it lowers the oil temperature and makes the coating greasy.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin sauce, brown sugar, stock, and 1 teaspoon of cornflour mixed with 1 tablespoon of cold water.
instructions.tip: Mix the slurry immediately before adding it so the cornflour does not settle.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat a clean wok over medium heat with a teaspoon of oil. Add the dried chillies, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry for 20–30 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the aromatics moving to prevent the garlic from burning.

instructions.title: Thicken the glaze
instructions.instruction: Pour the prepared sauce into the wok and simmer for 2–3 minutes, stirring until glossy and lightly thickened. Stir in the sesame oil.
instructions.tip: If the sauce becomes too thick, add a tablespoon of stock or water.

instructions.title: Toss and serve
instructions.instruction: Add the fried chicken and toss quickly to coat every piece in the sauce. Garnish with spring onions and sesame seeds, then serve immediately with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Toss the chicken in the sauce just before serving to preserve as much crispness as possible.

tips: Remove some or all of the dried chillies for a milder version.
For a lighter option, air-fry the coated chicken with a light spray of oil until cooked through.
Serve with steamed broccoli or bok choy to balance the rich sauce.

alternatives: Oyster sauce with a pinch of sugar
A little extra soy sauce and brown sugar

title: Hot and Sour Soup
description: A warming Chinese soup with mushrooms, tofu, bamboo shoots, and egg ribbons in a peppery, tangy broth. Soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper create its signature balance of savoury, sour, and spicy flavours.

ingredients.item: Firm tofu, cut into thin strips

instructions.title: Prepare the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Slice the mushrooms and bamboo shoots into thin strips. Cut the tofu into matchsticks and beat the eggs in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Thinly sliced ingredients distribute evenly through the soup.

instructions.title: Simmer the broth
instructions.instruction: Bring the stock to a gentle boil in a saucepan. Add the ginger, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots, then simmer for 4–5 minutes until the mushrooms soften.
instructions.tip: A gentle simmer keeps the broth clear and prevents the vegetables from breaking apart.

instructions.title: Season the soup
instructions.instruction: Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, white pepper, and chilli oil. Add the tofu and simmer for another 2 minutes.
instructions.tip: White pepper supplies the characteristic warmth; adjust it gradually to your preferred heat level.

instructions.title: Thicken the broth
instructions.instruction: Mix the cornflour with the cold water until smooth. Stir the soup in one direction and slowly pour in the slurry. Simmer for 1–2 minutes until lightly thickened.
instructions.tip: Add the slurry gradually because the soup should be silky rather than overly thick.

instructions.title: Add the egg ribbons
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat so the soup is barely simmering. Slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs while stirring gently to form fine ribbons. Let the eggs set for several seconds.
instructions.tip: A slow stream of egg creates delicate strands instead of large clumps.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Taste and adjust the vinegar, white pepper, and salt. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.
instructions.tip: Add a little extra vinegar at the end if you prefer a sharper sour flavour.

tips: Use vegetable stock and check the chilli oil ingredients for a vegetarian version.
Add wood ear mushrooms if available for a more traditional texture.
Adjust the vinegar and white pepper separately to control sourness and heat.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: A classic Sichuan-inspired stir-fry with tender chicken, roasted peanuts, dried chillies, and spring onions in a savoury, sweet, and tangy sauce. Sichuan peppercorns add a distinctive citrusy, tingling finish.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs or breast, diced
Spring onions, cut into short lengths

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Toss the diced chicken with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon of cornflour. Leave for 15 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
instructions.tip: Cut the chicken into similar-sized pieces for even cooking.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk the remaining soy sauce with the rice vinegar, brown sugar, water or stock, and remaining teaspoon of cornflour until smooth.
instructions.tip: Prepare the sauce before heating the wok because the stir-fry cooks quickly.

instructions.title: Toast the spices
instructions.instruction: Heat a wok over medium heat and add the Sichuan peppercorns and dried chillies. Toast briefly for 20–30 seconds until fragrant, then remove and set aside if the wok becomes too hot.
instructions.tip: Do not let the chillies turn black, as burnt chillies taste bitter.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the neutral oil to the wok. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4–6 minutes until browned and cooked through to 74°C internally. Work in batches if necessary.
instructions.tip: Give the chicken room to sear instead of crowding the wok.

instructions.title: Add aromatics and sauce
instructions.instruction: Return the toasted chillies and peppercorns to the wok. Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and toss until it thickens and coats the chicken.
instructions.tip: Keep the aromatics moving so they do not burn.

instructions.title: Finish with peanuts
instructions.instruction: Stir in the roasted peanuts and remove the wok from the heat. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Add the peanuts at the end to preserve their crunch.

tips: For a milder dish, reduce the dried chillies and remove their seeds.
Sichuan peppercorns are distinctive but can be omitted if unavailable.
Serve with plain rice to balance the spicy, savoury sauce.

alternatives: Water with a small splash of rice vinegar

title: Kung Po Prawns
description: A spicy Chinese-style prawn stir-fry with dried chillies, peanuts, spring onions, and a tangy soy-vinegar sauce. The prawns cook quickly, making this a flavour-packed dinner that pairs well with steamed rice.

ingredients.item: Spring onions, cut into short lengths

instructions.title: Season the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry and toss with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon of cornflour. Set aside for 10 minutes.
instructions.tip: Dry prawns sear better and release less water into the wok.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the remaining soy sauce with the rice vinegar, brown sugar, water or stock, and remaining teaspoon of cornflour until smooth.
instructions.tip: Taste the sauce before cooking and adjust the vinegar or sugar to suit your preference.

instructions.title: Toast chillies and peppercorns
instructions.instruction: Heat a wok over medium heat and briefly toast the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns for 20–30 seconds until fragrant. Remove them if they begin to darken too quickly.
instructions.tip: Keep the chillies whole for a gentler heat or break them for a spicier result.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the neutral oil to the wok and stir-fry the prawns for about 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Transfer to a plate if they cook before the sauce is ready.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking the prawns, as they become rubbery.

instructions.title: Build the sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic, ginger, spring onions, toasted chillies, and peppercorns to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and simmer briefly until glossy.
instructions.tip: If the sauce thickens too quickly, loosen it with a tablespoon of water.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the prawns to the wok and toss for 30–60 seconds until coated and heated through. Stir in the peanuts and serve immediately with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Add the peanuts at the last moment to keep them crunchy.

tips: Use large prawns so they remain juicy during quick stir-frying.
Reduce the dried chillies for a milder dish.
Serve immediately with rice or noodles.

alternatives: Omit and add a splash of stock

title: Ma Po Tofu
description: A famous Sichuan dish featuring soft tofu in a bold, savoury sauce with minced meat, fermented chilli bean paste, garlic, and ginger. Sichuan peppercorns bring a distinctive tingling heat, while spring onions finish the dish.

ingredients.item: Soft or medium-firm tofu, cut into cubes

instructions.title: Prepare the tofu
instructions.instruction: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes. Bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer, add the tofu for 1–2 minutes, then drain carefully.
instructions.tip: Briefly warming the tofu helps it hold together and season evenly.

instructions.title: Brown the mince
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the minced pork or beef and cook for 4–5 minutes, breaking it into small pieces until browned.
instructions.tip: Small pieces distribute evenly throughout the sauce.

instructions.title: Fry the aromatics and paste
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the doubanjiang and chilli oil and cook for another minute until fragrant and the oil takes on a red colour.
instructions.tip: Doubanjiang is salty, so taste the finished sauce before adding extra salt.

instructions.title: Simmer the sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, stock, and ground Sichuan peppercorns. Bring to a gentle simmer, then carefully add the tofu cubes.
instructions.tip: Shake the wok gently rather than stirring vigorously to avoid breaking the tofu.

instructions.title: Thicken the sauce
instructions.instruction: Simmer for 4–5 minutes. Mix the cornflour with the cold water, then drizzle it into the wok while gently moving the sauce. Cook until the sauce lightly clings to the tofu.
instructions.tip: Add the slurry in stages if you prefer a looser sauce.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter over the spring onions and serve hot with steamed rice. Add a final pinch of ground Sichuan peppercorns if you enjoy its tingling flavour.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately because the tofu continues to absorb the sauce as it rests.

tips: For a vegetarian version, omit the mince and use finely chopped mushrooms with vegetable stock.
Adjust the chilli bean paste and chilli oil to control the heat.
Serve with plain rice to balance the intense, savoury sauce.

alternatives: A mixture of chilli paste and a little miso, though the flavour will differ
Omit and add a little extra stock

title: Napa Cabbage with Dried Shrimp
description: A simple Chinese home-style vegetable dish featuring tender napa cabbage stir-fried with fragrant garlic, ginger, and savoury dried shrimp. A splash of stock helps the cabbage soften while retaining its natural sweetness.

instructions.title: Rinse the dried shrimp
instructions.instruction: Rinse the dried shrimp under cold water, then soak in warm water for 10–15 minutes until softened. Drain and reserve a little soaking liquid if it is clean and not overly salty.
instructions.tip: Soaking softens the shrimp and helps release their savoury flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the cabbage
instructions.instruction: Separate the napa cabbage leaves, rinse thoroughly, and drain well. Cut the thicker white stems into smaller pieces than the leafy green sections.
instructions.tip: Keeping the stems and leaves separate allows the tougher parts to cook first.

instructions.title: Fry the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the dried shrimp, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Do not let the garlic brown too deeply because it can turn bitter.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the cabbage
instructions.instruction: Add the white cabbage stems and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes. Add the leafy sections and continue cooking for another 2 minutes until they begin to wilt.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if necessary to keep the cabbage from steaming in an overcrowded wok.

instructions.title: Simmer and thicken
instructions.instruction: Add the stock, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and white pepper. Cover and cook for 2–3 minutes until the cabbage is tender but not mushy. Mix the cornflour with the cold water and stir it in to lightly thicken the juices.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if the pan becomes dry before the cabbage is tender.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Taste before adding salt, since dried shrimp and soy sauce can be salty. Finish with sesame oil if desired and serve hot with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Keep the final seasoning light so the cabbage's natural sweetness remains noticeable.

tips: For a vegetarian alternative, omit the dried shrimp and use sliced shiitake mushrooms.
Use low-sodium stock if the dried shrimp are strongly salted.
Serve as a vegetable side with rice, noodles, or steamed fish.

alternatives: Omit and add a little stock

title: Ramen Noodles with Boiled Egg
description: A comforting bowl of ramen noodles in a savoury broth, topped with a soft-boiled egg, spring onions, mushrooms, and nori. The simple soy-seasoned broth is quick to make and easy to customise with your favourite toppings.

instructions.title: Boil the eggs
instructions.instruction: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Lower in the eggs and cook for 6–7 minutes for soft yolks or 9–10 minutes for firmer yolks. Transfer to cold water, cool, and peel carefully.
instructions.tip: Use a timer and cool the eggs promptly to make peeling easier.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Place the stock, ginger, and garlic in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes to infuse the broth.
instructions.tip: Avoid a vigorous boil, which can reduce the broth too quickly.

instructions.title: Season the broth
instructions.instruction: Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, and sesame oil. Add the sliced mushrooms and simmer for 3–4 minutes until tender.
instructions.tip: Taste before adding extra salt because soy sauce contributes plenty of seasoning.

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook the ramen noodles in a separate pot according to the package directions. Drain well and divide between two serving bowls.
instructions.tip: Cooking noodles separately keeps excess starch from clouding the broth.

instructions.title: Wilt the greens
instructions.instruction: Add the spinach or bok choy to the simmering broth for 1–2 minutes until just wilted. Remove the ginger and garlic if you prefer a smoother broth.
instructions.tip: Add leafy greens near the end to preserve their colour and texture.

instructions.title: Assemble the ramen
instructions.instruction: Pour the hot broth and vegetables over the noodles. Halve the boiled eggs and arrange them on top with spring onions and nori. Add chilli oil if desired and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Add the nori just before serving so it does not become soggy too early.

tips: For extra protein, add sliced cooked chicken, tofu, or edamame.
Use vegetable stock and check the noodles for a vegetarian version.
For a richer broth, simmer a spoonful of miso paste into a small amount of warm broth before stirring it into the pot.

alternatives: A little water with a pinch of sugar
Dry sherry with a small pinch of sugar

title: Sesame Cucumber Salad
description: A refreshing Chinese-style cucumber salad with garlic, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Lightly crushed cucumbers absorb the tangy dressing, making this a quick side dish for rice, noodles, or stir-fries.

instructions.title: Prepare the cucumbers
instructions.instruction: Wash and dry the cucumbers. Lightly crush them with the flat side of a knife or rolling pin until they split slightly, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
instructions.tip: Crushing creates rough surfaces that hold the dressing better.

instructions.title: Salt and drain
instructions.instruction: Place the cucumber pieces in a bowl and toss with half the salt. Leave for 10 minutes, then drain off any released liquid.
instructions.tip: This step keeps the salad crisp and prevents the dressing from becoming watery.

instructions.title: Mix the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, sugar, and chilli oil if using, until the sugar dissolves.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing before adding more salt because soy sauce is already salty.

instructions.title: Dress the cucumbers
instructions.instruction: Add the drained cucumbers to the dressing and toss thoroughly so every piece is coated.
instructions.tip: Use a wide bowl to make tossing easier without spilling.

instructions.title: Let the flavours develop
instructions.instruction: Refrigerate the salad for 10–15 minutes if time allows, tossing once halfway through.
instructions.tip: Do not leave it dressed for too long, or the cucumbers will gradually soften.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter over the toasted sesame seeds and spring onions. Serve chilled or cool alongside noodles, rice, or grilled dishes.
instructions.tip: Add the sesame seeds just before serving to keep them crunchy.

tips: Persian or English cucumbers work well because they have fewer large seeds.
For extra heat, add finely sliced fresh chilli or more chilli oil.
Serve soon after dressing for the crispest texture.

title: Shrimp Chow Fun
description: A Cantonese-inspired stir-fry of wide rice noodles, juicy shrimp, bean sprouts, spring onions, and a savoury soy-based sauce. High heat gives the noodles a lightly toasted flavour while keeping the shrimp tender.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: If using refrigerated fresh rice noodles, gently separate them according to the package directions. If they are firm, warm them briefly to loosen without breaking. Pat the shrimp dry.
instructions.tip: Handle rice noodles gently because they can tear when cold.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Combine the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, and white pepper in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Prepare the sauce before heating the wok because the noodles cook quickly.

instructions.title: Sear the shrimp
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of neutral oil in a wok over high heat. Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes per side until pink and nearly cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking the shrimp; they will warm through again when returned to the wok.

instructions.title: Fry the noodles
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the noodles and spread them out, letting them sit briefly before tossing. Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until hot and lightly browned in places.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if the wok is small to avoid steaming the noodles.

instructions.title: Add vegetables and sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic and spring onions and stir-fry for 20–30 seconds. Add the bean sprouts and pour in the sauce, tossing gently to coat the noodles evenly.
instructions.tip: Use two spatulas or tongs to turn the noodles without crushing them.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the shrimp to the wok and toss for another 1–2 minutes until hot and fully cooked. Add a splash of water if the noodles seem dry, then serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Serve straight from the wok for the best noodle texture.

tips: Fresh wide rice noodles give the most authentic texture; dried rice noodles can be used if prepared according to their package directions.
Keep the wok hot and avoid adding too much liquid.
For a vegetarian version, use tofu and vegetarian mushroom sauce instead of shrimp and oyster sauce.

title: Shrimp With Snow Peas
description: A light Chinese-style stir-fry of tender shrimp and crisp snow peas in a delicate garlic, ginger, and soy sauce. It comes together quickly and makes a fresh, balanced meal served with steamed rice.

instructions.title: Prepare the shrimp and snow peas
instructions.instruction: Pat the shrimp dry and ensure they are fully peeled and deveined. Trim the ends and remove the strings from the snow peas if necessary.
instructions.tip: Dry shrimp sear more effectively and release less liquid into the pan.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the soy sauce, oyster sauce, stock, white pepper, and cornflour mixed with the cold water.
instructions.tip: Stir the sauce again immediately before adding it because the cornflour may settle.

instructions.title: Sear the shrimp
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes per side until pink and nearly cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Do not cook the shrimp completely at this stage; they will return to the pan shortly.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic and ginger to the same pan and stir-fry for 20–30 seconds until fragrant. Add the snow peas and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat high and the vegetables moving to preserve their crunch.

instructions.title: Add the sauce
instructions.instruction: Pour the prepared sauce into the pan and stir for 1–2 minutes until it bubbles and lightly thickens around the snow peas.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of stock or water if the sauce becomes too thick.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the shrimp to the pan and toss for 1–2 minutes until fully opaque and cooked through. Finish with sesame oil and spring onions, then serve immediately with steamed rice.
instructions.tip: Shrimp are ready when they are opaque throughout; avoid cooking them until tightly curled.

tips: Do not overcook the snow peas; they should retain a slight crunch.
Add sliced mushrooms or red bell pepper for more colour and texture.
Serve with steamed rice or noodles for a more filling meal.

title: Beef Bourguignon
description: A classic French Burgundy beef stew featuring tender chunks of beef slowly braised in red wine with mushrooms, pearl onions, carrots, and aromatic herbs. Rich, comforting, and ideal for serving with crusty bread or creamy mashed potatoes.

ingredients.item: Beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes

instructions.title: Prepare the beef
instructions.instruction: Pat the beef cubes dry and season with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Dry beef browns better. Avoid crowding the pot, which causes the meat to steam.

instructions.title: Cook the bacon and aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the diced bacon to the pot and cook until lightly crisp. Add the chopped onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot to build flavor.

instructions.title: Build the braising liquid
instructions.instruction: Return the beef and any accumulated juices to the pot. Sprinkle with flour and stir for 1–2 minutes. Pour in the red wine and beef stock, stirring to combine. Add the thyme and bay leaves.
instructions.tip: Use a dry red wine you would enjoy drinking, such as Burgundy or Pinot Noir.

instructions.title: Braise until tender
instructions.instruction: Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer, cover, and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Cook for about 2 hours, checking occasionally, until the beef is nearly fork-tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the liquid at a gentle simmer rather than a vigorous boil for tender beef.

instructions.title: Cook the mushrooms and onions
instructions.instruction: About 20 minutes before the beef is done, melt the butter in a skillet. Cook the mushrooms and pearl onions for 8–10 minutes until golden. Add them to the stew and continue braising until the beef is very tender.
instructions.tip: Browning the mushrooms separately gives them a deeper flavor and better texture.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning. If the sauce is too thin, simmer the stew uncovered on the stovetop until slightly thickened. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.
instructions.tip: The flavor often improves overnight, making this an excellent make-ahead dish.

tips: Prepare the stew a day ahead and refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor.
Trim excess fat from the beef, but leave some marbling for tenderness.
Serve with mashed potatoes, buttered noodles, or crusty French bread.

alternatives: Additional beef stock with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
Omit and use extra olive oil

title: Coq au vin
description: A traditional French chicken stew braised slowly in red wine with mushrooms, bacon, pearl onions, garlic, and herbs. The chicken becomes tender while the wine-based sauce develops a deep, savory flavor.

instructions.title: Season and brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in batches on both sides. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Brown the skin well for richer flavor, but do not cook the chicken through at this stage.

instructions.title: Cook the bacon and vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the bacon and cook until lightly crisp. Stir in the chopped onion and carrot and cook for 4–5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: Use the rendered bacon fat to help soften the vegetables.

instructions.title: Add wine and stock
instructions.instruction: Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for a minute. Slowly pour in the red wine and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits from the base. Add the thyme and bay leaf.
instructions.tip: Stir thoroughly to prevent flour lumps from forming in the sauce.

instructions.title: Braise the chicken
instructions.instruction: Return the chicken and its juices to the pot, skin-side up. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 40–50 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Keep the simmer gentle so the chicken stays moist and the sauce does not reduce too quickly.

instructions.title: Cook the mushrooms and onions
instructions.instruction: In a separate skillet, cook the mushrooms and pearl onions with a small splash of oil for 8–10 minutes until golden. Add them to the stew for the final 10 minutes of cooking.
instructions.tip: Cooking these separately helps them retain texture and develop a browned flavor.

instructions.title: Adjust the sauce and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf and thyme stems. Check that the thickest chicken pieces have reached 74°C internally. Adjust the seasoning and simmer uncovered briefly if the sauce needs thickening. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
instructions.tip: Serve with mashed potatoes, buttered noodles, or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.

tips: Bone-in chicken adds flavor and is less likely to dry out during braising.
Prepare the stew ahead and reheat gently before serving.
Use a wine with good flavor rather than a sweet cooking wine.

alternatives: Chicken stock with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
Omit and add a little extra olive oil
Boneless chicken thighs with a shorter cooking time

title: Fish Stew with Rouille
description: A Provençal-style French fish stew with firm white fish, tomatoes, fennel, garlic, saffron, and a fragrant broth. It is served with rouille, a garlicky saffron mayonnaise traditionally spread on toasted bread and dipped into the stew.

ingredients.item: Firm white fish fillets, cut into large pieces

instructions.title: Make the rouille
instructions.instruction: Blend the mayonnaise, roasted red pepper, grated garlic, lemon juice, and cayenne until smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then refrigerate while preparing the stew.
instructions.tip: For a more traditional texture, use a thick garlic-and-saffron mayonnaise and keep the finished sauce chilled.

instructions.title: Soften the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and fennel and cook for 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in four minced garlic cloves and the tomato paste and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: Avoid browning the garlic heavily, as it can make the broth bitter.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes, fish stock, saffron, orange zest, bay leaf, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes to develop the flavor.
instructions.tip: Crush the saffron threads lightly and let them bloom in a spoonful of warm stock before adding them.

instructions.title: Cook the fish
instructions.instruction: Add the white fish pieces to the simmering broth and cook gently for 4–6 minutes, depending on their thickness. Avoid stirring vigorously so the fish stays intact.
instructions.tip: Use firm fish such as cod, hake, or monkfish that holds together in broth.

instructions.title: Add the prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the prawns and simmer for another 3–4 minutes, until they are opaque and cooked through. Remove the bay leaf and thyme stems and taste the broth for seasoning.
instructions.tip: Do not overcook the seafood; prawns become tough when left simmering too long.

instructions.title: Serve with rouille
instructions.instruction: Ladle the hot stew into bowls. Spread the rouille over toasted baguette slices or serve it alongside, allowing the bread to soak up the broth.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately while the seafood is tender and the toasted bread is crisp.

tips: Use a mixture of firm fish for varied texture and flavor.
Make the rouille ahead and keep it refrigerated until serving.
For a stronger seafood flavor, simmer fish bones in the stock before straining.

alternatives: Thick Greek yogurt with olive oil

title: French Lentils With Garlic and Thyme
description: A simple French side dish of earthy green lentils simmered with garlic, onion, carrots, and fresh thyme. The lentils hold their shape while absorbing the aromatic cooking liquid, making this a satisfying accompaniment or a light vegetarian main.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Rinse the lentils under cold water and drain. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 5–6 minutes until softened.
instructions.tip: French green lentils are ideal because they retain their shape during cooking.

instructions.title: Add garlic and herbs
instructions.instruction: Stir in the crushed garlic and cook for about 30 seconds. Add the lentils, thyme, bay leaf, and vegetable stock or water.
instructions.tip: Leave the garlic cloves whole or lightly crushed for a gentle, rounded flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer the lentils
instructions.instruction: Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
instructions.tip: Cooking time varies with the age of the lentils, so begin checking for tenderness after 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Drain if necessary
instructions.instruction: If excess liquid remains once the lentils are tender, drain off most of it, reserving a few spoonfuls to keep them moist. Remove the bay leaf and thyme stems.
instructions.tip: Do not drain completely dry; a little cooking liquid keeps the lentils succulent.

instructions.title: Season the lentils
instructions.instruction: Stir in the Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper, then taste and adjust the acidity or seasoning as needed.
instructions.tip: Adding vinegar near the end keeps the lentils from taking longer to soften.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Fold in the chopped parsley and a small drizzle of olive oil. Serve warm as a side dish or spoon over toasted bread or cooked grains for a light meal.
instructions.tip: The lentils are also delicious chilled and served as a salad the following day.

tips: Avoid adding acidic ingredients until the lentils are nearly tender.
For extra depth, cook the lentils in vegetable stock rather than water.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

alternatives: Omit and add extra vinegar to taste

title: French Onion Soup
description: A beloved French soup made by slowly caramelizing onions until deeply golden, then simmering them in beef stock with herbs. Served beneath toasted baguette and melted Gruyère, it is rich, savory, and comforting.

instructions.title: Slice the onions
instructions.instruction: Peel the onions and slice them thinly and evenly. Heat the butter and olive oil in a large heavy saucepan over medium-low heat.
instructions.tip: A heavy-based pan distributes heat evenly and helps prevent scorching.

instructions.title: Caramelize the onions
instructions.instruction: Add the onions and cook for 35–45 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deeply golden and sweet. Lower the heat if the onions begin sticking or darkening too quickly.
instructions.tip: Proper caramelization takes time; avoid increasing the heat to rush the process.

instructions.title: Add garlic and wine
instructions.instruction: Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for one minute. Pour in the white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan to release the browned onion flavor.
instructions.tip: The flour helps give the soup a lightly full-bodied texture.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Add the beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 25–30 minutes. Remove the herbs and season with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Taste before adding much salt because stock and cheese can already be salty.

instructions.title: Toast the bread
instructions.instruction: While the soup simmers, preheat the grill or broiler. Toast the baguette slices on both sides until crisp and lightly golden.
instructions.tip: Dry, crisp bread holds up better when topped with hot soup and melted cheese.

instructions.title: Add cheese and gratinate
instructions.instruction: Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls placed on a sturdy baking tray. Float one or two toast slices on each bowl and sprinkle generously with Gruyère. Grill for 2–4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden, watching carefully.
instructions.tip: Use oven-safe bowls and handle them with oven mitts when serving.

tips: Cook the onions slowly for the deepest, sweetest flavor.
Gruyère melts beautifully, but Comté or Emmental can also work.
If you do not have oven-safe bowls, melt the cheese on toast separately and place it over each serving.

alternatives: Additional stock with 1 tsp white wine vinegar

title: Pear Tarte Tatin
description: A French upside-down tart made with ripe but firm pears caramelized in butter and sugar beneath a crisp pastry crust. Once inverted, the fruit forms a glossy amber topping with a delicate balance of sweetness and buttery pastry.

ingredients.item: Firm pears, peeled, halved, and cored

instructions.title: Prepare the pears and pastry
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Peel, halve, and core the pears, then toss them gently with lemon juice. Roll the puff pastry into a circle slightly larger than a 23 cm ovenproof skillet or tart pan.
instructions.tip: Choose pears that are ripe enough to be fragrant but firm enough to hold their shape.

instructions.title: Make the caramel
