instructions.instruction: Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes, then serve with the chilled slaw and lemon wedges. Spoon any fully cooked pan juices over the chicken just before serving.
instructions.tip: Resting helps the juices redistribute through the meat.

tips: Marinate the chicken overnight for deeper flavour.
Adjust the chilli quantity to suit your preferred heat level.
Keep the slaw cold until serving for a refreshing contrast.

alternatives: Boneless chicken thighs, with a shorter cooking time

title: Portuguese barbecued pork (Febrar assadas)
description: Portuguese-style grilled pork prepared with garlic, paprika, white wine, bay leaf, and olive oil. The marinated pork is barbecued until tender and lightly charred, creating a savoury dish often served with potatoes, salad, or crusty bread.

instructions.title: Prepare the marinade
instructions.instruction: Combine the garlic, paprika, oregano, crushed bay leaves, white wine, vinegar, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
instructions.tip: Taste the marinade before adding the pork and adjust the acidity or seasoning as needed.

instructions.title: Marinate the pork
instructions.instruction: Add the pork steaks and turn them to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably 4–8 hours, turning once if possible.
instructions.tip: Marinate in the refrigerator rather than at room temperature.

instructions.title: Prepare the barbecue
instructions.instruction: Preheat a barbecue or grill to medium-high heat. Remove the pork from the marinade and let excess liquid drip off. Discard marinade that has contacted the raw pork, or boil it thoroughly before using it as a sauce.
instructions.tip: A lightly oiled grill grate helps prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the pork
instructions.instruction: Place the pork steaks over direct heat and grill for approximately 4–7 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until browned and cooked through. For whole-muscle pork steaks, check that the centre reaches at least 63°C followed by a 3-minute rest.
instructions.tip: Move the pork to a cooler part of the grill if flare-ups cause excessive charring.

instructions.title: Rest the meat
instructions.instruction: Transfer the grilled pork to a clean plate and rest for 3 minutes or longer for thicker cuts. Check the temperature before serving and slice against the grain if the steaks are particularly thick.
instructions.tip: Resting helps the meat retain its juices.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter chopped parsley over the pork and serve with lemon wedges, grilled vegetables, boiled potatoes, or a simple tomato salad.
instructions.tip: A little fresh lemon juice just before serving brightens the rich grilled pork.

tips: Pork shoulder steaks offer good flavour and stay moist on the grill.
Allow enough time for the marinade to flavour the meat.
Avoid excessive direct heat that burns the garlic and paprika before the pork cooks through.

alternatives: Pork loin steaks, with shorter cooking time
Water with an extra splash of vinegar

title: Portugese custard tarts
description: Portuguese pastéis de nata are crisp, flaky pastry shells filled with rich, lightly lemon-scented egg custard. Baked at high heat until the pastry is golden and the custard develops characteristic dark spots, they are delicious warm with a dusting of cinnamon.

ingredients.amount: A little, for greasing the tin if needed

instructions.title: Prepare the pastry
instructions.instruction: Roll the puff pastry tightly into a log. Cut it into 12 equal pieces and place each piece cut-side down into a greased muffin tin. Press and stretch the dough up the sides to create thin pastry shells, then refrigerate while making the custard.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry cold so it puffs into crisp layers during baking.

instructions.title: Infuse the milk
instructions.instruction: Pour the milk into a saucepan and add the lemon peel and cinnamon stick. Heat gently until steaming but not boiling, then remove from the heat and allow the flavours to infuse for 5 minutes.
instructions.tip: Avoid including the bitter white pith of the lemon peel.

instructions.title: Prepare the sugar syrup
instructions.instruction: Combine the sugar and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil and simmer for 3–5 minutes until slightly syrupy. Remove from the heat.
instructions.tip: Do not stir excessively once the syrup starts boiling, as sugar crystals can form on the sides.

instructions.title: Thicken the custard base
instructions.instruction: Whisk the flour with a small amount of the infused milk until smooth. Gradually whisk in the remaining milk, then return the mixture to a saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until it thickens slightly. Slowly whisk in the sugar syrup, then remove from the heat and cool for several minutes.
instructions.tip: Keep whisking to prevent lumps and avoid overheating the milk mixture.

instructions.title: Add the egg yolks and fill
instructions.instruction: Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon stick. Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl, then gradually mix in a little of the warm custard base before incorporating the yolks into the saucepan. Strain the mixture and pour it into the pastry shells, filling each about three-quarters full.
instructions.tip: Tempering the yolks helps prevent them from scrambling in the warm custard.

instructions.title: Bake until blistered
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 240–250°C, or as high as your oven safely allows. Bake for approximately 12–18 minutes, until the pastry is deeply golden and the custard has dark brown spots. Cool in the tin for a few minutes before carefully removing. Serve warm with ground cinnamon.
instructions.tip: Ovens vary considerably; watch the tarts closely during the final minutes.

tips: Keep the pastry cold before baking to preserve its flaky layers.
Strain the custard for a smooth filling.
Serve the tarts warm, ideally on the day they are baked.

alternatives: A mixture of milk and a little cream
A small amount of vanilla extract

title: Portuguese fish stew (Caldeirada de peixe)
description: A rustic Portuguese fish stew layered with firm white fish, potatoes, tomatoes, onions, peppers, garlic, herbs, and white wine. The ingredients simmer gently in one pot, creating a fragrant broth that captures the flavours of the Atlantic coast.

instructions.title: Prepare the fish and vegetables
instructions.instruction: Cut the fish into large, even chunks and pat dry. Peel and slice the potatoes, slice the onions and peppers, and chop the tomatoes and garlic.
instructions.tip: Large fish pieces are less likely to break apart during simmering.

instructions.title: Start the vegetable base
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large, wide, heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and peppers and cook for 5 minutes until beginning to soften. Stir in the garlic and paprika and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: A wide pot allows the ingredients to be layered without crushing the fish.

instructions.title: Layer the potatoes and tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Arrange a layer of potato slices over the vegetables, followed by some tomatoes. Season lightly with salt and pepper, add a bay leaf, and repeat the layers until the ingredients are used.
instructions.tip: Keep the potato slices reasonably thin so they cook in the same time as the stew.

instructions.title: Add the cooking liquid
instructions.instruction: Pour in the white wine and fish stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 20–25 minutes until the potatoes are almost tender. Avoid vigorous stirring; gently shake the pot if needed.
instructions.tip: If the liquid does not reach the upper layers, add a little more stock or water.

instructions.title: Cook the seafood
instructions.instruction: Arrange the fish chunks over the vegetables and simmer gently for 6–8 minutes. Add the prawns and cook for another 3–5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the prawns are fully cooked.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat low and avoid stirring after adding the fish to help the pieces stay intact.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaves, scatter the chopped parsley over the stew, and taste the broth for seasoning. Serve hot in deep bowls with lemon wedges and crusty bread.
instructions.tip: A final drizzle of good olive oil enhances the flavour of the finished broth.

tips: Choose firm fish that holds together during simmering.
Add seafood near the end to avoid overcooking.
Use a wide pot and gentle heat to keep the layers intact.

alternatives: Water with a little extra seasoning

title: Portuguese prego with green piri-piri
description: A Portuguese steak sandwich featuring thinly sliced beef seared with garlic and olive oil, served in a crusty roll with a fresh green piri-piri sauce made from chillies, herbs, lemon, and vinegar. It is a bold, savoury sandwich with bright, spicy flavour.

ingredients.item: Portuguese rolls or crusty bread rolls

instructions.title: Make the green piri-piri sauce
instructions.instruction: Blend the green chillies, parsley, coriander, garlic for the sauce, lemon juice, vinegar, and extra-virgin olive oil until finely chopped but not completely smooth. Season to taste and set aside.
instructions.tip: Start with one chilli if you prefer a milder sauce, then add more after tasting.

instructions.title: Prepare the steak
instructions.instruction: Slice the beef thinly across the grain and pat dry. Season both sides with salt and black pepper. If the slices are uneven, gently flatten them between sheets of baking parchment.
instructions.tip: Thin slices cook quickly and are easier to bite through in a sandwich.

instructions.title: Sauté the garlic
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sliced garlic and bay leaf and cook briefly until fragrant, taking care not to burn the garlic.
instructions.tip: Remove the garlic temporarily if it starts to brown too quickly.

instructions.title: Sear the beef
instructions.instruction: Add the beef in batches and sear for approximately 1–3 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. Transfer the cooked slices to a plate. Avoid overcrowding the pan.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches so the beef sears instead of releasing too much liquid.

instructions.title: Deglaze the pan
instructions.instruction: Pour the white wine into the hot skillet and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer for 1–2 minutes until slightly reduced, then return the beef and any accumulated juices to the pan and toss briefly to coat.
instructions.tip: If you prefer not to use wine, substitute beef stock with a small splash of vinegar.

instructions.title: Assemble the prego
instructions.instruction: Split the rolls and warm them briefly. Fill each roll with the garlic beef and spoon over some pan juices. Add green piri-piri sauce to taste and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Serve extra sauce on the side so everyone can adjust the heat.

tips: Slice the beef thinly across the grain for a tender sandwich.
Make the green piri-piri sauce ahead of time and refrigerate it until serving.
Warm the bread briefly to give it a crisp crust without drying out the inside.

alternatives: Beef flank steak, thinly sliced across the grain
Fresh mint in a small quantity

title: Chickpea, chorizo & spinach stew
description: A hearty Spanish-inspired stew combining smoky chorizo, tender chickpeas, tomatoes, and fresh spinach in a rich paprika-seasoned broth. Serve with crusty bread for a comforting one-pot meal.

instructions.title: Brown the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced chorizo and cook for 4–5 minutes until browned and its smoky oils are released.
instructions.tip: Use a slotted spoon to remove some excess fat if the chorizo releases a lot.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the diced onion to the pan and cook for 4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and cumin and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic moving so it does not burn.

instructions.title: Build the stew
instructions.instruction: Add the chopped tomatoes, chickpeas, and stock. Stir well, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
instructions.tip: For a thicker stew, lightly mash a few chickpeas against the side of the saucepan.

instructions.title: Simmer
instructions.instruction: Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.tip: Let the liquid reduce until it coats the chickpeas without becoming dry.

instructions.title: Add the spinach
instructions.instruction: Stir in the spinach and cook for 2–3 minutes until wilted. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Add the spinach in batches if your saucepan is small.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle the stew into bowls and serve hot, with crusty bread or cooked rice if desired.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lemon juice just before serving brightens the smoky flavours.

tips: Use Spanish cooking chorizo rather than thinly sliced cured chorizo for the best texture.
The stew tastes even better the next day as the flavours develop.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes for extra heat.

title: Chocolate churros with chocolate & salted caramel sauce
description: Crisp Spanish-style churros with a tender centre, coated in cinnamon sugar and served with silky chocolate sauce and buttery salted caramel for an indulgent dessert.

ingredients.amount: 750 ml, or enough for deep frying

instructions.title: Make the churros dough
instructions.instruction: Bring the water and butter to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from the heat, add the flour, and stir vigorously until a smooth dough forms and pulls away from the sides. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until fully incorporated.
instructions.tip: Add the egg only after the dough has cooled slightly so it does not scramble.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauces
instructions.instruction: For the chocolate sauce, warm 100 ml cream until steaming, pour over the chopped chocolate, and stir until smooth. For the caramel, melt the granulated sugar in a clean saucepan over medium heat until amber. Carefully whisk in the butter, then slowly add the 60 ml cream. Stir in the sea salt and let cool slightly.
instructions.tip: The caramel will bubble vigorously when cream is added, so use a deep saucepan and keep your hands clear.

instructions.title: Heat the oil
instructions.instruction: Heat the frying oil in a deep, heavy saucepan to 175–180°C. Mix the caster sugar and cinnamon in a shallow bowl.
instructions.tip: Use a thermometer for consistent results; oil that is too cool makes greasy churros.

instructions.title: Pipe the churros
instructions.instruction: Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star-shaped nozzle. Pipe 8–10 cm lengths carefully into the hot oil, cutting each length with kitchen scissors.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan and keep the piping nozzle close to the oil.

instructions.title: Fry and coat
instructions.instruction: Fry the churros in batches for about 3–4 minutes, turning until golden and crisp. Drain briefly on kitchen paper, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while still warm.
instructions.tip: Make sure each churro is cooked through before serving.

instructions.title: Serve with sauces
instructions.instruction: Arrange the warm churros on a serving plate and serve immediately with the chocolate and salted caramel sauces for dipping.
instructions.tip: If either sauce thickens, warm it gently over low heat before serving.

tips: A star nozzle creates the classic churro ridges and helps the exterior crisp evenly.
Serve the churros immediately for the best texture.
Keep the sauces warm over very low heat if serving over a longer period.

alternatives: Coconut cream for a dairy-free variation

title: Chorizo & chickpea soup
description: A warming, rustic soup with smoky chorizo, creamy chickpeas, vegetables, and a paprika-infused broth. It is filling enough for lunch and easy to prepare in one pot.

instructions.title: Brown the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced chorizo and cook for 4 minutes until browned and fragrant.
instructions.tip: The chorizo releases flavourful oils, so only a small amount of additional oil is needed.

instructions.title: Soften the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to soften. Add the garlic and paprika and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables into similarly sized pieces so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Add the broth
instructions.instruction: Stir in the chopped tomatoes, chickpeas, stock, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat.
instructions.tip: Use low-sodium stock so you can control the final seasoning.

instructions.title: Simmer the soup
instructions.instruction: Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the flavours have blended.
instructions.tip: For a thicker texture, mash a small ladleful of chickpeas and return them to the pot.

instructions.title: Season and finish
instructions.instruction: Remove the bay leaf. Taste the soup and season with black pepper and salt if needed. Stir through the chopped parsley.
instructions.tip: Chorizo and stock can already be salty, so taste before adding extra salt.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle into warm bowls and serve with crusty bread or toasted sourdough.
instructions.tip: A small squeeze of lemon juice can balance the smoky richness.

tips: This soup can be refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheated gently.
Add chopped kale or spinach during the last few minutes for extra greens.
For a spicier soup, use hot chorizo or add chilli flakes.

title: Chorizo & salt-boiled egg salad
description: A satisfying salad of smoky pan-fried chorizo, tender greens, potatoes, and eggs seasoned with salt and pepper, finished with a sharp mustard vinaigrette.

instructions.title: Cook the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Place the baby potatoes in a saucepan, cover with water, add a generous pinch of salt, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until tender, then drain and halve.
instructions.tip: Choose potatoes of similar size for even cooking.

instructions.title: Boil the eggs
instructions.instruction: Place the eggs in a saucepan of cold water with a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 7–9 minutes depending on how firm you like the yolks. Cool under cold running water, peel, and halve.
instructions.tip: For easier peeling, gently crack the shells all over before peeling under water.

instructions.title: Cook the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Place the chorizo in a frying pan over medium heat and cook for 4–5 minutes until browned and the edges are slightly crisp. Transfer to a plate, reserving a little of the flavoured oil.
instructions.tip: Drain excess fat if needed, but keep a teaspoon for the dressing.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, a teaspoon of the reserved chorizo oil, and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing before adding salt because the chorizo is already seasoned.

instructions.title: Assemble the salad
instructions.instruction: Arrange the salad leaves, potatoes, cherry tomatoes, and red onion in a large bowl. Add the warm chorizo and drizzle with the dressing.
instructions.tip: Toss the potatoes with a little dressing while warm so they absorb more flavour.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Top with the halved eggs and chopped parsley. Season lightly with salt and pepper, then serve straight away.
instructions.tip: Serve the chorizo warm against the cool leaves for a pleasing contrast.

tips: Use a mix of peppery leaves and mild lettuce for varied texture.
Cook the eggs a little longer if you prefer fully set yolks.
Add roasted red peppers or olives for a more Mediterranean flavour.

title: Chorizo & tomato salad
description: A simple Mediterranean-style salad pairing juicy ripe tomatoes with crisped chorizo, red onion, fresh herbs, and a sherry vinegar dressing.

instructions.title: Prepare the tomatoes
instructions.instruction: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and place them in a serving bowl. Sprinkle lightly with salt and leave for 5 minutes to release their juices.
instructions.tip: Use ripe, fragrant tomatoes for the best flavour.

instructions.title: Crisp the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Add the chorizo slices and cook for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until lightly crisp and fragrant.
instructions.tip: The chorizo usually releases enough fat to cook without extra oil.

instructions.title: Mix the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the olive oil, sherry vinegar, grated garlic, and black pepper in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: If you do not have sherry vinegar, red wine vinegar works well.

instructions.title: Add the onion and herbs
instructions.instruction: Add the thinly sliced red onion, parsley, and basil to the tomatoes. Pour over the dressing and toss gently.
instructions.tip: Slice the onion very thinly to keep its sharpness from overpowering the tomatoes.

instructions.title: Combine and serve
instructions.instruction: Arrange the warm chorizo over the salad and spoon over any tomato juices from the bowl. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately so the chorizo stays warm and the tomatoes remain fresh.

tips: A mixture of red, yellow, and heirloom tomatoes makes the salad colourful.
Add toasted bread cubes to turn it into a more substantial meal.
Avoid refrigerating ripe tomatoes just before serving, as chilling can dull their flavour.

title: Chorizo, potato & cheese omelette
description: A hearty Spanish-inspired omelette filled with tender potatoes, smoky chorizo, and melted cheese. It is delicious served warm for brunch or with a crisp green salad for dinner.

instructions.title: Cook the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Boil the diced potatoes in lightly salted water for 7–9 minutes until just tender but not falling apart. Drain thoroughly.
instructions.tip: Cut the potatoes into small, even cubes so they cook quickly.

instructions.title: Brown the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add the chorizo and cook for 3–4 minutes until it begins to release its oils.
instructions.tip: Use a pan that can comfortably hold all the eggs and fillings.

instructions.title: Soften the onion
instructions.instruction: Add the onion to the chorizo and cook for 3 minutes until softened. Add the drained potatoes and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring gently.
instructions.tip: Let the potatoes take on a little colour for extra flavour.

instructions.title: Beat the eggs
instructions.instruction: Whisk the eggs with the milk, grated cheese, parsley, black pepper, and a small pinch of salt.
instructions.tip: Go easy on the salt because the chorizo and cheese can be salty.

instructions.title: Cook the omelette
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat to low and pour the egg mixture over the potato and chorizo filling. Cook for 6–8 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is nearly cooked.
instructions.tip: Gently lift the edges to let uncooked egg run underneath.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Cover the pan briefly to help the top set, or place it under a preheated grill until fully cooked. Rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve.
instructions.tip: Use an oven-safe pan if finishing the omelette under the grill.

tips: For a traditional Spanish-style texture, allow the cooked potato mixture to cool slightly before adding it to the eggs.
Serve with sliced tomatoes or a green salad to balance the richness.
Leftover omelette can be refrigerated and eaten cold the next day.

title: Clam, chorizo & white bean stew
description: A coastal-inspired stew of fresh clams, smoky chorizo, creamy white beans, garlic, and tomatoes simmered in a savoury broth. Serve with crusty bread to soak up the juices.

instructions.title: Prepare the clams
instructions.instruction: Rinse and scrub the clams under cold running water. Discard any cracked clams and any open clams that do not close when tapped.
instructions.tip: Keep clams chilled until you are ready to cook them.

instructions.title: Brown the chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large, lidded pot over medium heat. Add the chorizo and cook for 4 minutes until browned and fragrant.
instructions.tip: Use a pot wide enough to hold the clams in a fairly even layer.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Avoid browning the garlic too deeply, as it can turn bitter.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Pour in the white wine and simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly. Add the tomatoes, fish stock, and white beans, then simmer for 8 minutes.
instructions.tip: If using salted stock, taste the broth before adding any extra seasoning.

instructions.title: Steam the clams
instructions.instruction: Add the clams, cover tightly, and cook for 5–8 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally, until the shells open. Discard any clams that remain closed after cooking.
instructions.tip: Do not overcook the clams; remove the pot from the heat as soon as they have opened.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in most of the parsley and black pepper. Ladle into bowls, scatter over the remaining parsley, and serve hot with crusty bread.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lemon adds freshness to the smoky broth.

tips: Discard clams with broken shells or those that do not close when tapped before cooking.
For a richer broth, stir in a spoonful of the cooking liquid from the clams after straining it if sandy.
Serve immediately while the clams are tender.

alternatives: Additional fish stock with 1 tsp lemon juice

title: Easy Spanish chicken
description: An easy one-pan Spanish-inspired chicken dish with paprika-seasoned chicken, sweet peppers, tomatoes, olives, and herbs. It is simple enough for a weeknight and pairs well with rice or crusty bread.

instructions.title: Season the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season with smoked paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Drying the chicken helps it brown instead of steam.

instructions.title: Brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 3–4 minutes on each side, then transfer it to a plate.
instructions.tip: Brown the chicken in batches if the pan is crowded.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and red pepper to the same pan and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Scrape up the browned bits left by the chicken to add flavour to the sauce.

instructions.title: Make the sauce
instructions.instruction: Stir in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, then add the olives.
instructions.tip: If the tomatoes taste sharp, a small pinch of sugar can balance the sauce.

instructions.title: Simmer the chicken
instructions.instruction: Return the chicken and any resting juices to the pan. Cover partially and simmer for 18–22 minutes, turning the chicken once, until cooked through and tender.
instructions.tip: Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 74°C at its thickest point.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Taste the sauce, adjust the seasoning, and serve with rice, potatoes, or crusty bread.
instructions.tip: Allow the chicken to rest in the sauce for a few minutes before serving.

tips: Chicken thighs remain juicy during simmering, but chicken breast can also be used with a shorter cooking time.
Add sliced chorizo before the vegetables for a smokier version.
Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

title: gambas al ajillo
description: A classic Spanish tapas dish of juicy prawns gently cooked in fragrant olive oil with plenty of garlic, dried chilli, and parsley. Serve sizzling with crusty bread to mop up the infused oil.

instructions.title: Prepare the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry with kitchen paper and season lightly with salt.
instructions.tip: Dry prawns sear better and are less likely to dilute the garlic oil.

instructions.title: Infuse the oil
instructions.instruction: Place the olive oil in a wide frying pan over low-medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes and cook gently for 2–3 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and pale golden.
instructions.tip: Do not let the garlic turn dark brown, as it will taste bitter.

instructions.title: Add paprika and prawns
instructions.instruction: Stir in the smoked paprika, then add the prawns in a single layer. Increase the heat to medium and cook for 1–2 minutes on each side, depending on their size.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook in batches if necessary.

instructions.title: Deglaze with sherry
instructions.instruction: Pour in the dry sherry and let it bubble for about 1 minute, scraping up the flavourful bits from the pan.
instructions.tip: Keep the pan uncovered so the sherry reduces quickly.

instructions.title: Finish the dish
instructions.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat when the prawns are opaque and cooked through. Stir in the parsley and lemon juice.
instructions.tip: Prawns cook quickly, so remove them from the heat as soon as they are done.

instructions.title: Serve sizzling
instructions.instruction: Transfer the prawns and garlic oil to a warm shallow dish. Serve immediately with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions.tip: Warm the serving dish first so the oil stays hot at the table.

tips: Use fresh or fully thawed prawns and pat them dry before cooking.
Serve as tapas or alongside rice for a fuller meal.
Adjust the chilli to suit your preferred level of heat.

alternatives: 1 tbsp lemon juice mixed with 1 tbsp water

title: Garlicky prawns with sherry
description: Succulent prawns cooked in a buttery garlic sauce deglazed with dry sherry, finished with lemon and parsley. This quick seafood dish works beautifully as a starter or as a main with rice or bread.

instructions.title: Prepare the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry and season lightly with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: If using frozen prawns, thaw them completely and drain well first.

instructions.title: Sauté the garlic
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for about 1 minute until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate to prevent the butter and garlic from burning.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side until they turn pink and opaque.
instructions.tip: If the pan is small, cook the prawns in two batches.

instructions.title: Add the sherry
instructions.instruction: Pour in the dry sherry and simmer for 2–3 minutes, allowing it to reduce slightly and form a light sauce.
instructions.tip: Use a dry sherry rather than a sweet dessert sherry for a balanced savoury flavour.

instructions.title: Finish the sauce
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lemon juice, lemon zest, and parsley. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
instructions.tip: Add a small splash of water if the sauce reduces too much.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Serve the prawns hot with the garlic-sherry sauce spooned over them, accompanied by crusty bread, rice, or steamed vegetables.
instructions.tip: A little extra parsley and lemon zest just before serving keeps the flavours fresh.

tips: Do not overcook the prawns, as they become firm and rubbery.
For a richer finish, swirl in a small extra knob of butter after removing the pan from the heat.
Serve straight away while the sauce is glossy.

alternatives: Fish stock with a small squeeze of lemon

title: Drunken noodles (pad kee mao)
description: A bold Thai stir-fry of wide rice noodles, tender chicken, garlic, chilli, vegetables, and fragrant Thai basil tossed in a savoury, slightly sweet sauce. It delivers the signature balance of heat, saltiness, and fresh herbal flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions until just tender. Drain well and toss with a few drops of oil to prevent sticking.
instructions.tip: Keep the noodles slightly firm because they will cook further in the wok.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: In a small bowl, combine the light soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, and brown sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
instructions.tip: Prepare the sauce before heating the wok, as stir-frying moves quickly.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until nearly cooked through. Transfer to a plate if the pan is crowded.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if needed to avoid steaming the chicken.

instructions.title: Fry the aromatics and vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic and chillies to the hot wok and stir-fry for 20–30 seconds. Add the bell pepper, baby corn, and spring onions and cook for 2 minutes.
instructions.tip: Keep the ingredients moving to prevent the garlic from burning.

instructions.title: Toss the noodles
instructions.instruction: Return the chicken to the wok and add the noodles and sauce. Toss vigorously for 2–3 minutes until the noodles are coated and the chicken is cooked through.
instructions.tip: If the noodles stick, add a tablespoon of water and toss again.

instructions.title: Add basil and serve
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and fold in the Thai basil until just wilted. Divide between bowls and serve with lime wedges.
instructions.tip: Add extra fresh chilli if you prefer a hotter version, and use Thai holy basil when available for a more traditional flavour.

tips: Use a very hot wok and prepare all ingredients before cooking.
Wide fresh rice noodles can be used instead of dried noodles; handle them gently to avoid breaking.
For a vegetarian version, replace chicken with firm tofu and use vegetarian stir-fry sauce instead of fish and oyster sauces.

title: Spring onion and prawn empanadas
description: Golden, flaky pastry parcels filled with juicy prawns, fresh spring onions, garlic, and a lightly spiced filling. These savoury empanadas make an excellent snack, appetiser, or light lunch.

instructions.title: Prepare the pastry
instructions.instruction: Mix the flour and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add cold water gradually and mix until a firm dough forms. Wrap and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
instructions.tip: Avoid overworking the dough to keep the pastry tender and flaky.

instructions.title: Cook the filling
instructions.instruction: Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the spring onions, bell pepper, and garlic, and cook for 3 minutes until softened. Stir in the paprika and cumin.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetables finely chopped so the filling fits neatly inside the pastry.

instructions.title: Add the prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the chopped prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and nearly cooked through. Stir in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and let the filling cool completely.
instructions.tip: Cool the filling before assembling to prevent the pastry from becoming soggy.

instructions.title: Shape the empanadas
instructions.instruction: Roll the chilled dough to approximately 3 mm thick. Cut out 12–14 cm circles. Place a spoonful of filling on one half of each circle, leaving a border around the edge.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill the pastry, or the edges may open during baking.

instructions.title: Seal and glaze
instructions.instruction: Brush the pastry edges lightly with water, fold each circle over the filling, and press firmly to seal. Crimp the edges with a fork and brush the tops with beaten egg.
instructions.tip: Make sure there are no gaps in the sealed edges.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Place the empanadas on a lined baking tray and bake in a preheated oven at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until crisp and golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
instructions.tip: Allow steam to escape naturally after baking rather than covering the empanadas.

tips: Prepare the filling a day ahead and refrigerate it until needed.
For extra flavour, add finely chopped coriander or parsley.
Freeze uncooked, assembled empanadas on a tray before transferring them to a freezer-safe container.

title: Fish Soup (Ukha)
description: A traditional Russian fish soup featuring delicate pieces of white fish, potatoes, carrots, and onion in a clear, lightly seasoned broth with fresh dill. Its clean flavours make it a comforting yet light meal.

ingredients.item: Firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks

instructions.title: Prepare the broth
instructions.instruction: Pour the water or fish stock into a large pot. Add the onion, bay leaf, and peppercorns and bring to a gentle boil.
instructions.tip: A light stock keeps the delicate flavour of the fish at the centre of the soup.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the potatoes and carrot to the pot. Reduce the heat and simmer for 12–15 minutes until the vegetables are almost tender.
instructions.tip: Cut the potatoes into evenly sized pieces for consistent cooking.

instructions.title: Add the fish
instructions.instruction: Gently lower the fish chunks into the simmering broth. Cook for 6–10 minutes, depending on thickness, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
instructions.tip: Avoid vigorous stirring, which can break the fish into small pieces.

instructions.title: Season the soup
instructions.instruction: Remove the onion, bay leaf, and peppercorns if desired. Season the broth with salt and add the lemon juice.
instructions.tip: Add lemon gradually so it enhances rather than overwhelms the mild broth.

instructions.title: Add fresh herbs
instructions.instruction: Stir in the chopped dill and parsley, reserving a little dill for garnish. Let the soup stand off the heat for 2 minutes.
instructions.tip: Fresh dill is particularly important for the characteristic flavour of ukha.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle the fish and vegetables into warm bowls with plenty of broth. Garnish with the remaining dill and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Serve with dark rye bread or boiled potatoes on the side.

tips: Cod, haddock, pollock, or pike-perch are suitable choices for this soup.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer after adding the fish.
For a more substantial soup, add a small handful of rice with the potatoes.

alternatives: Water with a little extra seasoning

title: Lamb Pilaf (Plov)
description: A Central Asian-style pilaf of tender lamb, long-grain rice, carrots, onions, and cumin cooked together in a fragrant broth. The rice absorbs the meat juices and spices to create a rich, satisfying one-pot meal.

ingredients.item: Lamb shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes

instructions.title: Rinse the rice
instructions.instruction: Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Leave it to drain while preparing the meat and vegetables.
instructions.tip: Rinsing removes excess surface starch and helps keep the grains separate.

instructions.title: Brown the lamb
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a heavy, wide pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the lamb in batches and brown on all sides, then transfer it to a plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pot, as the lamb needs to brown rather than steam.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables and spices
instructions.instruction: Add the onions to the same pot and cook for 5 minutes. Add the carrots and cook for another 5 minutes, then stir in the cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Cut the carrots into thin strips rather than grating them so they retain their texture.

instructions.title: Braise the lamb
instructions.instruction: Return the lamb to the pot and pour in enough water or stock to nearly cover it. Add the whole garlic heads, cover, and simmer for 35–45 minutes until the lamb begins to soften.
instructions.tip: Check the liquid occasionally and add a little water if the pot becomes too dry.

instructions.title: Add the rice
instructions.instruction: Spread the drained rice evenly over the lamb and vegetables without stirring everything together. Add enough hot water to cover the rice by about 1–1.5 cm, adjusting for the liquid already in the pot. Add the optional raisins.
instructions.tip: Keep the rice layer level so it cooks evenly.

instructions.title: Steam and rest
instructions.instruction: Bring the liquid to a gentle boil, then cook uncovered until most of the liquid has been absorbed. Make several holes through the rice with the handle of a spoon, cover tightly, and cook on very low heat for 15–20 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest for 10 minutes before fluffing and serving.
instructions.tip: Avoid stirring during the steaming stage; this helps preserve distinct grains of rice.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pot with a tight-fitting lid for even cooking.
Lamb shoulder is ideal because it becomes tender during slow cooking.
Serve with sliced tomatoes, cucumber salad, or plain yogurt.

alternatives: Medium-grain rice, adjusted for liquid and cooking time

title: Potato Salad (Olivier Salad)
description: A popular Eastern European salad made with diced potatoes, carrots, peas, pickles, eggs, and a creamy mayonnaise dressing. Olivier salad is commonly served chilled at celebrations and family gatherings.

instructions.title: Cook the potatoes and carrots
instructions.instruction: Place the potatoes and carrots in a saucepan, cover with water, and simmer until tender, about 15–20 minutes for the potatoes and 10–15 minutes for the carrots. Drain and cool completely.
instructions.tip: Cook the vegetables whole to prevent them from absorbing too much water.

instructions.title: Boil the eggs
instructions.instruction: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 9–10 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel, and dice.
instructions.tip: Cool the eggs completely before mixing them into the salad.

instructions.title: Cook the peas
instructions.instruction: Cook the frozen peas in boiling water for 2–3 minutes until tender. Drain and rinse briefly with cold water, then leave to dry.
instructions.tip: Do not overcook the peas; they should retain their shape and colour.

instructions.title: Dice the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Peel the cooled potatoes and carrots, then cut them into small, even cubes. Dice the pickles and ham to a similar size.
instructions.tip: Uniform pieces make the salad easier to mix and give each serving a balanced combination of ingredients.

instructions.title: Mix the salad
instructions.instruction: Combine the potatoes, carrots, eggs, peas, pickles, and ham in a large bowl. Fold in the mayonnaise, mustard, and dill until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Fold gently to avoid crushing the potatoes.

instructions.title: Chill and serve
instructions.instruction: Season with salt and black pepper, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. Stir gently and check the seasoning just before serving.
instructions.tip: Keep the salad refrigerated until it is ready to serve.

tips: Chill the cooked vegetables before dicing to help them hold their shape.
For a lighter dressing, replace part of the mayonnaise with plain Greek yogurt.
For food safety, refrigerate promptly and avoid leaving the salad at room temperature for extended periods.

title: Air fryer patatas bravas
description: Crispy golden potato cubes made in the air fryer and served with a smoky, mildly spicy Spanish tomato sauce. This lighter take on the classic tapas dish is perfect for sharing.

instructions.title: Prepare the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Cut the potatoes into evenly sized cubes. Rinse under cold water to remove excess starch, then dry thoroughly with a clean towel.
instructions.tip: Dry potatoes crisp better in the air fryer.

instructions.title: Season the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and salt until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Use just enough oil to coat the surfaces without leaving excess oil at the bottom of the bowl.

instructions.title: Air-fry until crisp
instructions.instruction: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C if required. Arrange the potatoes in a single layer and cook for 20–25 minutes, shaking the basket every 7–8 minutes, until golden and tender.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding.

instructions.title: Make the bravas sauce
instructions.instruction: Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste, chopped tomatoes, hot paprika, and cayenne.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate so the garlic does not burn.

instructions.title: Simmer and season the sauce
instructions.instruction: Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes until thickened. Stir in the red wine vinegar and season to taste. Blend if you prefer a smooth sauce.
instructions.tip: Add a tablespoon of water if the sauce becomes too thick.

instructions.title: Serve the patatas bravas
instructions.instruction: Transfer the crisp potatoes to a serving dish, spoon the warm bravas sauce over them or serve it alongside, and garnish with chopped parsley.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately so the potatoes remain crisp.

tips: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 15 minutes if you have extra time, then dry them very well.
Adjust the cayenne to control the sauce's heat.
For a creamy contrast, serve with a small bowl of garlic aioli.

title: Arroz al horno (baked rice)
description: A traditional Valencian-style oven-baked rice dish featuring rice, chickpeas, potatoes, tomatoes, garlic, and pork sausage in a rich, paprika-scented broth. Baking gives the rice a deeply savoury flavour and a lightly toasted surface.

ingredients.item: Pork ribs, cut into small pieces
Spanish morcilla or cooking sausage, sliced

instructions.title: Heat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Warm the chicken stock in a saucepan and steep the saffron in a small amount of the hot stock.
instructions.tip: Hot stock helps the rice begin cooking as soon as it enters the oven.

instructions.title: Brown the meat
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof casserole or frying pan. Brown the pork ribs on all sides, then add the sausage and cook for 2–3 minutes. Transfer the meat to a plate if needed.
instructions.tip: Brown the meat in batches if the pan is crowded.

instructions.title: Prepare the rice base
instructions.instruction: Add the rice to the pan and stir for 1–2 minutes to coat the grains in the cooking oil. Stir in the paprika and chickpeas, then arrange the meat evenly through the rice.
instructions.tip: Use an ovenproof dish wide enough for the rice to cook in a fairly shallow layer.

instructions.title: Arrange the toppings
instructions.instruction: Pour in the hot stock and saffron mixture. Arrange the potato and tomato slices on top and place the whole garlic head in the centre.
instructions.tip: Spread the rice evenly and avoid stirring it once the stock has been added.

instructions.title: Bake the rice
instructions.instruction: Transfer the dish to the oven and bake uncovered for 30–40 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed. Add a little extra hot stock if the rice becomes dry before it is cooked.
instructions.tip: Cooking time varies with the rice variety and the depth of the dish.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the dish from the oven and rest for 5–10 minutes. Check that the meat is fully cooked and tender, then serve the rice with the roasted garlic and toppings.
instructions.tip: Allowing the rice to rest helps the grains settle and the remaining moisture distribute evenly.

tips: Use short- or medium-grain rice for a texture closer to traditional Valencian baked rice.
Morcilla adds traditional depth, but a firm cooking sausage can be used if it is unavailable.
Check the liquid level during baking and use hot stock if extra moisture is needed.

title: Arroz con gambas y calamar
description: A Spanish seafood rice dish combining prawns and tender squid with garlic, tomatoes, paprika, and saffron-infused stock. The rice absorbs the seafood flavours for a fragrant, satisfying meal inspired by coastal Spanish cooking.

ingredients.item: Ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

instructions.title: Prepare the seafood and stock
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns and squid dry. Warm the fish stock in a saucepan and steep the saffron in a small ladleful of the hot stock.
instructions.tip: Keep the stock hot throughout cooking so the rice cooks evenly.

instructions.title: Sear the seafood
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a wide paella pan or frying pan over medium-high heat. Briefly sear the prawns for about 1 minute per side and the squid for 1–2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Do not cook the seafood fully at this stage, as it will finish cooking with the rice.

instructions.title: Make the sofrito
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining olive oil to the pan. Cook the bell pepper for 3 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika. Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 5–7 minutes until thickened.
instructions.tip: Let the tomato mixture reduce well to build a concentrated flavour base.

instructions.title: Toast the rice
instructions.instruction: Add the rice and stir for 1–2 minutes until the grains are coated in the tomato mixture. Pour in the hot stock and saffron mixture and season carefully.
instructions.tip: Spread the rice evenly and avoid stirring once the stock is added.

instructions.title: Cook the rice
instructions.instruction: Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for about 15 minutes, adjusting the heat to maintain a steady simmer. Arrange the prawns and squid over the rice during the final 5–7 minutes, cooking until the rice is tender and the seafood is opaque.
instructions.tip: If the rice is still firm and the pan is dry, add a small amount of hot stock.

instructions.title: Rest and garnish
instructions.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat, cover loosely, and rest for 5 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
instructions.tip: A short resting period helps the rice finish absorbing moisture without becoming mushy.

tips: Short-grain rice gives a more traditional texture, but medium-grain rice also works well.
Use good-quality fish stock and adjust salt only after tasting it.
Serve immediately for the best seafood texture.

title: Chicken & chorizo rice pot
description: A one-pot Spanish-inspired rice dish with golden chicken, smoky chorizo, peppers, tomatoes, and paprika-seasoned rice. The rice cooks directly in the flavourful broth, making this a practical and satisfying family dinner.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into chunks

instructions.title: Brown the chicken and chorizo
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep saucepan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with black pepper and a little salt, then brown for 4–5 minutes. Add the chorizo and cook for another 3 minutes.
instructions.tip: Brown the chicken in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and oregano and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan for extra flavour.

instructions.title: Add tomatoes and rice
instructions.instruction: Stir in the chopped tomatoes and rice, coating the grains in the seasoned oil. Cook for 1 minute.
instructions.tip: Toasting the rice briefly helps it absorb the flavourful cooking liquid.

instructions.title: Pour in the stock
instructions.instruction: Add the hot chicken stock and bring to a gentle boil. Stir once to distribute the rice evenly, then reduce the heat to low.
instructions.tip: Use hot stock to avoid slowing the cooking process.

instructions.title: Simmer until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover and cook for 15–18 minutes, or according to the rice package instructions, until the rice is nearly tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Stir in the peas for the final 5 minutes.
instructions.tip: Keep the lid on and avoid frequent stirring so the rice cooks evenly.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Check that the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender. Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork, garnish with parsley, and serve.
instructions.tip: If the rice is still firm, add a splash of hot stock and cook covered for a few more minutes.

tips: Choose cooking chorizo for the best flavour and texture in the rice.
Avoid adding too much salt before tasting, as chorizo and stock can be salty.
Let the rice rest before serving to help it finish steaming.

title: Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts
description: Tender chicken simmered with fragrant saffron, sweet raisins, toasted pine nuts, and warm spices in a lightly sweet and savoury sauce. Inspired by Mediterranean and Spanish flavour combinations, this elegant dish pairs beautifully with couscous or rice.

instructions.title: Bloom the saffron
instructions.instruction: Place the saffron threads in a small bowl and pour over 2 tablespoons of warm chicken stock. Leave to infuse for 5–10 minutes.
instructions.tip: Blooming saffron releases its colour and aroma more effectively than adding the dry threads directly.

instructions.title: Toast the pine nuts
instructions.instruction: Heat a dry frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the pine nuts and toast for 2–3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently until lightly golden. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Pine nuts burn quickly, so remove them as soon as they turn golden.

instructions.title: Brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a deep frying pan or casserole over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then brown on both sides for 3–4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Work in batches if needed to achieve a golden surface.

instructions.title: Cook the onions and spices
instructions.instruction: Add the onion to the same pan and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, and cumin and cook for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Keep the spices moving so they become fragrant without scorching.

instructions.title: Simmer the chicken
instructions.instruction: Return the chicken and any resting juices to the pan. Add the remaining stock, saffron infusion, and raisins. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 20–25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
instructions.tip: Turn the chicken once during cooking so it absorbs the sauce evenly.

instructions.title: Finish and garnish
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lemon juice and half the toasted pine nuts. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter the remaining pine nuts and parsley over the chicken and serve with rice, couscous, or flatbread.
instructions.tip: A small squeeze of extra lemon balances the sweetness of the raisins.

tips: Use boneless chicken thighs for a tender result, or bone-in thighs for deeper flavour and a longer cooking time.
Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes if they are particularly dry.
Serve with a simple cucumber salad to contrast with the rich, gently sweet sauce.

title: Lemongrass beef stew with noodles
description: A fragrant Southeast Asian-inspired beef stew featuring tender beef simmered with lemongrass, ginger, garlic, and warming spices, served over soft rice noodles in a savoury aromatic broth.

instructions.title: Prepare the beef
instructions.instruction: Pat the beef cubes dry and season with salt and black pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Brown the beef in batches to develop a deeper flavour.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the onion to the same pot and cook for 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and ground coriander and cook for another minute until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Bruise the lemongrass before cooking to release its aromatic oils.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Return the beef to the pot. Add the beef stock, fish sauce, soy sauce, star anise, and carrots. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat.
instructions.tip: Taste the broth later before adding extra salt because fish sauce is already salty.

instructions.title: Braise until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is fork-tender. Add a little water or stock if the liquid reduces too much.
instructions.tip: Keep the stew at a gentle simmer rather than a rapid boil.

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and divide among serving bowls.
instructions.tip: Rinse the noodles briefly with warm water if they begin sticking together.

instructions.title: Assemble and serve
instructions.instruction: Remove the star anise and any tough lemongrass pieces. Ladle the beef, vegetables, and hot broth over the noodles. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with lime wedges.
instructions.tip: Add lime juice just before eating to brighten the rich broth.

tips: Prepare the stew a day ahead for deeper flavour.
Trim excess fat from the beef while leaving enough marbling for tenderness.
Add sliced mushrooms or bok choy near the end for extra vegetables.

alternatives: Soy sauce with a little lime juice

title: Massaman Beef curry
description: A rich Thai curry combining tender beef, creamy coconut milk, potatoes, peanuts, and aromatic Massaman spices. The sauce balances gentle heat with sweet, savoury, and tangy flavours.

instructions.title: Brown the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches until well coloured on several sides, then set aside.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pot so the beef develops a good sear.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the Massaman curry paste and cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant.
instructions.tip: If the paste begins sticking, add a spoonful of the thick coconut cream from the top of the can.

instructions.title: Start the curry
instructions.instruction: Pour in the coconut milk and beef stock, stirring to dissolve the curry paste. Return the beef to the pot and add the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods.
instructions.tip: Use unsweetened full-fat coconut milk for a rich, smooth sauce.

instructions.title: Braise the beef
instructions.instruction: Cover partially and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, until the beef is becoming tender. Stir occasionally and add a little water if needed.
instructions.tip: The exact cooking time depends on the size of the beef cubes.

instructions.title: Add vegetables and seasonings
instructions.instruction: Add the potatoes and onion and simmer for another 20–25 minutes until tender. Stir in the peanuts, fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar. Taste and adjust the sweet, salty, and sour balance.
instructions.tip: Add the potatoes only after the beef has had time to soften so they do not break apart.

instructions.title: Serve with rice
instructions.instruction: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions. Remove the whole spices from the curry if desired, then serve the beef curry over rice with extra peanuts scattered on top.
instructions.tip: Let the curry stand for 5 minutes before serving to allow the sauce to settle.

tips: Massaman curry paste varies in heat and saltiness, so adjust the quantity to taste.
For a deeper flavour, prepare the curry a day in advance and reheat gently.
Add a splash of stock if the coconut sauce becomes too thick during simmering.

title: Pad See Ew
description: A popular Thai stir-fried noodle dish made with wide rice noodles, tender chicken, Chinese broccoli, egg, and a savoury soy-based sauce. High-heat cooking gives the noodles their characteristic caramelised flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles and sauce
instructions.instruction: Separate the fresh rice noodles gently. If they are firm, warm them briefly according to the package instructions. Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar, and white pepper in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Fresh noodles should be soft and pliable before stir-frying.

instructions.title: Sear the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until lightly browned and nearly cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Slice the chicken thinly across the grain for a tender texture.

instructions.title: Cook the garlic and greens
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the garlic for 20 seconds, then add the Chinese broccoli stems and cook for 1 minute. Add the leaves and cook until just wilted.
instructions.tip: Add thicker stems before the leaves so everything finishes cooking together.

instructions.title: Scramble the eggs
instructions.instruction: Push the vegetables to one side of the wok. Crack in the eggs and scramble briefly until softly set.
instructions.tip: Leave the eggs slightly soft because they will cook a little more when combined with the noodles.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the noodles
instructions.instruction: Add the noodles and chicken to the wok, pour over the sauce, and toss gently over high heat for 2–3 minutes. Allow the noodles to sit against the hot pan briefly between tosses to develop caramelised patches.
instructions.tip: Avoid excessive stirring, which can break the noodles.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodles between bowls and serve hot with lime wedges and extra white pepper if desired.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if your wok is small; a crowded wok tends to steam rather than sear.

tips: Use fresh wide rice noodles when possible for the classic soft, chewy texture.
Chinese broccoli can be replaced with regular broccoli or bok choy.
Have all ingredients prepared before heating the wok because cooking is very fast.

title: Panang chicken curry (kaeng panang gai)
description: A creamy Thai curry featuring tender chicken in a thick coconut sauce flavoured with Panang curry paste, kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, and a touch of sweetness. It is aromatic, rich, and delicious with steamed jasmine rice.

instructions.title: Prepare the curry base
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the Panang curry paste and cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring until fragrant.
instructions.tip: If the paste begins to stick, add a spoonful of coconut milk.

instructions.title: Add coconut milk
instructions.instruction: Pour in the coconut milk and stir until the curry paste is evenly dispersed. Bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Full-fat coconut milk produces a richer and more traditional texture.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the sliced chicken and simmer gently for 8–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through.
instructions.tip: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer to prevent it from splitting excessively.

instructions.title: Season the curry
instructions.instruction: Stir in the fish sauce, palm sugar, ground peanuts, and sliced red pepper. Simmer for another 3–4 minutes until the pepper is just tender and the sauce thickens.
instructions.tip: Taste before adding extra fish sauce because curry paste can already be salty.

instructions.title: Add lime leaves
instructions.instruction: Stir in the finely sliced kaffir lime leaves. Taste and balance the curry with a little more sugar or fish sauce if needed.
instructions.tip: Remove the central rib of each lime leaf before slicing it finely.

instructions.title: Serve with rice
instructions.instruction: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions. Serve the Panang chicken curry over the rice, garnished with Thai basil if desired.
instructions.tip: A small amount of finely sliced red chilli makes a colourful garnish.

tips: Panang curry is typically thicker and less soupy than Thai red curry.
Add extra curry paste gradually if you prefer a stronger flavour.
Serve with cucumber slices or a fresh herb salad to balance the richness.

title: Prawn stir-fry
description: A quick, colourful stir-fry of juicy prawns, crisp vegetables, garlic, and ginger tossed in a savoury soy and oyster sauce. It is ideal for a speedy weeknight dinner served over steamed rice or noodles.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, cornflour, and water in a small bowl until smooth.
instructions.tip: Mix the cornflour thoroughly to prevent lumps in the finished sauce.

instructions.title: Prepare the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry and season lightly with black pepper. Keep them refrigerated until ready to cook.
instructions.tip: Dry prawns develop a better texture in a hot wok.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a wok over high heat. Add the broccoli and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the bell pepper and cook for another 2 minutes.
instructions.tip: Add a tablespoon of water and cover briefly if the broccoli needs help softening.

instructions.title: Add aromatics and prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes, turning until they turn pink and opaque.
instructions.tip: Avoid cooking the prawns for too long, as they can become rubbery.

instructions.title: Finish the stir-fry
instructions.instruction: Pour the prepared sauce into the wok and toss everything together for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the prawns and vegetables. Stir in the sesame oil.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Serve immediately with steamed rice or noodles, spooning the glossy sauce over the top.
instructions.tip: Garnish with extra spring onions or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

tips: Prepare and arrange all ingredients before heating the wok.
Use seasonal vegetables such as snap peas, mushrooms, or bok choy.
For extra heat, add fresh chilli or chilli crisp at the end.

title: Red curry chicken kebabs
description: Juicy chicken pieces marinated in Thai red curry paste, coconut milk, lime, and garlic, then grilled on skewers until lightly charred. These flavourful kebabs are delicious with jasmine rice and a fresh cucumber salad.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
Red bell pepper, cut into chunks

instructions.title: Make the marinade
instructions.instruction: Mix the red curry paste, coconut milk, fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, and oil in a bowl until combined.
instructions.tip: Taste a little of the marinade before adding the chicken and adjust the lime or sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the chicken chunks and toss until well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
instructions.tip: Marinating longer helps the flavour penetrate the chicken.

instructions.title: Prepare the skewers
instructions.instruction: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 20–30 minutes. Thread the chicken, bell pepper, and onion onto the skewers, alternating the ingredients.
instructions.tip: Leave small gaps between pieces so heat can circulate and the chicken cooks evenly.

instructions.title: Heat the grill
instructions.instruction: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Lightly oil the grates to reduce sticking.
instructions.tip: Remove excess marinade from the surface of the chicken to reduce flare-ups.

instructions.title: Grill the kebabs
instructions.instruction: Grill the skewers for 12–16 minutes, turning every few minutes, until lightly charred and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 74°C.
instructions.tip: Cooking time depends on the size of the chicken pieces and the heat of the grill.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest the kebabs for 3 minutes, then sprinkle with fresh coriander and serve with rice, lime wedges, or cucumber salad.
instructions.tip: Serve with extra lime juice to balance the creamy, spicy marinade.

tips: Chicken thighs are more forgiving than breast meat on the grill.
Cook the kebabs under a hot oven grill if outdoor grilling is not possible.
Keep raw-chicken marinade separate from any sauce intended for serving.

alternatives: Plain yogurt for a different marinade texture

title: Spicy Thai prawn noodles
description: A vibrant Thai-inspired noodle dish featuring juicy prawns, rice noodles, fresh vegetables, chilli, lime, and a savoury-sweet sauce. Fresh herbs and lime juice bring brightness to the spicy stir-fry.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions until just tender. Drain well and set aside.
instructions.tip: Do not overcook the noodles because they will be stir-fried again.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Combine the soy sauce, fish sauce, sweet chilli sauce, and lime juice in a small bowl. Stir well and set aside.
instructions.tip: Adjust the sweet chilli sauce and lime to balance sweetness, saltiness, and acidity.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the prawns and cook for 1–2 minutes per side until pink and almost cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Remove the prawns promptly to keep them tender.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the garlic and chopped chilli to the wok and stir-fry for 20 seconds. Add the bell pepper, carrot, and spring onions and cook for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetables slightly crisp for a better contrast with the noodles.

instructions.title: Toss the noodles
instructions.instruction: Return the prawns to the wok, add the noodles and prepared sauce, and toss over high heat for 2–3 minutes until everything is heated through and coated.
instructions.tip: Add a tablespoon of water if the noodles seem dry or begin sticking.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodles among bowls and top with chopped coriander and roasted peanuts. Serve with extra lime wedges if desired.
instructions.tip: Add the peanuts just before serving so they stay crunchy.

tips: Use fresh lime juice for a brighter flavour than bottled juice.
Adjust the number of chillies to suit your heat preference.
Add bean sprouts or sliced cabbage for extra crunch.

title: Stir-fried chicken with chillies & basil
description: A classic Thai-style stir-fry of tender chicken, fresh chillies, garlic, and aromatic basil in a savoury sauce. Quick cooking preserves the fresh basil fragrance and gives the chicken a deliciously spicy finish.

ingredients.item: Boneless chicken thighs or breast, finely chopped

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and water in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Have the sauce ready before cooking because the stir-fry comes together quickly.

instructions.title: Prepare the chicken
instructions.instruction: Finely chop or mince the chicken into small pieces. Pat dry if necessary so it browns well in the wok.
instructions.tip: Small pieces cook quickly and absorb the sauce evenly.

instructions.title: Fry the garlic and chillies
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Add the garlic and chillies and stir-fry for 20–30 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the ingredients moving to avoid burning the garlic.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4–6 minutes, breaking up any clumps, until browned and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Do not overcrowd the wok; cook in batches if necessary.

instructions.title: Add the sauce and basil
instructions.instruction: Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until the chicken is evenly coated. Turn off the heat and fold in the basil leaves until just wilted.
instructions.tip: Adding the basil off the heat helps preserve its aroma.

instructions.title: Serve with rice
instructions.instruction: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions. Serve the chicken stir-fry over the rice, adding a fried egg on top if desired.
instructions.tip: Thai holy basil gives the most authentic flavour, but regular basil can be used if unavailable.

tips: For a traditional texture, chop the chicken finely instead of cutting it into large cubes.
Use fewer chillies for a milder dish or remove their seeds to reduce heat.
Serve with cucumber slices to add freshness alongside the spicy chicken.

title: Thai beef stir-fry
description: Thinly sliced beef stir-fried with colourful vegetables, garlic, ginger, and a tangy Thai-inspired sauce. Fresh lime, soy, fish sauce, and a hint of chilli create a balanced savoury and bright flavour.

instructions.title: Slice and season the beef
instructions.instruction: Slice the beef thinly across the grain. In a bowl, combine it with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and half the cornflour, mixing until lightly coated.
instructions.tip: Partially freezing the beef for 15–20 minutes makes thin slicing easier.

instructions.title: Mix the sauce
instructions.instruction: Combine the remaining soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, remaining cornflour, and 2 tablespoons of water in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Mix the cornflour thoroughly so the sauce thickens smoothly.

instructions.title: Sear the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef in batches for 1–2 minutes until browned but not overcooked. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: A hot wok and small batches help the beef brown quickly.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the wok. Stir-fry the broccoli and bell pepper for 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onions and cook for another 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water and cover briefly if you prefer softer broccoli.

instructions.title: Combine and glaze
instructions.instruction: Return the beef to the wok and pour in the sauce. Toss for 1–2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and vegetables.
instructions.tip: Add a little water if the sauce becomes too thick before everything is heated through.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Remove from the heat, stir in the coriander, and serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions.tip: Finish with extra lime juice or sliced chilli for a brighter, spicier dish.

tips: Choose a tender cut such as sirloin or flank steak and slice it across the grain.
Prepare all vegetables and sauce before turning on the heat.
For extra crunch, add cashews or toasted sesame seeds before serving.

title: Thai chicken cakes with sweet chilli sauce
description: Juicy Thai-inspired chicken cakes seasoned with red curry paste, garlic, spring onions, and fresh herbs, pan-fried until golden. Serve with sweet chilli sauce and crunchy cucumber for a flavourful starter or snack.

instructions.title: Mix the chicken mixture
instructions.instruction: In a large bowl, combine the chicken mince, red curry paste, egg, cornflour, spring onions, garlic, coriander, fish sauce, and lime zest. Mix until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Mix just until combined to keep the cakes tender.

instructions.title: Shape the cakes
instructions.instruction: With slightly damp hands, shape the mixture into 12 small, flat cakes of similar thickness. Place them on a plate.
instructions.tip: Making the cakes evenly sized helps them cook at the same rate.

instructions.title: Heat the pan
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Work in batches if necessary to leave space between the cakes.
instructions.tip: Avoid overheating the pan, as the outside can brown before the chicken is cooked through.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken cakes
instructions.instruction: Fry the cakes for 4–5 minutes on each side, adjusting the heat as needed, until golden and cooked through. The centre should reach 74°C.
instructions.tip: Turn the cakes carefully with a spatula so they hold their shape.

instructions.title: Prepare the dipping sauce
instructions.instruction: Pour the sweet chilli sauce into a small serving bowl. Add a squeeze of lime juice if you prefer a tangier dip.
instructions.tip: Serve the sauce separately to keep the cakes crisp.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Arrange the warm chicken cakes on a platter with cucumber slices and lime wedges. Serve with the sweet chilli sauce for dipping.
instructions.tip: Garnish with extra coriander for a fresh finish.

tips: Refrigerate the shaped cakes for 15 minutes if the mixture feels too soft.
Use a thermometer to confirm the chicken is fully cooked.
Serve as a starter or with rice and vegetables for a light main meal.

alternatives: Sriracha mixed with a little honey and lime juice

title: Thai coconut & veg broth
