description: A fragrant Thai-inspired broth with creamy coconut milk, mushrooms, carrots, peppers, and greens simmered with lemongrass, ginger, lime, and red curry paste. This warming, colourful soup can be enjoyed on its own or with rice noodles.

instructions.title: Prepare the aromatic base
instructions.instruction: Heat a small splash of the coconut milk in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the red curry paste and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Start with less curry paste if you prefer a mild broth.

instructions.title: Add aromatics and stock
instructions.instruction: Stir in the garlic and ginger, then add the vegetable stock and bruised lemongrass. Bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Bruise the lemongrass with the back of a knife to release its flavour.

instructions.title: Simmer the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the carrots and mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the red bell pepper and cook for another 3 minutes.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables into similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Add coconut milk
instructions.instruction: Pour in the remaining coconut milk and add the soy sauce and brown sugar. Simmer gently for 3–4 minutes without boiling vigorously.
instructions.tip: A gentle simmer helps keep the coconut broth smooth.

instructions.title: Finish with greens and lime
instructions.instruction: Add the spinach or bok choy and cook until just wilted. Remove the lemongrass and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
instructions.tip: Add lime juice near the end to preserve its fresh, bright flavour.

instructions.title: Serve the broth
instructions.instruction: If using rice noodles, prepare them separately according to the package instructions and divide among bowls. Ladle the hot coconut broth and vegetables over the noodles, then garnish with coriander.
instructions.tip: Keep the noodles separate until serving to prevent them from absorbing too much broth.

tips: For a more filling meal, add firm tofu, cooked chickpeas, or prawns.
Remove the lemongrass before serving because its stalk remains fibrous.
Adjust the lime juice and curry paste to balance acidity and heat.

alternatives: A mixture of chilli paste, garlic, and ginger

title: Thai curry noodle soup
description: A comforting Thai-inspired noodle soup featuring tender chicken, rice noodles, vegetables, and a fragrant coconut curry broth infused with lemongrass, ginger, lime, and red curry paste.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook or soak the rice noodles according to the package instructions until just tender. Drain, rinse briefly, and set aside.
instructions.tip: Keep the noodles separate until serving so they do not absorb too much broth.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic, ginger, and red curry paste. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Add a tablespoon of coconut milk if the paste begins sticking.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Pour in the chicken stock and coconut milk. Add the bruised lemongrass, fish sauce, and brown sugar. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Avoid boiling coconut milk vigorously, as the broth can separate.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the sliced chicken and simmer for 8–10 minutes until fully cooked. Add the bell pepper during the final 4 minutes.
instructions.tip: Slice the chicken evenly to ensure consistent cooking.

instructions.title: Finish the soup
instructions.instruction: Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted. Remove the lemongrass and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
instructions.tip: Add lime juice after reducing the heat to preserve its fresh flavour.

instructions.title: Assemble and serve
instructions.instruction: Divide the cooked noodles among four bowls. Ladle the hot chicken curry broth over them and garnish with fresh coriander.
instructions.tip: Serve with extra lime wedges and sliced chillies if desired.

tips: Use full-fat coconut milk for a richer broth.
Add mushrooms, bok choy, or bean sprouts for extra vegetables.
Store noodles and broth separately when preparing leftovers.

title: Thai drumsticks
description: Juicy chicken drumsticks marinated in Thai-inspired garlic, ginger, lemongrass, soy sauce, lime, and sweet chilli sauce, then roasted until golden and lightly caramelised.

instructions.title: Prepare the marinade
instructions.instruction: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, fish sauce, sweet chilli sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, oil, and white pepper in a bowl.
instructions.tip: Finely mince the tender inner part of the lemongrass for the best texture.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the drumsticks dry and coat thoroughly with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
instructions.tip: Marinating overnight gives the chicken a stronger aromatic flavour.

instructions.title: Preheat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Arrange the drumsticks on a lined baking tray or wire rack, leaving space between each piece.
instructions.tip: A wire rack allows hot air to circulate around the chicken.

instructions.title: Roast the drumsticks
instructions.instruction: Roast for 35–45 minutes, turning once halfway through, until the chicken is golden and reaches an internal temperature of at least 74°C.
instructions.tip: Cover loosely with foil if the glaze darkens before the chicken is cooked.

instructions.title: Caramelise the glaze
instructions.instruction: During the final 5 minutes, increase the oven temperature to 220°C if needed to lightly caramelise the exterior. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
instructions.tip: Discard marinade that has contacted raw chicken unless it is boiled thoroughly before reuse.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Rest the drumsticks for 5 minutes, then garnish with coriander and serve with jasmine rice, cucumber salad, and lime wedges.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of fresh lime balances the sweet and savoury glaze.

tips: For extra heat, add finely chopped bird's eye chilli to the marinade.
Cook the drumsticks in an air fryer at 190°C for approximately 25–30 minutes, checking for doneness.
Serve with a refreshing cucumber and mint salad.

alternatives: Honey mixed with chilli flakes and lime juice

title: Thai fried rice with prawns & peas
description: A quick Thai-style fried rice with juicy prawns, sweet peas, scrambled eggs, garlic, and fragrant jasmine rice, seasoned with fish sauce and lime.

instructions.title: Prepare the rice and sauce
instructions.instruction: Break up any clumps in the chilled rice. Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and white pepper in a small bowl.
instructions.tip: Use properly refrigerated cooked rice rather than rice left at room temperature.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat. Add the prawns and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until opaque. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Pat the prawns dry before cooking to prevent excess moisture.

instructions.title: Scramble the eggs
instructions.instruction: Add a little of the remaining oil to the wok. Crack in the eggs and scramble until just set. Transfer to the plate with the prawns.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking the eggs because they will return to the wok later.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil, onion, and garlic. Stir-fry for 1–2 minutes, then add the peas and cook until heated through.
instructions.tip: Keep the wok hot so the vegetables cook quickly.

instructions.title: Fry the rice
instructions.instruction: Add the chilled rice and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, breaking up clumps. Pour in the prepared sauce and toss until the rice is evenly seasoned.
instructions.tip: Allow the rice to contact the hot wok briefly between tosses for a lightly toasted flavour.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Return the prawns and eggs to the wok. Add the spring onions and toss for another minute. Serve with lime wedges and cucumber slices.
instructions.tip: Squeeze lime over the rice just before eating.

tips: Chilled jasmine rice produces better-separated grains than freshly cooked rice.
Keep the heat high and avoid overcrowding the wok.
Add sliced chillies or Thai chilli fish sauce for extra heat.

title: Thai green chicken soup
description: A fragrant Thai soup with tender chicken, green curry paste, creamy coconut milk, mushrooms, and fresh vegetables, finished with lime and Thai basil.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the green curry paste, garlic, and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Use less curry paste initially if you prefer a milder soup.

instructions.title: Make the broth
instructions.instruction: Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock. Add the makrut lime leaves, fish sauce, and palm sugar, then bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Avoid boiling the coconut broth aggressively.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the sliced chicken and simmer for 7–9 minutes until nearly cooked through.
instructions.tip: Slice the chicken thinly so it cooks quickly and remains tender.

instructions.title: Add the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the mushrooms and baby corn and simmer for 4 minutes. Stir in the bok choy and cook for another 2 minutes.
instructions.tip: Add leafy greens last to preserve their colour and texture.

instructions.title: Balance the flavours
instructions.instruction: Remove the lime leaves if desired. Stir in the lime juice and taste, adjusting with a little extra fish sauce or sugar if needed.
instructions.tip: A good Thai soup balances spicy, salty, sweet, and sour flavours.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Ladle the soup into bowls and scatter Thai basil over each serving. Serve hot, optionally with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions.tip: Add the basil just before serving to retain its aroma.

tips: Use homemade or good-quality green curry paste for the best aroma.
Add rice noodles for a more substantial meal.
Store leftover soup refrigerated and reheat gently.

title: Thai Green Curry
description: A classic Thai green curry featuring tender chicken, creamy coconut milk, Thai aubergines, bamboo shoots, and fragrant basil in a vibrant green chilli curry sauce.

instructions.title: Prepare the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Slice the chicken evenly, quarter the aubergines, drain the bamboo shoots, and prepare the herbs. Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions.
instructions.tip: Keep the cut aubergines in water until needed to reduce browning.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil and 3 tablespoons of thick coconut cream in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the green curry paste and fry for 2 minutes until aromatic.
instructions.tip: Stir continuously to prevent the curry paste from burning.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Add the chicken and stir until coated in the curry paste. Cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the remaining coconut milk and chicken stock.
instructions.tip: Do not cook the chicken completely before adding the liquid.

instructions.title: Add vegetables and aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the Thai aubergines, bamboo shoots, and makrut lime leaves. Simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the aubergines are tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate to maintain a smooth coconut sauce.

instructions.title: Season the curry
instructions.instruction: Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then add the sliced red chilli and Thai basil.
instructions.tip: Add the basil near the end to preserve its fragrance.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Remove from the heat and serve the curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions.tip: Garnish with extra basil and thinly sliced chilli if desired.

tips: Thai green curry paste varies in strength, so adjust the amount to taste.
Use full-fat coconut milk for a rich, creamy curry.
Traditional Thai aubergines can be replaced with small pieces of regular aubergine.

title: Thai pork & peanut curry
description: A rich Thai-inspired pork curry with tender pork shoulder simmered in coconut milk, red curry paste, roasted peanuts, and fragrant spices. The creamy peanut sauce pairs perfectly with jasmine rice.

instructions.title: Brown the pork
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium-high heat. Brown the pork cubes in batches for 5–6 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Use pork shoulder rather than lean pork for tender results after simmering.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, and curry paste and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of stock if the paste begins sticking.

instructions.title: Build the curry
instructions.instruction: Return the pork to the saucepan. Pour in the coconut milk and stock, stirring until the curry paste is evenly distributed.
instructions.tip: Keep the curry at a gentle simmer to prevent the coconut milk from separating excessively.

instructions.title: Simmer until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover partially and simmer for 60–75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pork is tender. Add extra water if the sauce reduces too quickly.
instructions.tip: The pork should be easily pierced with a fork before the final seasoning is added.

instructions.title: Add peanuts and seasoning
instructions.instruction: Finely chop half the peanuts and stir them into the curry with the fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
instructions.tip: Taste and balance the sweet, salty, and sour flavours.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions. Serve the pork curry over rice, topped with the remaining peanuts and fresh coriander.
instructions.tip: Add the final peanut garnish immediately before serving for crunch.

tips: Pork shoulder becomes tender when simmered slowly.
For a smoother sauce, blend part of the peanuts before adding them.
Reheat leftovers gently with a splash of water or stock.

alternatives: Sunflower seed butter for a nut-free variation
Rice vinegar with a pinch of sugar

title: Thai prawn curry
description: A quick and aromatic Thai red curry with juicy prawns, creamy coconut milk, vegetables, lime leaves, and fresh basil. It is rich, lightly spicy, and perfect with steamed jasmine rice.

instructions.title: Prepare the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry and refrigerate them while preparing the remaining ingredients. Slice the vegetables evenly.
instructions.tip: Fully thaw frozen prawns before cooking.

instructions.title: Fry the curry paste
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and red curry paste and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Stir continuously so the curry paste does not burn.

instructions.title: Prepare the coconut sauce
instructions.instruction: Pour in the coconut milk and add the lime leaves, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Stir until combined and bring to a gentle simmer.
instructions.tip: Use full-fat coconut milk for a creamier sauce.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the bell pepper, courgette, and baby corn. Simmer for 6–8 minutes until the vegetables are almost tender.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetables slightly crisp to contrast with the soft prawns.

instructions.title: Add the prawns
instructions.instruction: Add the prawns and simmer for 3–5 minutes until pink, opaque, and cooked through. Stir in the lime juice and Thai basil.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking the prawns, as they become rubbery.

instructions.title: Serve with rice
instructions.instruction: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package instructions. Remove the lime leaves if desired and serve the curry over the rice.
instructions.tip: Garnish with sliced red chilli or extra basil for freshness.

tips: Add the prawns only near the end of cooking.
Adjust the curry paste to suit your preferred spice level.
Use fresh Thai basil for a more aromatic finish.

title: Adana kebab
description: A traditional Turkish kebab made with seasoned minced lamb, red pepper, and chilli, shaped onto skewers and grilled until smoky and juicy. Serve with flatbread, grilled vegetables, and fresh parsley.

ingredients.item: Red bell pepper, very finely chopped

instructions.title: Prepare the meat mixture
instructions.instruction: Combine the minced lamb, finely chopped red pepper, pul biber, cumin, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Knead thoroughly for 4–5 minutes until the mixture becomes sticky and cohesive.
instructions.tip: Squeeze excess moisture from the chopped pepper before adding it.

instructions.title: Chill the mixture
instructions.instruction: Cover and refrigerate the seasoned lamb for at least 30 minutes to help it firm up and hold together on the skewers.
instructions.tip: Keep the mixture cold until shaping.

instructions.title: Shape the kebabs
instructions.instruction: Divide the lamb mixture into 8 portions. With damp hands, press each portion firmly around a wide, flat metal skewer, forming a long, evenly thick kebab.
instructions.tip: Flat skewers help prevent the kebabs from rotating during grilling.

instructions.title: Prepare the grill
instructions.instruction: Preheat a charcoal grill or barbecue to medium-high heat. Arrange the tomatoes and green peppers nearby for grilling.
instructions.tip: Charcoal gives the kebabs a traditional smoky flavour.

instructions.title: Grill the kebabs
instructions.instruction: Grill for approximately 8–12 minutes, turning carefully, until browned and fully cooked. The minced lamb should reach an internal temperature of 71°C. Grill the tomatoes and peppers until lightly charred.
instructions.tip: Avoid pressing the kebabs during cooking, which can squeeze out their juices.

instructions.title: Serve traditionally
instructions.instruction: Warm the flatbreads briefly on the grill. Serve the kebabs with flatbread, sliced red onion, parsley, grilled tomatoes, peppers, and lemon wedges.
instructions.tip: A sprinkle of sumac over the onions adds a traditional tangy flavour.

tips: Use lamb with sufficient fat to keep the kebabs juicy.
Kneading the mince helps the mixture adhere to the skewers.
Serve with sumac onions, flatbread, and grilled vegetables.

alternatives: A mixture of lamb and beef

title: Aubergine & hummus grills
description: Smoky grilled aubergine slices topped with creamy hummus, lemon, parsley, and toasted pine nuts. This Mediterranean-inspired dish is ideal as a vegetarian appetiser, light lunch, or part of a mezze platter.

instructions.title: Prepare the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Slice the aubergines lengthwise into approximately 1 cm thick slices. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
instructions.tip: Choose firm aubergines with smooth skin for the best texture.

instructions.title: Season the slices
instructions.instruction: Mix the olive oil, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Brush the mixture over both sides of the aubergine slices.
instructions.tip: Brush rather than soak the slices with oil, as aubergines absorb oil readily.

instructions.title: Grill the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Heat a grill pan or barbecue over medium-high heat. Grill the aubergine slices for 4–5 minutes per side until tender with visible grill marks.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches to avoid overcrowding and ensure the centres become soft.

instructions.title: Toast the pine nuts
instructions.instruction: Place the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat and toast for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden, shaking the pan frequently.
instructions.tip: Watch closely because pine nuts can burn quickly.

instructions.title: Assemble the grills
instructions.instruction: Arrange the grilled aubergine slices on a serving platter. Spoon hummus over each slice and scatter with cherry tomatoes and chopped parsley.
instructions.tip: Warm the hummus slightly if you prefer a fully warm dish.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Drizzle with lemon juice, scatter over the toasted pine nuts, and serve with warm pita bread.
instructions.tip: Add a little extra olive oil or a pinch of sumac for a finishing touch.

tips: Grill the aubergines until fully tender rather than leaving them firm in the centre.
Use homemade hummus for a fresher flavour.
Serve alongside tabbouleh, olives, or a cucumber salad for a complete mezze meal.

title: Baklava with spiced nuts, ricotta & chocolate
description: A rich dessert combining crisp, buttery layers of filo pastry with cinnamon-spiced nuts, creamy ricotta, dark chocolate, and fragrant honey syrup. It brings a decadent twist to traditional baklava flavours.

instructions.title: Prepare the syrup
instructions.instruction: Combine the sugar, water, honey, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 5–7 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla, and allow to cool.
instructions.tip: Prepare the syrup first so it has time to cool before being poured over the hot pastry.

instructions.title: Mix the nut filling
instructions.instruction: Combine the chopped walnuts, pistachios, almonds, cinnamon, and cardamom in a bowl. Divide the mixture into two portions.
instructions.tip: Keep the nuts in small pieces rather than grinding them into a paste.

instructions.title: Prepare the filo layers
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Brush a baking dish with melted butter. Layer half the filo sheets in the dish, brushing each sheet lightly with butter as you work.
instructions.tip: Keep unused filo covered with a slightly damp towel to prevent it drying out.

instructions.title: Add ricotta, nuts, and chocolate
instructions.instruction: Spread the ricotta evenly over the pastry base, leaving a small border around the edges. Scatter over the first portion of nuts and half the chopped chocolate. Add the remaining nut mixture and chocolate, then cover with the remaining filo sheets, brushing each with butter.
instructions.tip: Drain very wet ricotta before spreading it to prevent a soggy centre.

instructions.title: Cut and bake
instructions.instruction: Using a sharp knife, cut the layered pastry into diamonds or squares before baking. Bake for 35–45 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
instructions.tip: Cutting the pastry before baking makes it easier to portion once crisp.

instructions.title: Add syrup and cool
instructions.instruction: Remove the baklava from the oven and immediately pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot pastry. Leave to rest for at least 3 hours before serving so the syrup can soak in.
instructions.tip: Pour the syrup slowly around the cuts to help it reach the lower layers.

tips: Use a sharp knife to cut through the filo without compressing the layers.
Allow the dessert to cool fully before storing so the pastry retains its structure.
Serve small portions because the combination of nuts, chocolate, butter, and syrup is rich.

title: Chicken wings with cumin, lemon & garlic
description: Oven-roasted chicken wings coated in a fragrant marinade of cumin, garlic, lemon, and olive oil. The wings develop crisp golden skin and a tangy, savoury flavour, making them ideal for sharing.

instructions.title: Prepare the marinade
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, cumin, coriander, paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
instructions.tip: Freshly ground cumin gives the wings a stronger aroma.

instructions.title: Marinate the wings
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken wings dry, add them to the marinade, and toss until evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 8 hours.
instructions.tip: For crispier skin, pat the wings dry before coating and avoid using an excessive amount of marinade.

instructions.title: Preheat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Line a baking tray with foil and place a wire rack on top if available.
instructions.tip: A wire rack allows hot air to circulate around the wings.

instructions.title: Roast the wings
instructions.instruction: Arrange the wings in a single layer and roast for 35–45 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden, crisp, and fully cooked.
instructions.tip: Leave space between the wings so they brown rather than steam.

instructions.title: Check and finish
instructions.instruction: Check that the thickest parts of the wings reach at least 74°C internally. If needed, roast for a few more minutes until crisp.
instructions.tip: Watch the garlic carefully near the end because it can brown quickly.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the wings to a serving platter, sprinkle with fresh parsley, and serve with lemon wedges and a yoghurt dip if desired.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately while the skin is at its crispest.

tips: Marinate the wings overnight for a deeper flavour.
For extra crispiness, refrigerate the uncovered, seasoned wings for a few hours before roasting.
Serve with chopped cucumber, lemon wedges, and a simple yoghurt sauce.

title: Chilli ginger lamb chops
description: Tender lamb chops marinated in fresh ginger, garlic, chilli, soy, and lemon, then seared or grilled until browned on the outside and juicy inside. The spicy, aromatic marinade complements the rich flavour of lamb.

instructions.title: Mix the marinade
instructions.instruction: Combine the ginger, garlic, chilli, cumin, coriander, soy sauce, lemon juice, olive oil, honey, and black pepper in a bowl.
instructions.tip: Adjust the chilli according to your preferred heat level.

instructions.title: Marinate the lamb
instructions.instruction: Coat the lamb chops evenly in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 4 hours.
instructions.tip: Avoid leaving the chops in the acidic marinade overnight, as the surface texture can deteriorate.

instructions.title: Prepare the grill or pan
instructions.instruction: Remove the chops from the refrigerator about 15 minutes before cooking. Preheat a grill or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat and lightly oil the cooking surface.
instructions.tip: Let excess marinade drip off before searing to help the chops brown.

instructions.title: Sear the chops
instructions.instruction: Cook the chops for approximately 3–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. Avoid moving them too often so a good crust forms.
instructions.tip: Cooking time varies with the thickness of the chops and whether they are loin or rib chops.

instructions.title: Check doneness and rest
instructions.instruction: Check the internal temperature with a food thermometer. For whole cuts of lamb, aim for at least 63°C followed by a 3-minute rest, or cook longer according to preference and local food-safety guidance.
instructions.tip: Resting allows the juices to redistribute and keeps the meat succulent.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the chops to a warm plate, sprinkle with fresh coriander, and serve with flatbread, grilled vegetables, or a crisp salad.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of fresh lemon just before serving brightens the spicy marinade.

tips: Bring the chops close to room temperature before cooking for more even results.
Use a meat thermometer rather than relying on colour alone.
Serve with mint yoghurt or a cucumber salad to balance the chilli.

title: Griddled aubergines with sesame dressing
description: Smoky griddled aubergine slices topped with a nutty sesame dressing, soy, garlic, and fresh herbs. This simple dish draws on Mediterranean and East Asian flavours and works well as a side or light vegetarian meal.

instructions.title: Slice the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Cut the aubergines lengthwise into slices approximately 1 cm thick. Pat dry and season lightly with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Even slices cook at the same rate and are easier to turn on the griddle.

instructions.title: Make the sesame dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, and honey. Add warm water gradually until the dressing becomes smooth and pourable.
instructions.tip: Tahini thickens when first mixed with liquid; continue whisking and add water gradually.

instructions.title: Heat the griddle
instructions.instruction: Heat a griddle pan over medium-high heat. Brush the aubergine slices lightly with olive oil on both sides.
instructions.tip: Use a lightly oiled pan rather than pouring oil directly onto it.

instructions.title: Griddle the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Cook the slices in batches for 4–6 minutes per side until tender, browned, and marked with grill lines. Reduce the heat if the surface darkens before the centre softens.
instructions.tip: Aubergine should be fully tender rather than spongy in the centre.

instructions.title: Dress the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Arrange the cooked slices on a serving platter. Drizzle the sesame dressing evenly over them.
instructions.tip: Dress the aubergines while warm so they absorb some of the flavour.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter the sesame seeds, spring onions, and coriander over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
instructions.tip: Add a little chilli oil if you enjoy a spicy finish.

tips: For a smoky flavour, cook the aubergines on an outdoor barbecue.
Thin the dressing with a little extra water if it becomes too thick.
Serve alongside rice, grilled tofu, or roasted chickpeas for a more filling meal.

title: Grilled aubergines with spicy chickpeas & walnut sauce
description: Tender grilled aubergine halves topped with smoky, spicy chickpeas and a rich walnut sauce flavoured with garlic, lemon, and herbs. This hearty vegetarian dish combines Mediterranean ingredients with bold textures and flavours.

instructions.title: Prepare the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Halve the aubergines lengthwise and score the cut surfaces in a crosshatch pattern without cutting through the skin. Brush with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
instructions.tip: Scoring helps the aubergine cook evenly and allows the seasonings to penetrate.

instructions.title: Grill until tender
instructions.instruction: Heat a grill pan or barbecue to medium-high heat. Grill the aubergine halves cut-side down for 5–7 minutes, then turn and cook for another 8–12 minutes until soft throughout.
instructions.tip: If the outside browns too quickly, move the aubergines to a cooler part of the grill.

instructions.title: Season the chickpeas
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a frying pan. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, ground coriander, and chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds. Add the chickpeas and toss for 4–5 minutes until heated through and lightly crisp.
instructions.tip: Dry the chickpeas before frying to improve browning.

instructions.title: Prepare the walnut sauce
instructions.instruction: Place the walnuts, lemon juice, remaining olive oil, a pinch of salt, and 3 tablespoons of water in a food processor. Blend into a coarse sauce, adding more water until spoonable.
instructions.tip: Keep a little walnut texture rather than blending completely smooth for a rustic finish.

instructions.title: Assemble the dish
instructions.instruction: Place the grilled aubergines on a serving platter. Spoon the spicy chickpeas over the top and drizzle generously with the walnut sauce.
instructions.tip: Let the aubergines rest for a few minutes before assembling so the toppings remain in place.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter over the chopped parsley and optional pomegranate seeds. Serve warm with flatbread or a fresh green salad.
instructions.tip: A final squeeze of lemon brightens the rich walnut sauce.

tips: Roast the aubergines in a 220°C oven if a barbecue or griddle is unavailable.
Add a spoonful of harissa to the chickpeas for a deeper spicy flavour.
The walnut sauce can be prepared a day ahead and refrigerated.

title: Hot cumin lamb wrap with crunchy slaw & spicy mayo
description: Warm flatbreads filled with cumin-spiced lamb, crisp cabbage and carrot slaw, and creamy chilli mayonnaise. Fresh lime and coriander balance the rich, savoury meat in this flavour-packed wrap.

instructions.title: Season the lamb
instructions.instruction: Combine the lamb mince with cumin, coriander, paprika, garlic, salt, and black pepper. Mix until the spices are evenly distributed.
instructions.tip: Allow the seasoned lamb to rest for 10 minutes while preparing the slaw.

instructions.title: Make the crunchy slaw
instructions.instruction: Combine the shredded cabbage, grated carrot, red onion, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Toss well and set aside.
instructions.tip: Massage the cabbage gently with the lemon juice to soften it slightly while keeping its crunch.

instructions.title: Prepare the spicy mayo
instructions.instruction: Mix the mayonnaise, sriracha, and plain yogurt in a small bowl until smooth. Taste and add more chilli sauce if desired.
instructions.tip: The yogurt lightens the mayonnaise and adds a slight tang.

instructions.title: Cook the lamb
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the lamb and cook for 7–9 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and fully cooked.
instructions.tip: Let the lamb brown before stirring frequently to develop more flavour.

instructions.title: Warm the wraps
instructions.instruction: Warm the flatbreads in a dry frying pan for 20–30 seconds per side or according to the package instructions.
instructions.tip: Keep the warmed wraps covered with a clean towel so they remain flexible.

instructions.title: Fill and serve
instructions.instruction: Spread spicy mayo over each wrap. Add the hot lamb, crunchy slaw, and fresh coriander. Fold in the sides, roll tightly, and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill the wraps, or they will be difficult to roll.

tips: Use lean lamb mince if you prefer a less rich filling.
Add sliced pickled chillies or cucumbers for extra tang and crunch.
Wrap tightly in parchment paper for easier serving on the go.

title: Imam bayildi with BBQ lamb & tzatziki
description: A creative Turkish-inspired dish combining tender aubergines stuffed with slow-cooked onion and tomato, smoky barbecued lamb, and cool cucumber-yogurt tzatziki. The sweet, savoury aubergine contrasts beautifully with the grilled meat and refreshing sauce.

ingredients.item: Lamb shoulder, cut into small cubes

instructions.title: Prepare the lamb
instructions.instruction: Toss the lamb cubes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, cumin, paprika, half the garlic, salt, and black pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.tip: Cut the lamb into evenly sized pieces for more consistent grilling.

instructions.title: Prepare the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve the aubergines lengthwise and score the flesh in a crosshatch pattern. Brush with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and roast cut-side up for 25–30 minutes until beginning to soften.
instructions.tip: Keep the skin intact so the aubergine halves hold their shape when stuffed.

instructions.title: Make the tomato and onion filling
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a frying pan. Add the sliced onions and cook over low-medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Add the remaining garlic and tomatoes and simmer for 8–10 minutes until thick. Stir in the honey and half the parsley.
instructions.tip: Cook the onions slowly to bring out their natural sweetness.

instructions.title: Fill and finish the aubergines
instructions.instruction: Press the softened aubergine flesh down gently to create space, then spoon the tomato and onion mixture over each half. Return to the oven for 10–15 minutes until fully tender.
instructions.tip: Avoid scraping out all the flesh; leaving it in place keeps the aubergine moist.

instructions.title: Grill the lamb and make tzatziki
instructions.instruction: Thread the lamb onto skewers or place it in a grill basket. Grill over medium-high heat, turning regularly, until browned and cooked to your preferred safe doneness. Meanwhile, mix the Greek yogurt, squeezed cucumber, mint, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt to make tzatziki.
instructions.tip: If the lamb cubes are large, finish them in a covered ovenproof dish until tender.

instructions.title: Plate and serve
instructions.instruction: Place a stuffed aubergine half on each plate, add the grilled lamb, and serve with a generous spoonful of tzatziki. Finish with the remaining parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
instructions.tip: Serve with warm flatbread or bulgur wheat to soak up the juices.

tips: For a quicker version, use thin lamb steaks and slice them after grilling.
Drain the grated cucumber well to keep the tzatziki thick.
Prepare the stuffed aubergines ahead and grill the lamb just before serving.

title: Lamb & apricot meatballs
description: Juicy lamb meatballs flavoured with cumin, coriander, garlic, and fresh herbs, simmered in a gently spiced tomato sauce with sweet dried apricots. Serve with couscous or rice for a comforting North African-inspired meal.

instructions.title: Make the meatball mixture
instructions.instruction: In a large bowl, combine the lamb mince, half the onion, half the garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, cumin, ground coriander, half the cinnamon, half the paprika, salt, pepper, and half the coriander. Mix gently until combined.
instructions.tip: Avoid overmixing, which can make the meatballs dense.

instructions.title: Shape the meatballs
instructions.instruction: Roll the mixture into approximately 16 evenly sized meatballs. Place them on a plate and refrigerate for 10–15 minutes to help them hold their shape.
instructions.tip: Dampen your hands slightly to prevent the mixture sticking.

instructions.title: Brown the meatballs
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for 5–6 minutes, turning carefully. Transfer to a plate; they do not need to be fully cooked yet.
instructions.tip: Leave space between the meatballs so they brown instead of steam.

instructions.title: Prepare the apricot tomato sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining olive oil to the pan. Cook the remaining onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, remaining cinnamon, and paprika. Stir in the chopped tomatoes, stock, and chopped apricots.
instructions.tip: Scrape up the browned bits from the pan to add depth to the sauce.

instructions.title: Simmer the meatballs
instructions.instruction: Return the meatballs and their juices to the pan. Simmer gently, partially covered, for 15–20 minutes until cooked through and the sauce thickens. Check that the centres reach at least 71°C.
instructions.tip: Stir gently to keep the meatballs intact.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in the remaining coriander and parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot with couscous, rice, or flatbread.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lemon juice balances the sweetness of the apricots.

tips: For a more complex flavour, add a pinch of ground ginger or chilli flakes.
The sauce can be made a day ahead and reheated with freshly cooked meatballs.
Serve with toasted almonds or extra chopped herbs for added texture.

title: Bubble & Squeak
description: A traditional British dish made from mashed potatoes and cooked cabbage, mixed together and fried until golden and crisp. This comforting way to use leftover vegetables works beautifully as a breakfast, brunch, or savoury side dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Ensure the cooked potatoes are mashed and the cabbage is finely chopped. If the cabbage is wet, squeeze out excess moisture before mixing.
instructions.tip: Cold leftover potatoes work particularly well because they hold their shape.

instructions.title: Soften the onion
instructions.instruction: Melt half the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened but not deeply browned.
instructions.tip: Allow the onion to cool slightly before mixing it with the potatoes.

instructions.title: Mix the ingredients
instructions.instruction: Combine the mashed potatoes, cabbage, softened onion, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Mix until evenly distributed without making the mixture overly smooth.
instructions.tip: Keep some texture in the potatoes for a more rustic result.

instructions.title: Shape the mixture
instructions.instruction: Form the mixture into 8 small patties or leave it as one large cake, depending on the size of your frying pan.
instructions.tip: If the mixture feels too soft, chill it for 15 minutes before frying.

instructions.title: Fry until crisp
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil and remaining butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the patties and fry for 4–5 minutes per side until deeply golden and crisp. Cook in batches if needed.
instructions.tip: Let the patties form a crust before turning them to prevent breaking.

instructions.title: Serve hot
instructions.instruction: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve immediately. Add fried or poached eggs, baked beans, or grilled tomatoes if desired.
instructions.tip: For one large cake, press the mixture into the pan and carefully turn it using a large plate.

tips: Bubble & Squeak is ideal for using leftover roast potatoes and cooked cabbage.
Add cooked carrots, Brussels sprouts, peas, or leeks if you have them available.
Avoid overcrowding the pan so the patties become crisp rather than soggy.

alternatives: A mixture of potatoes and parsnips

title: Apple & Blackberry Crumble
description: A comforting British fruit dessert made with tender apples, juicy blackberries, and a golden buttery crumble topping. Serve warm with custard, vanilla ice cream, or cream.

instructions.title: Prepare the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Lightly butter a medium baking dish.
instructions.tip: A shallow baking dish helps the crumble topping brown evenly.

instructions.title: Prepare the fruit
instructions.instruction: Toss the sliced apples and blackberries with the granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice. Spread the fruit evenly in the baking dish.
instructions.tip: Taste the fruit mixture and adjust the sugar depending on the sweetness of the apples.

instructions.title: Make the crumble
instructions.instruction: Combine the flour and brown sugar in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs, then stir in the oats.
instructions.tip: Keep some larger crumbs for a varied, crunchy topping.

instructions.title: Assemble the crumble
instructions.instruction: Scatter the crumble mixture evenly over the fruit without pressing it down.
instructions.tip: Leaving the topping loose helps it become crisp.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the topping is golden brown and the fruit is bubbling around the edges.
instructions.tip: Cover loosely with foil if the topping browns too quickly.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Allow the crumble to rest for 10 minutes before serving warm with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream.
instructions.tip: Resting lets the fruit juices thicken slightly.

tips: Use a mixture of tart and sweet apples for balanced flavour.
Frozen blackberries can be used without thawing; add a few extra minutes of baking if needed.
Store leftovers covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheat in the oven to restore crispness.

title: Apple Frangipan Tart
description: A classic British-style tart with crisp pastry, a rich almond frangipane filling, and neatly arranged apple slices. It makes an elegant dessert served warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.item: Apples, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced

instructions.title: Prepare the pastry case
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Roll out the pastry and line a 23 cm tart tin. Trim the edges, prick the base with a fork, and chill for 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Chilling helps prevent the pastry from shrinking during baking.

instructions.title: Blind-bake the pastry
instructions.instruction: Line the pastry with baking paper and baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the beans and paper, then bake for another 5 minutes until the base looks dry.
instructions.tip: A partially baked base helps prevent a soggy tart.

instructions.title: Make the frangipane
instructions.instruction: Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the ground almonds, flour, and vanilla extract.
instructions.tip: If the mixture looks slightly curdled after adding the eggs, fold in the dry ingredients as directed.

instructions.title: Arrange the apples
instructions.instruction: Spread the frangipane evenly in the pastry case. Toss the apple slices with lemon juice, then arrange them in overlapping rows or a spiral over the filling.
instructions.tip: Slice the apples evenly so they soften at the same rate.

instructions.title: Bake the tart
instructions.instruction: Bake for 30–40 minutes, until the frangipane is set, golden, and slightly springy in the centre.
instructions.tip: If the apples brown too quickly, cover the tart loosely with foil.

instructions.title: Glaze and cool
instructions.instruction: Warm the apricot jam with a teaspoon of water and brush it over the hot apples. Cool the tart before slicing.
instructions.tip: Strain the jam if you want a particularly smooth glaze.

tips: Use firm apples that hold their shape when baked.
Allow the tart to cool before cutting so the filling sets cleanly.
Serve with lightly whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

title: Baked salmon with fennel & tomatoes
description: A light Mediterranean-inspired meal of salmon fillets baked with sweet cherry tomatoes, aromatic fennel, lemon, and herbs. The vegetables soften into a fragrant, juicy accompaniment for the fish.

instructions.title: Heat the oven
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lightly oil a large baking dish.
instructions.tip: Choose a dish that allows the vegetables to spread in a single layer.

instructions.title: Season the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Combine the fennel, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and garlic with the olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread them in the baking dish.
instructions.tip: Slice the fennel thinly so it becomes tender while the salmon cooks.

instructions.title: Start baking the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Bake the vegetables for 12–15 minutes, until the fennel begins to soften and the tomatoes start releasing their juices.
instructions.tip: This short head start helps the vegetables finish at the same time as the fish.

instructions.title: Add the salmon
instructions.instruction: Place the salmon fillets on top of the vegetables. Arrange lemon slices around the fish and spoon some of the tomato juices over each fillet.
instructions.tip: Keep the salmon skin-side down if the fillets have skin.

instructions.title: Bake until cooked
instructions.instruction: Return the dish to the oven for 12–15 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fillets, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches a safe internal temperature of 63°C.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking; check the thickest part of the fish first.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter the chopped parsley over the dish and serve the salmon with the roasted fennel, tomatoes, and pan juices.
instructions.tip: Crusty bread, couscous, or boiled potatoes make useful accompaniments.

tips: Pat the salmon dry before baking for a better texture.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes if you prefer a little heat.
Leftovers can be refrigerated promptly and used within 2 days.

title: Beed and Mustard Pie
description: A rich British-style beef pie with tender chunks of beef slowly cooked in a savoury gravy flavoured with English mustard, onions, and thyme, then baked beneath a crisp golden pastry lid.

ingredients.item: Beef chuck, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions.title: Brown the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat. Season the beef and brown it in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan so the beef browns instead of steams.

instructions.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and carrots to the pan and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: The flour helps thicken the gravy as it simmers.

instructions.title: Make the mustard gravy
instructions.instruction: Gradually stir in the beef stock, scraping the base of the pan. Add the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme, then return the beef and its juices to the pan.
instructions.tip: Start with less mustard if you prefer a milder flavour.

instructions.title: Slow-cook the filling
instructions.instruction: Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until the beef is tender. Remove the lid for the last few minutes if the gravy needs thickening, then cool the filling completely.
instructions.tip: The filling should be thick rather than watery before it goes into the pastry.

instructions.title: Assemble the pie
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the cooled filling into a pie dish. Cover with puff pastry, trim the edges, press to seal, and cut a small steam vent in the centre. Brush with beaten egg.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry cold until you are ready to top the pie.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Bake for 25–35 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and deep golden brown. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
instructions.tip: Serve with peas, carrots, or buttery mashed potatoes.

tips: Use a braising cut such as chuck or blade for tender results.
Make the filling a day ahead to deepen the flavour and simplify assembly.
Allow the pie to rest before cutting so the gravy settles.

title: Beef and Oyster pie
description: A traditional British savoury pie combining slow-braised beef with oysters in a deeply flavoured gravy, enclosed in crisp pastry. The oysters add a distinctive savoury, briny note to the rich filling.

ingredients.item: Fresh shucked oysters, with liquor reserved

instructions.title: Brown the beef
instructions.instruction: Melt the butter in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat. Season and brown the beef in batches, then set aside.
instructions.tip: Browning in batches develops a deeper flavour in the finished gravy.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and celery to the casserole and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
instructions.tip: Stir continuously after adding the flour to prevent it catching.

instructions.title: Braise the beef
instructions.instruction: Pour in the wine and scrape up any browned bits. Add the beef stock, thyme, bay leaf, and beef. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
instructions.tip: Add a little extra stock if the liquid reduces too much during cooking.

instructions.title: Add the oysters
instructions.instruction: Remove the thyme stems and bay leaf. Stir in the oysters and a little strained oyster liquor, then simmer gently for 2–3 minutes. Cool the filling before assembling the pie.
instructions.tip: Do not cook the oysters for too long at this stage, as they will cook further in the oven.

instructions.title: Top the pie
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the cooled filling into a pie dish, cover with shortcrust pastry, seal the edges, and cut a steam vent. Brush the pastry with beaten egg.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry chilled until you are ready to cover the filling.

instructions.title: Bake and serve
instructions.instruction: Bake for 30–35 minutes until the pastry is golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with steamed greens or mashed potatoes.
instructions.tip: Use fresh oysters from a reliable food supplier and keep them refrigerated until needed.

tips: Strain the oyster liquor to remove any grit before using it.
Keep the filling fairly thick so the pastry base does not become soggy.
For food safety, cook the beef until tender and ensure the pie is piping hot throughout before serving.

alternatives: Omit the shellfish and add extra mushrooms
Additional beef stock with 1 tsp lemon juice

title: Beef Dumpling Stew
description: A warming British beef stew with tender chunks of beef, root vegetables, and soft, fluffy herb dumplings cooked directly in a rich savoury broth. It is a complete comfort-food meal in one pot.

ingredients.amount: 2 tbsp for coating, plus 150 g for dumplings

instructions.title: Prepare and brown the beef
instructions.instruction: Toss the beef cubes with 2 tablespoons of flour, salt, and pepper. Heat a little oil in a large heavy pot and brown the beef in batches.
instructions.tip: Do not overcrowd the pot; good browning adds flavour to the stew.

instructions.title: Start the stew
instructions.instruction: Add the onion and celery to the pot and cook for 4–5 minutes. Stir in the tomato purée, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaf.
instructions.tip: Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen the browned bits.

instructions.title: Simmer until tender
instructions.instruction: Return the beef and its juices to the pot. Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour 30 minutes, then add the carrots and potatoes and cook for another 25–30 minutes.
instructions.tip: The beef should be tender before the dumplings are added.

instructions.title: Make the dumpling dough
instructions.instruction: Mix the 150 g flour with the baking powder, a pinch of salt, and the parsley. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then add enough cold water or milk to form a soft dough.
instructions.tip: Handle the dough gently and avoid kneading it, which can make dumplings tough.

instructions.title: Cook the dumplings
instructions.instruction: Divide the dough into 8 equal balls. Place them on top of the simmering stew, leaving space between them. Cover and cook gently for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
instructions.tip: Keeping the lid closed traps steam and helps the dumplings rise.

instructions.title: Season and serve
instructions.instruction: Check that the dumplings are cooked through and the vegetables are tender. Remove the bay leaf, adjust the seasoning, and serve in deep bowls.
instructions.tip: If the stew is too thin, remove the dumplings briefly and simmer the liquid uncovered before serving.

tips: Use beef chuck or blade for the best texture after slow cooking.
Keep the stew at a gentle simmer rather than a rapid boil.
Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly and add a splash of stock if needed.

title: Beef Sunday Roast
description: A traditional British Sunday roast featuring a seasoned joint of beef, roasted until browned outside and tender within. Serve with crispy roast potatoes, seasonal vegetables, Yorkshire pudding, and rich gravy.

ingredients.item: Beef roasting joint, such as topside or sirloin

instructions.title: Bring the beef to temperature
instructions.instruction: Remove the beef from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before cooking. Pat it dry and preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
instructions.tip: Drying the surface helps the beef brown properly.

instructions.title: Season the joint
instructions.instruction: Mix the olive oil, garlic, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper. Rub the mixture over the beef. Place the onion in a roasting tin and set the beef on top.
instructions.tip: Tuck any loose herbs against the surface so they do not burn as easily.

instructions.title: Start roasting
instructions.instruction: Roast the beef for 20 minutes at the high temperature to brown the outside. Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and continue roasting, allowing approximately 15–20 minutes per 500 g for medium-rare, depending on the cut and shape.
instructions.tip: Use a meat thermometer rather than time alone; temperature is the more reliable guide.

instructions.title: Check doneness and rest
instructions.instruction: Check the centre with a thermometer and cook to your preferred doneness, following appropriate food-safety guidance. Transfer the beef to a board, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 20–30 minutes.
instructions.tip: Resting allows the juices to redistribute and makes carving easier.

instructions.title: Make the gravy
instructions.instruction: Place the roasting tin over medium heat, leaving the onions and drippings inside. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer until thickened, then strain if desired.
instructions.tip: Add stock gradually to avoid lumps and adjust the thickness to your preference.

instructions.title: Carve and serve
instructions.instruction: Slice the beef across the grain and serve with the gravy, roast potatoes, vegetables, and Yorkshire puddings if desired.
instructions.tip: Carving across the grain makes the meat easier to chew.

tips: Choose a joint suited to roasting; topside is lean, while sirloin is richer.
Save the resting juices and stir them into the gravy.
Cooking time varies by joint shape, oven, and desired doneness, so use a thermometer.

alternatives: A small splash of soy sauce

title: Bread and Butter Pudding
description: A classic British dessert made with slices of buttered bread layered in a dish, soaked in a vanilla custard, and baked until golden on top with a soft, creamy centre. Raisins add sweetness and texture.

instructions.title: Prepare the bread
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter a medium baking dish. Butter the bread slices and cut them into triangles or quarters.
instructions.tip: Slightly stale bread absorbs the custard especially well.

instructions.title: Layer the pudding
instructions.instruction: Arrange half the bread in the dish, scatter over half the raisins, then add the remaining bread and raisins.
instructions.tip: Overlap the bread slices slightly so the custard reaches every layer.

instructions.title: Make the custard
instructions.instruction: Whisk the eggs and sugar in a bowl. Warm the milk and cream in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling. Gradually whisk the warm dairy into the eggs, then stir in the vanilla and cinnamon.
instructions.tip: Pour the warm milk in slowly while whisking to avoid scrambling the eggs.

instructions.title: Soak the bread
instructions.instruction: Pour the custard evenly over the bread. Gently press the top pieces down and leave to soak for 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: For a richer centre, let the pudding stand for up to 30 minutes before baking.

instructions.title: Bake until set
instructions.instruction: Sprinkle the nutmeg over the top and bake for 35–45 minutes, until golden and just set in the centre with a slight wobble.
instructions.tip: Cover loosely with foil if the top browns before the custard sets.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Leave the pudding to rest for 10 minutes, then serve warm on its own or with custard or cream.
instructions.tip: Avoid overbaking, which can make the custard rubbery.

tips: Use brioche or raisin bread for a richer variation.
Add orange zest or a small splash of brandy to the custard for extra aroma.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat until hot throughout.

title: Broccoli & Stilton soup
description: A creamy British soup that pairs fresh broccoli with the bold, tangy flavour of Stilton blue cheese. It is smooth, warming, and ideal for lunch with crusty bread.

instructions.title: Soften the onion
instructions.instruction: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook for 5–7 minutes until soft but not browned. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Gentle cooking keeps the onion sweet and prevents the garlic from turning bitter.

instructions.title: Add the potato and stock
instructions.instruction: Add the diced potato and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for about 10 minutes, until the potato is beginning to soften.
instructions.tip: The potato gives the soup body without needing extra flour.

instructions.title: Cook the broccoli
instructions.instruction: Add the broccoli and simmer for 6–8 minutes, until tender but still bright green.
instructions.tip: Avoid prolonged cooking, which can dull the broccoli's colour and flavour.

instructions.title: Blend the soup
instructions.instruction: Remove the pan from the heat and blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth, or carefully blend in batches.
instructions.tip: If using a countertop blender, allow steam to escape according to the blender's instructions.

instructions.title: Add milk and Stilton
instructions.instruction: Return the soup to low heat and stir in the milk and most of the crumbled Stilton. Heat gently until the cheese melts, but do not boil. Taste before adding salt, as the cheese is already salty.
instructions.tip: Reserve a little Stilton to crumble over each bowl.

instructions.title: Serve warm
instructions.instruction: Ladle the soup into bowls, finish with the reserved Stilton and a little black pepper, and serve with crusty bread.
instructions.tip: For a thinner soup, stir in a little extra warm stock before serving.

tips: For a stronger blue-cheese flavour, add a little extra Stilton just before serving.
Use the broccoli stalk as well as the florets; peel and chop it first.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and consume within 3 days, reheating gently.

alternatives: Mature cheddar for a milder flavour

title: Chicken & mushroom Hotpot
description: A comforting British-style chicken hotpot featuring tender chicken, earthy mushrooms, carrots, and onions simmered in a creamy herb gravy beneath a layer of golden sliced potatoes.

instructions.title: Prepare the oven and potatoes
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Bring a saucepan of salted water to a boil, add the sliced potatoes, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain carefully.
instructions.tip: Slice the potatoes evenly so they cook at the same rate.

instructions.title: Brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof casserole. Season the chicken and brown it in batches for 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: The chicken does not need to be fully cooked yet.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Melt half the butter in the casserole. Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and garlic and cook for another 4 minutes.
instructions.tip: Allow the mushrooms to release their moisture before adding the flour.

instructions.title: Make the creamy filling
instructions.instruction: Stir in the flour and thyme, then gradually add the chicken stock while stirring. Mix in the cream and parsley, return the chicken and its juices to the pan, and simmer for 3–4 minutes.
instructions.tip: The sauce should lightly coat the ingredients before baking.

instructions.title: Add the potato topping
instructions.instruction: Arrange the potato slices over the chicken mixture in overlapping layers. Melt the remaining butter and brush it over the potatoes.
instructions.tip: Overlap the slices slightly to create a crisp, attractive topping.

instructions.title: Bake until golden
instructions.instruction: Bake uncovered for 35–45 minutes, until the potatoes are golden and tender and the chicken reaches 74°C internally. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
instructions.tip: Cover loosely with foil if the potatoes brown before they become tender.

tips: Chicken thighs remain juicy during baking, but diced chicken breast can also be used.
Add a handful of frozen peas to the filling for extra colour.
Let the hotpot rest briefly before serving so the sauce thickens.

title: Chocolate Avocado  Mousse
description: A smooth, rich chocolate mousse made with ripe avocado, cocoa powder, and melted dark chocolate. The avocado creates a creamy texture while the chocolate and vanilla give this easy dessert a decadent flavour.

instructions.title: Melt the chocolate
instructions.instruction: Break the dark chocolate into pieces and melt gently in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, or microwave in short bursts. Set aside to cool slightly.
instructions.tip: Do not allow water or steam to enter the chocolate, as it can seize.

instructions.title: Prepare the avocados
instructions.instruction: Scoop the avocado flesh into a food processor or blender. Use fully ripe avocados with no dark or fibrous areas.
instructions.tip: Ripe avocados blend more smoothly and have a milder flavour.

instructions.title: Blend the mousse
instructions.instruction: Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup, almond milk, vanilla, and salt. Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
instructions.tip: Add another tablespoon of almond milk if the mixture is too thick to blend.

instructions.title: Add the chocolate
instructions.instruction: Pour in the melted chocolate and blend again until evenly combined and glossy. Taste and add a little more maple syrup if needed.
instructions.tip: Make sure the melted chocolate is not piping hot before adding it to the avocado.

instructions.title: Chill the mousse
instructions.instruction: Divide the mixture among four small glasses or ramekins. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1–2 hours to allow the mousse to firm up and the flavours to develop.
instructions.tip: Chilling also helps soften any lingering avocado notes.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Serve chilled with fresh raspberries, shaved chocolate, or a light dusting of cocoa powder.
instructions.tip: Use small portions because the mousse is rich and satisfying.

tips: Use ripe avocados and blend thoroughly for the smoothest texture.
For a deeper flavour, add a small pinch of espresso powder.
Keep the mousse covered in the refrigerator and consume within 2 days.

title: 15-minute chicken & halloumi burgers
description: Quick, flavour-packed burgers made with thin chicken breast, golden pan-fried halloumi, crisp lettuce, and a lemony yoghurt sauce in toasted burger buns. Ideal for a speedy lunch or weeknight dinner.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast, sliced horizontally into thin fillets

instructions.title: Season the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken dry and season with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Slice the fillets thinly so they cook quickly.
instructions.tip: For more even cooking, gently flatten thicker sections to an even thickness.

instructions.title: Make the yoghurt sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the Greek yoghurt with lemon juice, chopped mint, and a pinch of salt. Set aside while you cook the chicken and halloumi.
instructions.tip: Add a little lemon zest for a fresher flavour.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Heat half the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for approximately 3–4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until golden and cooked through to 74°C internally. Transfer to a clean plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook in batches if needed.

instructions.title: Fry the halloumi
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the pan and fry the halloumi slices for 1–2 minutes per side until golden.
instructions.tip: Halloumi browns quickly, so watch it closely.

instructions.title: Toast the buns
instructions.instruction: Lightly toast the burger buns in the same pan, cut-side down, for about 30–60 seconds.
instructions.tip: Toasting creates a barrier that helps prevent the buns from becoming soggy.

instructions.title: Assemble the burgers
instructions.instruction: Spread the yoghurt sauce over the buns. Add lettuce, chicken, golden halloumi, and tomato slices. Close the burgers and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Serve with a green salad, oven chips, or grilled vegetables.

tips: Thin chicken fillets help keep the cooking time close to 15 minutes.
Halloumi is naturally salty, so season the chicken sauce and cheese lightly.
Assemble just before eating to keep the buns fresh.

title: BBQ Pork Sloppy Joes
description: A messy, satisfying American sandwich filled with minced pork simmered in smoky barbecue sauce, tomatoes, onions, and a touch of mustard. Serve the juicy filling in soft toasted buns with coleslaw or pickles.

instructions.title: Cook the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
instructions.tip: Dice the vegetables finely so they blend into the sandwich filling.

instructions.title: Brown the pork
instructions.instruction: Add the minced pork and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Drain excess fat if necessary, leaving a little behind for flavour.

instructions.title: Make the barbecue sauce
instructions.instruction: Stir in the barbecue sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, smoked paprika, and cider vinegar.
instructions.tip: Choose a smoky or sweet barbecue sauce according to your preference.

instructions.title: Simmer the filling
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat and simmer for 5–8 minutes, stirring regularly, until the sauce thickens and coats the pork. Season with salt and pepper.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if the mixture becomes too thick before the flavours develop.

instructions.title: Toast the buns
instructions.instruction: Slice the buns and toast them lightly in a dry pan or under a grill until the cut sides are golden.
instructions.tip: Toasted buns hold the saucy filling better.

instructions.title: Fill and serve
instructions.instruction: Spoon the hot pork mixture generously into the buns. Serve with pickles, coleslaw, or a crisp green salad.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately and keep napkins handy; the filling is meant to be juicy.

tips: For a spicier filling, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or chopped jalapeño.
Prepare the filling ahead and reheat gently with a splash of water.
Use sturdy buns to prevent the sauce from soaking through too quickly.

alternatives: Tomato sauce with smoked paprika and a little honey

title: Beef Brisket Pot Roast
description: A slow-cooked American-style pot roast made with beef brisket, onions, carrots, garlic, and herbs braised in a rich beef broth until tender enough to slice or pull apart.

instructions.title: Preheat and season
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Pat the brisket dry and season generously on all sides with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: A dry surface helps the beef develop a good crust.

instructions.title: Sear the brisket
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a heavy ovenproof casserole over medium-high heat. Sear the brisket for 4–5 minutes per side until deeply browned, then transfer it to a plate.
instructions.tip: Avoid moving the meat too early; let each side form a proper crust.

instructions.title: Build the braising base
instructions.instruction: Add the onions, carrots, and celery to the casserole and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste, then cook for 1 minute.
instructions.tip: The browned vegetables add depth to the final gravy.

instructions.title: Deglaze and braise
instructions.instruction: Pour in the red wine and scrape up the browned bits. Add the beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Return the brisket to the casserole; the liquid should come partway up the meat.
instructions.tip: If you do not use wine, replace it with additional beef stock.

instructions.title: Slow-cook until tender
instructions.instruction: Cover tightly and cook in the oven for 3–4 hours, turning the brisket once halfway through, until a fork slides into the meat easily. Add a little stock or water if the liquid reduces too much.
instructions.tip: Brisket becomes tender through slow cooking; do not rush this stage.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the brisket to a board and rest for 15–20 minutes. Remove the herb stems and bay leaves, skim excess fat from the cooking liquid, and serve the beef sliced across the grain with the vegetables and gravy.
instructions.tip: For a thicker gravy, simmer the cooking liquid uncovered for a few minutes before serving.

tips: Choose a brisket cut with some marbling for better flavour and tenderness.
Cook the roast a day ahead if convenient; the flavours deepen overnight.
Always slice brisket across the grain for a more tender bite.

alternatives: Beef stock with 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar

title: Choc Chip Pecan Pie
description: A rich American-style pecan pie with a buttery pastry shell, toasted pecans, chocolate chips, and a sweet caramel-like filling. The crisp nuts and melted chocolate create a satisfying contrast in every slice.

instructions.title: Prepare the pastry
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Line a 23 cm pie dish with the shortcrust pastry, trim the edges, and chill for 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Chilling helps the pastry keep its shape while baking.

instructions.title: Partially bake the crust
instructions.instruction: Line the pastry with baking paper and baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the paper and beans, and bake for another 5 minutes.
instructions.tip: A partially baked crust helps prevent a soggy bottom.

instructions.title: Prepare the filling
instructions.instruction: Whisk the eggs, brown sugar, golden syrup, melted butter, vanilla, and salt in a bowl until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Allow the melted butter to cool slightly before mixing it with the eggs.

instructions.title: Add the pecans and chocolate
instructions.instruction: Scatter the pecans and chocolate chips over the pastry base. Pour the syrup mixture evenly over them.
instructions.tip: Arrange a few pecan halves on top for a decorative finish.

instructions.title: Bake the pie
instructions.instruction: Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre has only a slight wobble. Cover the crust with foil if it browns too quickly.
instructions.tip: The filling will continue to set as the pie cools, so avoid baking until completely firm.

instructions.title: Cool and slice
instructions.instruction: Cool the pie on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing. Serve at room temperature or slightly warm with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.
instructions.tip: Use a sharp knife and wipe it between slices for neater portions.

tips: Toast the pecans briefly before using them for a deeper nutty flavour.
Let the pie cool fully so the filling can set before cutting.
Store covered in the refrigerator and bring slices to room temperature before serving.

alternatives: Maple syrup, noting the filling may set more softly

title: Chocolate Raspberry Brownies
description: Fudgy chocolate brownies studded with juicy raspberries, combining intense cocoa flavour with a bright fruity tang. A crackly top and soft centre make these brownies a crowd-pleasing dessert.

instructions.title: Prepare the tin
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Line a 20 cm square baking tin with baking paper, leaving some overhang to help lift out the brownies.
instructions.tip: A metal tin helps the brownies bake evenly and develop crisp edges.

instructions.title: Melt the chocolate and butter
instructions.instruction: Place the chopped dark chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl. Melt gently over a pan of simmering water or in short microwave bursts, stirring until smooth. Leave to cool slightly.
instructions.tip: Avoid overheating the chocolate, which can make it grainy.

instructions.title: Whisk the eggs and sugar
instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and caster sugar for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened. Stir in the vanilla extract.
instructions.tip: Whisking the eggs and sugar well helps create a delicate crackly top.

instructions.title: Make the brownie batter
instructions.instruction: Gradually stir the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt, then fold gently until no dry streaks remain.
instructions.tip: Do not overmix once the flour has been added, or the brownies may become cakey.

instructions.title: Add raspberries and bake
instructions.instruction: Fold in half the raspberries and spread the batter in the prepared tin. Scatter the remaining raspberries over the top. Bake for 25–32 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still looks slightly soft.
instructions.tip: A few moist crumbs on a tester are ideal for fudgy brownies; wet batter means they need more time.

instructions.title: Cool and cut
instructions.instruction: Cool completely in the tin before lifting out and cutting into 12 squares. For especially neat slices, chill briefly before cutting.
instructions.tip: Use a warm, clean knife for smooth edges.

tips: Use chocolate with around 60–70% cocoa for a deep chocolate flavour.
If using frozen raspberries, add them while still frozen and expect a slightly longer baking time.
Store the cooled brownies in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Cream Cheese Tart
description: A creamy baked cheesecake-style tart with a crisp buttery pastry shell and a smooth, lightly tangy cream cheese filling. Serve chilled with fresh berries or a drizzle of fruit sauce for an elegant dessert.

instructions.title: Prepare the pastry case
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Roll out the shortcrust pastry and line a 23 cm tart tin. Trim the edges, prick the base with a fork, and chill for 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Chilling the pastry helps prevent shrinkage during baking.

instructions.title: Blind-bake the pastry
instructions.instruction: Line the pastry with baking paper and baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the beans and paper, then bake for another 5 minutes until the base looks dry.
