instructions.tip: A partially baked shell helps keep the finished tart crisp.

instructions.title: Prepare the filling
instructions.instruction: Beat the softened cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing gently after each addition. Stir in the cream, vanilla, lemon zest, and flour.
instructions.tip: Use room-temperature cream cheese to avoid lumps.

instructions.title: Fill the tart
instructions.instruction: Pour the cream cheese mixture into the cooled pastry shell and smooth the surface with a spatula.
instructions.tip: Tap the tin gently on the counter to release large air bubbles.

instructions.title: Bake until set
instructions.instruction: Bake for 25–35 minutes until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. Turn off the oven and leave the tart inside with the door slightly open for 10 minutes.
instructions.tip: Avoid overbaking, as the filling will firm further while cooling.

instructions.title: Cool and serve
instructions.instruction: Cool the tart completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Remove from the tin, slice, and serve with fresh strawberries.
instructions.tip: Wipe the knife between slices for clean edges.

tips: Do not whip the filling excessively, as too much air can cause cracks.
For a fruitier finish, spread a thin layer of strawberry jam over the cooled tart.
Keep covered in the refrigerator and consume within 3 days.

title: French Onion Chicken with Roasted Carrots & Mashed Potatoes
description: A comforting dinner featuring golden chicken breasts topped with deeply caramelised onions and melted cheese in a French onion-inspired sauce, served with sweet roasted carrots and creamy mashed potatoes.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the carrots with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, half the garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25–35 minutes, turning halfway through.
instructions.tip: Keep the carrot pieces similar in size for even roasting.

instructions.title: Caramelise the onions
instructions.instruction: Melt 25 g of butter in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-low heat. Add the sliced onions and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and deep golden. Add a splash of water if they begin to catch.
instructions.tip: Cook the onions slowly; proper caramelisation gives the sauce its signature flavour.

instructions.title: Brown the chicken
instructions.instruction: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Transfer the onions temporarily to a bowl, add the remaining olive oil to the skillet, and brown the chicken for 3–4 minutes per side.
instructions.tip: The chicken will finish cooking in the sauce, so browning is the goal at this stage.

instructions.title: Make the onion sauce
instructions.instruction: Return the onions to the skillet and stir in the remaining garlic, thyme, stock, and balsamic vinegar. Simmer for 2–3 minutes, then place the chicken among the onions and spoon some sauce over each piece.
instructions.tip: Scrape up the browned bits from the skillet to enrich the sauce.

instructions.title: Add cheese and finish baking
instructions.instruction: Sprinkle the Gruyère over the chicken and onions. Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 12–18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74°C internally and the cheese is melted.
instructions.tip: Cooking time depends on the thickness of the chicken breasts.

instructions.title: Make the mashed potatoes and serve
instructions.instruction: Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain, then mash with the remaining butter and milk. Serve the cheesy onion chicken with mashed potatoes, roasted carrots, and pan sauce.
instructions.tip: Warm the milk before adding it to the potatoes for a smoother mash.

tips: Use a mix of yellow and red onions for a slightly sweeter sauce.
Gruyère gives a traditional French onion flavour, but Swiss cheese also works.
For a lighter mash, replace some butter with warm chicken stock.

title: Fruit and Cream Cheese Breakfast Pastries
description: Flaky breakfast pastries made with buttery puff pastry, a lightly sweetened cream cheese filling, and fresh fruit. They are easy to customise with seasonal berries, peaches, or apples.

instructions.title: Prepare the oven and pastry
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper. Unroll the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface and cut it into 8 equal rectangles.
instructions.tip: Keep the pastry cool so it remains easy to handle.

instructions.title: Mix the cream cheese filling
instructions.instruction: Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until smooth and spreadable.
instructions.tip: Softened cream cheese mixes more easily and produces a lump-free filling.

instructions.title: Shape the pastries
instructions.instruction: Score a smaller rectangle inside each pastry piece, leaving a border without cutting all the way through. Spread a spoonful of cream cheese filling inside each scored border.
instructions.tip: The scored border helps the pastry rise around the filling.

instructions.title: Add the fruit
instructions.instruction: Arrange the sliced strawberries and blueberries over the cream cheese filling, distributing the fruit evenly among the pastries.
instructions.tip: Pat washed fruit dry to prevent excess moisture from softening the pastry.

instructions.title: Brush and bake
instructions.instruction: Brush the exposed pastry borders with beaten egg. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until puffed and golden brown.
instructions.tip: Rotate the tray if your oven browns unevenly.

instructions.title: Glaze and serve
instructions.instruction: Warm the apricot jam with the water and brush lightly over the fruit. Cool the pastries for 5–10 minutes before serving.
instructions.tip: The glaze gives the fruit a glossy finish and helps keep it moist.

tips: Serve warm for the flakiest pastry texture.
Avoid overfilling the pastries, as the cream cheese may spread during baking.
Refrigerate leftovers because of the cream cheese filling and consume within 2 days.

title: Honey Balsamic Chicken with Crispy Broccoli & Potatoes
description: A balanced sheet-pan dinner featuring juicy honey-balsamic glazed chicken, crispy roasted potatoes, and broccoli with caramelised edges. The sweet-tangy glaze brings the components together in an easy weeknight meal.

instructions.title: Preheat and roast the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the halved potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, half the oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread on a large baking tray and roast for 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Place the cut sides of the potatoes against the tray for better browning.

instructions.title: Make the honey balsamic glaze
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the honey, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, garlic, paprika, remaining oregano, and 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
instructions.tip: Reserve a little glaze separately if you want extra for serving; do not reuse glaze that has contacted raw chicken.

instructions.title: Season the chicken
instructions.instruction: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season with salt and pepper. Place them on the tray beside the potatoes and brush generously with the glaze.
instructions.tip: Arrange the chicken in a single layer so it roasts rather than steams.

instructions.title: Continue roasting
instructions.instruction: Return the tray to the oven and roast for 15 minutes. Turn the potatoes and brush the chicken with the pan glaze, ensuring the chicken reaches 74°C internally.
instructions.tip: If the glaze darkens too quickly, reduce the oven temperature slightly.

instructions.title: Add the broccoli
instructions.instruction: Toss the broccoli florets with the remaining olive oil and a pinch of salt. Add them to the tray and roast for another 10–15 minutes until crisp at the edges and tender, and the chicken is fully cooked.
instructions.tip: Keep the broccoli florets fairly large so they do not burn before the potatoes finish.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Let the chicken rest for 3–5 minutes. Toss the potatoes and broccoli through the tray juices, then serve with the chicken and any reserved fresh glaze.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of lemon just before serving brightens the sweet balsamic flavours.

tips: Cut the potatoes evenly to help them roast at the same speed.
Use a large tray and avoid overcrowding for crispier vegetables.
Chicken breast can be used, but check it earlier to avoid overcooking.

title: Hot Chocolate Fudge
description: A rich, soft chocolate fudge with the comforting flavour of hot cocoa, made with dark chocolate, condensed milk, butter, and a touch of vanilla. Cut into small squares for an indulgent sweet treat.

instructions.title: Prepare the tin
instructions.instruction: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper, leaving some overhang so the fudge can be lifted out easily.
instructions.tip: Lightly grease the paper if it tends to move around in the tin.

instructions.title: Melt the chocolate mixture
instructions.instruction: Place the chopped chocolate, condensed milk, and butter in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of gently simmering water. Stir until melted and smooth.
instructions.tip: Keep the bowl above the water rather than letting it touch the water directly.

instructions.title: Add the cocoa flavour
instructions.instruction: Remove the bowl from the heat. Sift in the cocoa powder, then stir in the vanilla extract and salt until evenly combined.
instructions.tip: Sifting the cocoa prevents dry lumps in the fudge.

instructions.title: Add marshmallows
instructions.instruction: Allow the mixture to cool for 2–3 minutes, then fold in the mini marshmallows, reserving a few to scatter over the top.
instructions.tip: Letting the chocolate cool slightly helps the marshmallows retain their shape.

instructions.title: Chill until firm
instructions.instruction: Spread the mixture into the prepared tin and smooth the surface. Scatter the remaining marshmallows over the top and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, or until firm.
instructions.tip: Press the mixture firmly into the corners to avoid air pockets.

instructions.title: Cut into squares
instructions.instruction: Lift the fudge from the tin using the baking paper and cut into 20 small squares with a sharp knife. Serve chilled or at cool room temperature.
instructions.tip: Warm and wipe the knife between cuts for neat squares.

tips: Use good-quality chocolate for a smoother texture and deeper flavour.
Store the fudge in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
For a hot-cocoa twist, add a pinch of cinnamon or instant espresso powder.

title: Kentucky Fried Chicken
description: A homemade take on Kentucky-style fried chicken with juicy bone-in pieces, a seasoned buttermilk marinade, and a crisp, peppery coating. The chicken is fried until golden and cooked through for a crunchy exterior and tender centre.

instructions.title: Marinate the chicken
instructions.instruction: Season the chicken lightly with salt and place it in a bowl with the buttermilk. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
instructions.tip: Marinating helps tenderise the chicken and lets the seasoning penetrate.

instructions.title: Prepare the seasoned flour
instructions.instruction: Combine the flour, cornflour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, thyme, black pepper, cayenne, and remaining salt in a large shallow bowl.
instructions.tip: Cornflour helps produce a crisp coating.

instructions.title: Coat the chicken
instructions.instruction: Remove one piece of chicken from the buttermilk, allow excess to drip off, and press it firmly into the flour mixture. Turn and coat thoroughly. Place on a rack and repeat with the remaining pieces.
instructions.tip: Pressing the coating onto the chicken helps it adhere during frying.

instructions.title: Heat the oil
instructions.instruction: Pour oil into a deep, heavy pot to a safe frying depth, leaving plenty of space at the top. Heat to 165–175°C and check with a cooking thermometer.
instructions.tip: Never fill the pot more than halfway with oil, and keep water away from hot oil.

instructions.title: Fry in batches
instructions.instruction: Carefully lower a few chicken pieces into the oil without crowding the pot. Fry, turning as needed, until golden and cooked through; smaller pieces may take 12–15 minutes, while larger bone-in pieces can take longer. The thickest part must reach 74°C without touching the bone.
instructions.tip: If the coating browns too quickly, lower the oil temperature and finish cooking gently.

instructions.title: Drain and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the fried chicken to a wire rack set over a tray and let it rest for a few minutes. Serve hot with coleslaw, corn, biscuits, or potato wedges.
instructions.tip: A wire rack allows air to circulate and keeps the coating crisp.

tips: Maintain the oil temperature between batches for a consistent crust.
Use a thermometer to confirm safe doneness, especially for large bone-in pieces.
Do not cover freshly fried chicken tightly, as trapped steam softens the coating.

alternatives: Milk mixed with lemon juice and rested for 5 minutes

title: key Lime Pie
description: A classic American citrus dessert with a buttery biscuit crust and a smooth filling made from lime juice, sweetened condensed milk, and egg yolks. Chilled until set and topped with whipped cream, it balances sweet creaminess with bright tartness.

ingredients.item: Digestive biscuits or graham crackers, crushed
Key lime juice or regular lime juice

instructions.title: Prepare the crust
instructions.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Mix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter until the crumbs resemble damp sand.
instructions.tip: Crush the biscuits finely so the crust holds together when sliced.

instructions.title: Shape and bake the crust
instructions.instruction: Press the mixture firmly into the base and sides of a 23 cm pie dish. Bake for 8–10 minutes, then cool slightly.
instructions.tip: Use the back of a spoon or the base of a glass to compact the crumbs evenly.

instructions.title: Mix the filling
instructions.instruction: Whisk the egg yolks until slightly thickened. Add the condensed milk, lime juice, and lime zest, whisking until smooth.
instructions.tip: Fresh lime juice gives the pie a brighter flavour than bottled juice.

instructions.title: Fill and bake
instructions.instruction: Pour the filling into the crust and bake for 15–18 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. The filling should reach a safe temperature for an egg-based dessert.
instructions.tip: Avoid overbaking, which can make the filling firm and less creamy.

instructions.title: Chill the pie
instructions.instruction: Cool the pie to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until fully set.
instructions.tip: Chilling is essential for clean slices and a firm filling.

instructions.title: Whip the cream and serve
instructions.instruction: Whip the double cream with the icing sugar until soft peaks form. Spread or pipe it over the chilled pie and finish with a little extra lime zest.
instructions.tip: Add the cream shortly before serving for the freshest finish.

tips: Regular Persian limes work well if Key limes are unavailable.
For a stronger citrus flavour, add extra lime zest rather than excessive juice.
Keep the pie refrigerated and consume within 3 days.

title: Krispy Kreme Donut
description: A homemade version of the classic glazed yeast doughnut, with a light, airy interior and a thin, sweet vanilla glaze. The dough is enriched with milk, butter, and egg, then fried until delicately golden.

instructions.title: Activate and mix the dough
instructions.instruction: Combine the warm milk, caster sugar, and yeast in a large bowl. Let stand for 5 minutes if using active dry yeast. Add the egg, softened butter, vanilla, flour, and salt, then mix until a soft dough forms.
instructions.tip: The milk should feel warm, not hot, so it does not damage the yeast.

instructions.title: Knead the dough
instructions.instruction: Knead by hand for 8–10 minutes or with a mixer fitted with a dough hook for 5–7 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Place in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise for 60–90 minutes until doubled.
instructions.tip: The dough should be soft and slightly tacky; avoid adding too much extra flour.

instructions.title: Shape the doughnuts
instructions.instruction: Roll the dough to about 1.2 cm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut out doughnut rings using a doughnut cutter or two round cutters. Transfer to parchment squares and cover loosely.
instructions.tip: Keep the doughnut holes; they can be fried as small doughnut bites.

instructions.title: Proof the doughnuts
instructions.instruction: Let the shaped doughnuts rise for 30–45 minutes until puffy. Meanwhile, mix the icing sugar with vanilla and enough hot water to make a smooth, pourable glaze.
instructions.tip: Avoid overproofing, which can make the doughnuts collapse when handled.

instructions.title: Fry until golden
instructions.instruction: Heat oil in a deep, heavy pot to 175°C. Fry the doughnuts in small batches for about 1–2 minutes per side until pale golden and cooked through. Drain briefly on a wire rack.
instructions.tip: Maintain the oil temperature and handle the proofed dough gently to preserve their shape.

instructions.title: Glaze and cool
instructions.instruction: While the doughnuts are still warm, dip each one into the glaze, turn to coat, and place on a rack to set. Serve fresh once the glaze has formed a thin shell.
instructions.tip: Glazing warm doughnuts helps create the classic thin, shiny coating.

tips: Use a thermometer to keep frying oil close to 175°C.
Doughnuts taste best on the day they are made.
Do not overcrowd the pot, as this lowers the oil temperature and can make the doughnuts greasy.

alternatives: Strong white bread flour for a chewier texture

title: Lasagna Sanwiches
description: A hearty Italian-American-inspired sandwich that captures the flavours of lasagna between toasted bread. Layers of seasoned beef, tomato sauce, creamy ricotta, and melted mozzarella create a rich, cheesy filling with crisp edges.

ingredients.item: Ciabatta rolls or sturdy sandwich rolls

instructions.title: Prepare the meat sauce
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, then add the ground beef and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Drain excess fat if needed, but leave a little for flavour.

instructions.title: Season and simmer
instructions.instruction: Stir in the marinara sauce, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 5–8 minutes until the sauce thickens. Stir in the chopped basil and remove from the heat.
instructions.tip: A thick meat sauce is easier to sandwich and less likely to soak the bread.

instructions.title: Prepare the cheese filling
instructions.instruction: Mix the ricotta with the Parmesan and half of the mozzarella in a bowl. Season lightly with black pepper.
instructions.tip: If the ricotta is very wet, drain it briefly in a fine sieve.

instructions.title: Assemble the sandwiches
instructions.instruction: Split the rolls and spread the cut sides lightly with butter. Spoon the meat sauce onto the bottom halves, add the ricotta mixture, and sprinkle over the remaining mozzarella. Place the top halves alongside or over the filling.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill the rolls, as the cheese and sauce will expand and soften during baking.

instructions.title: Bake until melted
instructions.instruction: Place the sandwiches on a baking tray and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8–12 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the bread is crisp. For a more open-faced finish, leave the tops off during baking and add them afterward.
instructions.tip: Watch the bread near the end so it becomes crisp without burning.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Close the sandwiches if they were baked open-faced, allow them to rest for 2 minutes, then serve hot with extra marinara sauce for dipping.
instructions.tip: Serve with a green salad or roasted vegetables to balance the richness.

tips: Use sturdy rolls that can hold the filling without falling apart.
For extra lasagna flavour, add a pinch of nutmeg to the ricotta mixture.
Prepare the meat sauce ahead of time and assemble the sandwiches just before baking.

alternatives: Cream cheese mixed with a little milk

title: Bang bang prawn salad
description: A vibrant Asian-inspired prawn salad featuring crisp vegetables, tender prawns, and a creamy, sweet-spicy bang bang dressing made with mayonnaise, sweet chilli sauce, and lime. Fresh herbs and crunchy peanuts complete this refreshing meal.

instructions.title: Make the bang bang dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the mayonnaise, sweet chilli sauce, sriracha, lime juice, and minced garlic in a small bowl until smooth. Taste and adjust the heat with additional sriracha if desired.
instructions.tip: Keep the dressing chilled while preparing the other ingredients.

instructions.title: Prepare the salad vegetables
instructions.instruction: Place the lettuce, red cabbage, carrot, cucumber, and spring onions in a large salad bowl. Toss lightly to distribute the vegetables evenly.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables into thin, similar-sized pieces for a pleasant crunch.

instructions.title: Season the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry with paper towels and season lightly with salt and black pepper.
instructions.tip: Dry prawns brown more effectively and release less water in the pan.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the prawns for approximately 2–3 minutes per side, depending on size, until opaque and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking, as prawns can quickly become rubbery.

instructions.title: Dress the salad
instructions.instruction: Allow the prawns to cool slightly. Add them to the salad and drizzle over most of the bang bang dressing. Toss gently until the ingredients are lightly coated.
instructions.tip: Keep a little dressing aside for serving so the salad does not become too heavy.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter the chopped coriander and roasted peanuts over the salad. Serve immediately with the remaining dressing on the side.
instructions.tip: Add cooked rice noodles if you want a more substantial meal.

tips: For extra crunch, add thinly sliced red bell pepper.
Adjust the sriracha to make the dressing milder or hotter.
For best texture, dress the salad immediately before serving.

title: Barbecue pork buns
description: Soft, fluffy steamed buns filled with Cantonese-inspired barbecue pork glazed in a sweet, savoury sauce. The tender filling combines hoisin, soy, honey, and aromatic garlic for a satisfying dim sum-style dish.

instructions.title: Prepare the dough
instructions.instruction: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm water, and 1 tablespoon of oil in a bowl. Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth, then cover and leave in a warm place for about 60–90 minutes, until doubled in size.
instructions.tip: The water should be warm rather than hot to protect the yeast.

instructions.title: Cook the pork
instructions.instruction: Heat the remaining oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced pork and cook until browned. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for another minute.
instructions.tip: Cut the pork into small, even pieces so the filling cooks consistently.

instructions.title: Make the barbecue filling
instructions.instruction: Add the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, honey, oyster sauce, and 100 ml water. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pork is tender. Mix the cornflour with 1 tablespoon of cold water, stir it into the pan, and cook until the sauce thickens. Cool completely.
instructions.tip: The filling must be thick and cool before being enclosed in the dough.

instructions.title: Shape the buns
instructions.instruction: Punch down the risen dough and divide it into 12 equal portions. Roll each portion into a circle, keeping the centre slightly thicker than the edges. Place a spoonful of cooled pork filling in the centre and pleat the edges together to seal.
instructions.tip: Avoid overfilling, which can make the buns difficult to close.

instructions.title: Proof and steam
instructions.instruction: Place each bun on a small square of baking paper in a steamer. Cover and let rise for 20–30 minutes. Steam over simmering water for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is cooked through.
instructions.tip: Leave space between the buns because they expand during steaming.

instructions.title: Rest and serve
instructions.instruction: Turn off the heat and leave the covered steamer for 3 minutes before opening the lid gradually. Serve the buns warm with extra hoisin or chilli sauce.
instructions.tip: Opening the lid too quickly can cause sudden temperature changes that make the buns wrinkle.

tips: Prepare the pork filling a day ahead and refrigerate it until needed.
Keep the steamer water at a steady simmer rather than a vigorous boil.
Refrigerate leftover buns promptly and reheat by steaming until hot throughout.

title: Beef Banh Mi Bowls with Sriracha Mayo, Carrot & Pickled Cucumber
description: A Vietnamese-inspired rice bowl with savoury marinated beef, tangy quick-pickled carrots and cucumber, fresh herbs, and creamy sriracha mayonnaise. It brings the contrasting flavours and textures of a banh mi sandwich to a colourful bowl.

instructions.title: Cook the rice
instructions.instruction: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs mostly clear. Cook according to the package instructions, then cover and keep warm.
instructions.tip: Rinsing removes excess surface starch and helps produce fluffy rice.

instructions.title: Quick-pickle the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Whisk the rice vinegar with the sugar and salt until dissolved. Add the carrot and cucumber, toss well, and leave to pickle for at least 20 minutes.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables thinly so they absorb the pickling liquid quickly.

instructions.title: Marinate the beef
instructions.instruction: Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce, honey, garlic, and ginger in a bowl. Add the sliced beef and toss to coat. Leave for 10–15 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
instructions.tip: Slice the beef across the grain for a more tender result.

instructions.title: Make the sriracha mayo
instructions.instruction: Combine the mayonnaise, sriracha, and lime juice in a small bowl. Taste and adjust the heat as desired.
instructions.tip: Add a teaspoon of water if you prefer a thinner drizzle.

instructions.title: Sear the beef
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the beef in batches for 2–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked to your preference. Avoid overcrowding the pan.
instructions.tip: A hot pan helps the beef brown rather than steam in its marinade.

instructions.title: Assemble the bowls
instructions.instruction: Divide the rice among four bowls. Top with the beef, drained pickled carrots and cucumber, coriander, and spring onions. Drizzle with sriracha mayo and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Keep the pickling liquid out of the bowls so the rice does not become watery.

tips: Prepare the pickled vegetables ahead and refrigerate them for a stronger tang.
Add sliced jalapeños for extra heat and crunch.
For a lighter bowl, replace some rice with shredded lettuce.

title: Beef pho
description: A Vietnamese noodle soup featuring a fragrant broth infused with star anise, cinnamon, ginger, and onion, served with rice noodles, thinly sliced beef, and fresh herbs. Lime, bean sprouts, and chilli bring freshness and balance to the rich broth.

instructions.title: Char the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Place the onion halves and ginger in a dry skillet over medium-high heat. Turn occasionally until the cut surfaces are darkened and fragrant, about 5–8 minutes.
instructions.tip: Light charring gives the broth its characteristic depth and aroma.

instructions.title: Toast the spices
instructions.instruction: In a small dry pan, toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, and coriander seeds for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat moderate so the spices do not burn.

instructions.title: Simmer the broth
instructions.instruction: Bring the beef stock to a gentle simmer in a large pot. Add the charred onion, ginger, and toasted spices. Simmer uncovered for 30–45 minutes, then strain the broth. Stir in the fish sauce and sugar, adjusting to taste.
instructions.tip: A gentle simmer keeps the broth clear and clean-tasting.

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and rinse briefly with warm water to prevent sticking.
instructions.tip: Cook noodles separately so excess starch does not cloud the broth.

instructions.title: Prepare the beef and bowls
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodles among four large heatproof bowls and arrange the raw, very thinly sliced beef on top. Bring the strained broth to a full boil immediately before serving.
instructions.tip: Freeze the beef for 20–30 minutes before slicing to make it easier to cut thinly.

instructions.title: Ladle and garnish
instructions.instruction: Pour the boiling broth over the beef, ensuring the slices are fully submerged and cook through safely. Garnish with bean sprouts, spring onions, basil or coriander, chilli, and lime wedges. Serve immediately.
instructions.tip: If you prefer not to rely on the hot broth to cook the beef, briefly simmer the slices in the broth first.

tips: Taste the broth before serving and balance it with fish sauce, sugar, or lime.
Use a sharp knife to slice the beef as thinly as possible.
Keep herbs and crunchy garnishes separate until serving.

title: Noodle bowl salad
description: A fresh Asian-inspired noodle salad bowl with crisp vegetables, tender noodles, fragrant herbs, and a tangy sesame-lime dressing. It works as a light lunch or a versatile side dish and can be customised with tofu, chicken, or prawns.

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool, then shake off excess water.
instructions.tip: Do not overcook the noodles, as they will soften further when dressed.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Place the cabbage, carrots, cucumber, bell pepper, and spring onions in a large bowl. Add the chopped coriander and mint.
instructions.tip: A julienne peeler makes quick work of the carrots and cucumber.

instructions.title: Mix the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the soy sauce, lime juice, sesame oil, neutral oil, honey, and grated ginger until well combined.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing and add extra lime for sharpness or honey for sweetness.

instructions.title: Combine the salad
instructions.instruction: Add the cooled noodles to the vegetables. Pour over the dressing and toss thoroughly until the noodles and vegetables are evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Use clean hands or two large forks to separate the noodles as you toss.

instructions.title: Add the toppings
instructions.instruction: Scatter the sesame seeds and chopped cashews over the salad. Toss lightly once more.
instructions.tip: Add the nuts just before serving to preserve their crunch.

instructions.title: Serve the noodle bowls
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodle salad among four bowls and serve chilled or at room temperature. Add extra herbs and lime wedges if desired.
instructions.tip: For a complete meal, top with grilled tofu, chicken, or prawns.

tips: Rinse the noodles after cooking to remove excess starch and cool them quickly.
Keep some dressing aside to refresh the salad before serving.
Add edamame or tofu for a higher-protein vegetarian bowl.

title: Prawn & noodle salad with crispy shallots
description: A bright Southeast Asian-inspired salad combining juicy prawns, rice noodles, crunchy vegetables, fresh herbs, and a tangy fish sauce and lime dressing. Crispy golden shallots add a savoury crunch to every serving.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook the rice vermicelli according to the package instructions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside to cool completely.
instructions.tip: Snip long noodles with kitchen scissors if you prefer them easier to toss and eat.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic, and sliced chilli until the sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, sweet, and spicy flavours.
instructions.tip: Add a tablespoon of water if the dressing tastes too concentrated.

instructions.title: Fry the shallots
instructions.instruction: Heat the neutral oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the sliced shallots and fry gently, stirring often, for 4–7 minutes until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
instructions.tip: Remove the shallots just before they become deep brown, as residual heat will continue to darken them.

instructions.title: Cook the prawns
instructions.instruction: Pat the prawns dry and season lightly. Heat 1 teaspoon of fresh oil in a skillet and cook the prawns for 2–3 minutes per side until opaque and cooked through.
instructions.tip: Cook in batches if needed to avoid overcrowding the pan.

instructions.title: Toss the salad
instructions.instruction: Combine the cooled noodles with the carrot, cucumber, bean sprouts, coriander, and mint. Pour over the dressing and toss until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Add the dressing gradually so the salad remains fresh rather than watery.

instructions.title: Finish with prawns and shallots
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodle salad among four bowls and arrange the cooked prawns on top. Scatter over the crispy shallots and serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Add the crispy shallots at the very end to preserve their texture.

tips: Keep the shallot oil for stir-fries or dressings after it cools and is strained.
Use fresh lime juice for a brighter, more balanced dressing.
Serve immediately after adding the shallots to keep them crisp.

title: Purple sprouting broccoli tempura with nuoc cham
description: Delicate purple sprouting broccoli coated in a light, crisp Japanese-style tempura batter and fried until golden. Served with Vietnamese nuoc cham dipping sauce, the dish combines crunchy vegetables with a lively balance of lime, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, and chilli.

instructions.title: Prepare the broccoli
instructions.instruction: Wash the purple sprouting broccoli and dry it thoroughly. Trim any tough stem ends and cut larger stems lengthwise so the pieces cook evenly.
instructions.tip: Dry vegetables help the batter adhere and reduce splattering during frying.

instructions.title: Make the nuoc cham
instructions.instruction: Stir the sugar into the warm water until dissolved. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, garlic, chilli, and shredded carrot. Taste and adjust with a little more lime or water as needed.
instructions.tip: Make the sauce first so the flavours have time to mingle.

instructions.title: Prepare the tempura batter
instructions.instruction: Whisk the egg lightly with the cold sparkling water. Add the flour, cornflour, and baking powder, stirring briefly until just combined. Leave a few small lumps in the batter.
instructions.tip: Keep the batter cold and avoid overmixing to maintain a light, crisp coating.

instructions.title: Heat the oil
instructions.instruction: Heat neutral oil in a deep, heavy saucepan to 175–180°C, leaving plenty of space at the top. Prepare a wire rack over a tray for draining the cooked broccoli.
instructions.tip: Use a thermometer for reliable temperature control and never leave hot oil unattended.

instructions.title: Fry the broccoli
instructions.instruction: Dip a few broccoli pieces into the batter, allowing excess to drip off. Carefully lower them into the hot oil and fry for 2–4 minutes, turning as needed, until crisp and pale golden. Cook in small batches.
instructions.tip: Do not crowd the pan, as this lowers the oil temperature and makes the coating greasy.

instructions.title: Drain and serve
instructions.instruction: Transfer the tempura to the wire rack and season lightly if desired. Serve immediately with the nuoc cham dipping sauce.
instructions.tip: Avoid stacking the tempura; airflow helps preserve its crisp coating.

tips: Broccoli florets and tenderstem broccoli can be used if purple sprouting broccoli is unavailable.
Prepare the batter immediately before frying for the best texture.
Serve the tempura as soon as it is cooked rather than covering it with a lid.

alternatives: 2 tbsp additional cold sparkling water and 1 tbsp extra flour

title: Rice paper dumplings
description: Crispy rice paper dumplings filled with seasoned vegetables, mushrooms, and tofu. The wrappers become chewy inside and golden outside when pan-fried, while a soy-vinegar dipping sauce adds a savoury, tangy finish.

ingredients.item: Shiitake or button mushrooms, finely chopped

instructions.title: Prepare the filling
instructions.instruction: Heat 1 teaspoon of neutral oil in a skillet. Add the mushrooms and cook for 4–5 minutes until their moisture evaporates. Add the cabbage, carrot, spring onions, garlic, and ginger and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
instructions.tip: Cook out excess moisture so the rice paper wrappers do not become soggy.

instructions.title: Season the filling
instructions.instruction: Stir in the crumbled tofu, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Cook for 2–3 minutes until everything is well combined. Remove from the heat and allow the filling to cool.
instructions.tip: Taste the filling before wrapping and adjust the soy sauce if needed.

instructions.title: Soften the wrappers
instructions.instruction: Fill a wide shallow dish with room-temperature water. Dip one rice paper sheet briefly until just pliable, then place it on a clean, slightly damp board.
instructions.tip: Do not soak the wrappers for too long; they continue softening after being removed from the water.

instructions.title: Wrap the dumplings
instructions.instruction: Place a small spoonful of filling near the lower centre of the wrapper. Fold the bottom over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll tightly to form a sealed parcel. Wrap a second softened sheet around each dumpling for extra strength.
instructions.tip: Keep the parcels small and well sealed to reduce the chance of tearing.

instructions.title: Pan-fry until crisp
instructions.instruction: Heat the remaining neutral oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Place the dumplings apart from one another and fry for 3–4 minutes per side, turning carefully, until golden and crisp.
instructions.tip: Rice paper can stick together, so leave space between dumplings and turn gently with a spatula.

instructions.title: Mix the dipping sauce and serve
instructions.instruction: Mix the rice vinegar with the remaining soy sauce if desired, chilli oil, and sesame seeds. Serve the dumplings hot with the dipping sauce.
instructions.tip: Serve straight from the pan for the best contrast between crisp wrappers and soft filling.

tips: Keep the rice paper sheets separate while working because softened wrappers stick easily.
Let the filling cool completely before wrapping.
For a non-vegetarian version, replace tofu with finely minced cooked chicken or prawns.

title: Salmon noodle soup
description: A warming Asian-inspired noodle soup with tender salmon, rice noodles, ginger, garlic, and a savoury soy-based broth. Fresh greens, spring onions, and lime brighten the bowl, making it a comforting yet light meal.

ingredients.item: Salmon fillets, skin removed and cut into chunks

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook or soak the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and rinse briefly with warm water, then set aside.
instructions.tip: Keep the noodles separate from the broth until serving to prevent them becoming overly soft.

instructions.title: Build the broth
instructions.instruction: Heat the sesame oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 30–60 seconds until fragrant without browning.
instructions.tip: Gentle cooking preserves the fresh aroma of the ginger and garlic.

instructions.title: Simmer the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Pour in the stock and soy sauce and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the carrot and cook for 4–5 minutes, then add the pak choi and simmer for another 2–3 minutes.
instructions.tip: Add firmer vegetables first so everything becomes tender at the same time.

instructions.title: Poach the salmon
instructions.instruction: Lower the salmon chunks into the gently simmering broth. Cook for approximately 4–6 minutes, depending on their size, until the fish is opaque and reaches 63°C internally.
instructions.tip: Avoid vigorous boiling, which can break the salmon apart.

instructions.title: Season the soup
instructions.instruction: Stir in the lime juice and black pepper. Taste the broth and add a little more soy sauce or lime juice if needed.
instructions.tip: Balance the savoury broth with acidity rather than adding excessive salt.

instructions.title: Assemble and serve
instructions.instruction: Divide the noodles among four bowls. Ladle over the hot broth, vegetables, and salmon, then garnish with spring onions and fresh coriander.
instructions.tip: Serve immediately while the salmon is tender and the greens remain bright.

tips: Use low-sodium stock and adjust the soy sauce to taste.
Add mushrooms or spinach for extra vegetables.
Store the broth and noodles separately if preparing ahead.

title: Salmon noodle wraps
description: Fresh rice paper wraps filled with flaky salmon, rice noodles, crunchy vegetables, and fragrant herbs, served with a tangy soy-lime dipping sauce. These light wraps are ideal for lunch, picnics, or a make-your-own dinner spread.

instructions.title: Cook the noodles
instructions.instruction: Prepare the rice vermicelli according to the package instructions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside to cool.
instructions.tip: Drain the noodles well so excess water does not make the wraps slippery.

instructions.title: Cook the salmon
instructions.instruction: Pat the salmon dry and season with black pepper. Heat the neutral oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the salmon for 3–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until it reaches 63°C internally. Allow to cool slightly, then flake into large pieces.
instructions.tip: Remove any pin bones before flaking the cooked fish.

instructions.title: Prepare the dipping sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the soy sauce, lime juice, honey, sesame oil, and grated ginger until combined. Set aside for serving.
instructions.tip: Add a splash of water if you prefer a milder, less salty sauce.

instructions.title: Prepare the wrap station
instructions.instruction: Arrange the cooled noodles, flaked salmon, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, lettuce, mint, and coriander on a clean work surface. Fill a wide shallow dish with room-temperature water.
instructions.tip: Having all fillings ready makes the rice paper easier to handle before it becomes sticky.

instructions.title: Fill and roll
instructions.instruction: Dip one rice paper wrapper briefly in water until pliable. Lay it on a clean board, add a small amount of noodles, salmon, vegetables, and herbs near the lower third, then fold the sides inward and roll tightly. Repeat with the remaining wrappers.
instructions.tip: Do not overfill the wraps, and leave space at the edges for folding.

instructions.title: Serve the wraps
instructions.instruction: Arrange the wraps seam-side down on a serving platter. Serve whole or cut in half with the soy-lime dipping sauce.
instructions.tip: Keep the wraps covered with a slightly damp clean cloth until serving to stop them drying out.

tips: Use room-temperature water for the rice paper rather than hot water, which can make it overly soft.
For easier rolling, place the fillings in a compact line and avoid sharp, protruding pieces.
Serve soon after assembling for the best wrapper texture.

alternatives: Shredded lettuce for a lower-carbohydrate option

title: salt & pepper squid
description: Crispy salt and pepper squid tossed with garlic, chilli and aromatic spices. This popular Chinese-inspired seafood dish makes a delicious starter or snack served with lime wedges and a fresh dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: squid tubes, cleaned and cut into rings

instructions.title: Prepare the squid
instructions.instruction: Pat the squid rings thoroughly dry with paper towels. Dry squid helps the coating adhere and become crisp instead of steaming.
instructions.tip: Remove excess moisture before coating.

instructions.title: Mix the coating
instructions.instruction: Combine cornflour, plain flour, five-spice powder, white pepper and half the salt in a large bowl. Toss the squid rings in the mixture until evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Shake off excess flour to keep the coating light.

instructions.title: Heat the oil
instructions.instruction: Heat vegetable oil in a deep, heavy saucepan to 180°C. Prepare a plate lined with paper towels for draining the cooked squid.
instructions.tip: Use a thermometer if possible to maintain an even frying temperature.

instructions.title: Fry until crisp
instructions.instruction: Fry the squid in small batches for 1–2 minutes, until the coating is lightly golden and crisp. Remove promptly and drain on paper towels.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcrowding the pan, which lowers the oil temperature.

instructions.title: Add the aromatics
instructions.instruction: In a clean frying pan, heat 1 tablespoon of fresh oil over medium-high heat. Add the garlic, chilli and spring onions and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the garlic moving so it does not burn.

instructions.title: Season and serve
instructions.instruction: Add the fried squid to the pan, sprinkle with the remaining salt and toss briefly with the aromatics. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
instructions.tip: Serve straight away for the best crunch.

tips: Cut the squid into similarly sized rings so they cook evenly.
Fry in small batches to keep the coating crisp.
For extra fragrance, add a pinch of Sichuan pepper to the seasoning.

alternatives: thin strips of firm white fish

title: Sea bass with sizzled ginger, chilli & spring onions
description: Tender sea bass fillets are steamed until flaky and topped with sizzling ginger, fresh chilli and spring onions. A simple Chinese-inspired dish with delicate flavours, ideal with steamed rice and greens.

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

instructions.title: Prepare the fish
instructions.instruction: Pat the sea bass fillets dry and place them skin-side up on a heatproof plate that fits inside a steamer. Make sure the fillets lie in a single layer.
instructions.tip: Choose fillets of similar thickness so they cook evenly.

instructions.title: Season the fish
instructions.instruction: Mix the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and sesame oil in a small bowl. Spoon half the mixture over the fillets and scatter half the ginger on top.
instructions.tip: Keep some sauce aside to dress the fish after steaming.

instructions.title: Steam until flaky
instructions.instruction: Bring water to a steady boil in a steamer or wok. Set the plate inside, cover and steam for 7–10 minutes, depending on thickness, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
instructions.tip: Avoid overcooking; thin fillets may finish sooner.

instructions.title: Arrange the aromatics
instructions.instruction: Carefully remove the plate from the steamer. Scatter the remaining ginger, spring onions and sliced chilli over the cooked fish.
instructions.tip: Use oven mitts and take care around the hot steam.

instructions.title: Sizzle the oil
instructions.instruction: Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan until shimmering but not smoking. Carefully pour it over the ginger, chilli and spring onions so they sizzle and release their aroma.
instructions.tip: Pour slowly to avoid splashing hot oil.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Drizzle the reserved soy mixture over the fish, garnish with coriander and serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions.tip: Serve the fish with the aromatic juices collected on the plate.

tips: Ask your fishmonger to remove the pin bones if needed.
Keep the ginger finely cut for a delicate texture.
Add extra chilli at the table for guests who enjoy more heat.

alternatives: extra water with a small splash of rice vinegar

title: Streak & Vietnamese noodle salad
description: A fresh Vietnamese-inspired noodle salad featuring seared steak, crunchy vegetables, fragrant herbs and rice noodles tossed in a bright lime and fish sauce dressing. It balances savoury, sweet, sour and spicy flavours in a satisfying meal.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk together the fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, minced garlic, chilli and 2 tablespoons of water until the sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust the lime or sugar as needed.
instructions.tip: The dressing should taste balanced, with a clear tangy and savoury flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the noodles
instructions.instruction: Cook or soak the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain, rinse briefly under cool water and set aside to drain thoroughly.
instructions.tip: Do not leave the noodles sitting in water, or they may become soggy.

instructions.title: Season and sear the steak
instructions.instruction: Pat the steak dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan over high heat and sear the steak for 3–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and preferred doneness.
instructions.tip: Let the steak rest for 5–10 minutes before slicing across the grain.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Place the carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, spring onions, mint and coriander in a large salad bowl. Keep the vegetables raw for a crisp, refreshing texture.
instructions.tip: Cut the vegetables into similar thin strips for easy eating.

instructions.title: Slice the steak
instructions.instruction: Slice the rested steak thinly across the grain. Add the cooled rice noodles and sliced steak to the bowl of vegetables.
instructions.tip: Slicing across the grain helps keep the steak tender.

instructions.title: Toss and serve
instructions.instruction: Pour most of the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything is coated. Divide among bowls and finish with chopped peanuts and the remaining dressing to taste.
instructions.tip: Add the dressing just before serving to keep the vegetables crisp.

tips: Use leftover cooked steak for a quicker version.
For a milder salad, remove the chilli seeds before chopping.
Keep extra dressing on the side so each person can adjust the flavour.

alternatives: soy sauce with a little extra lime juice

title: Tangy carrot, cabbage & onion salad
description: A crunchy, colourful salad of shredded carrot, cabbage and onion dressed with vinegar, citrus and a touch of sweetness. It works as a refreshing side dish alongside grilled foods, sandwiches or rice bowls.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Remove any damaged outer cabbage leaves, then shred the cabbage finely. Grate the carrots and slice the red onion as thinly as possible.
instructions.tip: A sharp knife or mandoline helps create evenly cut vegetables.

instructions.title: Soften the onion
instructions.instruction: Place the sliced onion in a small bowl with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Leave for 5 minutes to mellow its sharpness.
instructions.tip: This quick soak gives the onion a gentler flavour.

instructions.title: Whisk the dressing
instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk the apple cider vinegar, olive oil, honey, Dijon mustard, remaining salt and black pepper until combined.
instructions.tip: Taste the dressing before adding it to the vegetables.

instructions.title: Combine the salad
instructions.instruction: Put the cabbage and grated carrot in a large bowl. Add the onion along with its lemon juice, then pour over the dressing.
instructions.tip: Use clean hands or salad tongs to distribute the dressing evenly.

instructions.title: Toss and rest
instructions.instruction: Toss thoroughly, gently squeezing a handful of cabbage to help it begin absorbing the dressing. Leave the salad for 10–15 minutes.
instructions.tip: A short rest softens the cabbage slightly while keeping it crunchy.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir through the chopped parsley, taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve chilled or at room temperature.
instructions.tip: Drain off excess liquid if preparing the salad well ahead.

tips: For a sharper flavour, add another teaspoon of vinegar.
Prepare the salad up to a few hours ahead and refrigerate it.
Add sliced apple for extra sweetness and crunch.

alternatives: a mixture of green and red cabbage

title: Tofu, greens 7 cashew stir-fry
description: Golden tofu, crisp greens and crunchy cashews come together in a quick savoury stir-fry with garlic, ginger and soy sauce. Serve it with rice for an easy vegetarian dinner packed with texture and flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the sauce
instructions.instruction: Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, cornflour and water in a small bowl until smooth. Set aside near the stove.
instructions.tip: Mix the sauce again just before using because the cornflour may settle.

instructions.title: Brown the tofu
instructions.instruction: Pat the tofu dry and cut it into bite-sized cubes. Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 6–8 minutes, turning until golden on several sides. Transfer to a plate.
instructions.tip: Give the tofu space in the pan so it browns instead of steaming.

instructions.title: Toast the cashews
instructions.instruction: Add the cashews to the dry pan and toast for 1–2 minutes, stirring frequently until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
instructions.tip: Watch carefully because nuts can burn quickly.

instructions.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Add the remaining oil to the pan. Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the broccoli and bell pepper. Cook for 3–4 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed.
instructions.tip: Keep the heat high and stir frequently to preserve the vegetables' colour.

instructions.title: Add the greens and sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the pak choi and cook for another 1–2 minutes until just wilted. Return the tofu to the pan, pour in the sauce and toss until it thickens and coats the ingredients.
instructions.tip: If the sauce becomes too thick, add a tablespoon of water.

instructions.title: Finish and serve
instructions.instruction: Stir in the toasted cashews and sesame oil. Serve hot over cooked rice.
instructions.tip: Add the cashews at the end to keep them crunchy.

tips: Press tofu for at least 15 minutes for a firmer texture.
Prepare and measure all ingredients before heating the wok.
Use a mix of seasonal greens if broccoli and pak choi are unavailable.

title: Turkey Bánh mì
description: A Vietnamese-inspired baguette sandwich filled with seasoned turkey, tangy pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, coriander and a lightly spicy mayonnaise. It delivers a satisfying combination of savoury meat, crunchy vegetables and fresh herbs.

instructions.title: Quick-pickle the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Place the carrot and daikon in a bowl. Stir the rice vinegar, sugar, salt and 3 tablespoons of water until dissolved, then pour over the vegetables. Leave for at least 15 minutes.
instructions.tip: Drain the pickles well before assembling the sandwiches.

instructions.title: Season the turkey
instructions.instruction: Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce and minced garlic. Coat the turkey cutlets in the mixture and leave for 10 minutes while the pickles rest.
instructions.tip: Keep the turkey refrigerated if marinating for longer.

instructions.title: Cook the turkey
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey for 4–6 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until browned and the centre reaches 74°C. Rest briefly, then slice thinly.
instructions.tip: Use a food thermometer to confirm the turkey is fully cooked.

instructions.title: Prepare the spicy mayonnaise
instructions.instruction: Mix the mayonnaise and sriracha in a small bowl. Taste and add more sriracha if you prefer a spicier sandwich.
instructions.tip: Add a squeeze of lime for a brighter flavour.

instructions.title: Prepare the baguettes
instructions.instruction: Split the baguettes lengthwise without cutting all the way through. Warm them briefly in an oven until the crust is lightly crisp and the centres remain soft.
instructions.tip: Avoid over-toasting the bread, which can make it difficult to bite.

instructions.title: Assemble the bánh mì
instructions.instruction: Spread spicy mayonnaise inside each baguette. Add sliced turkey, drained pickled vegetables, cucumber, coriander and chilli. Serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Keep the pickles and sandwich filling separate until serving if preparing ahead.

tips: Use a crusty, light baguette for the best texture.
Prepare the pickled vegetables a day ahead for deeper flavour.
Adjust the chilli and mayonnaise to suit your preferred heat level.

title: Vegan banh mi
description: A plant-based Vietnamese-style baguette sandwich filled with savoury marinated tofu, quick-pickled carrot and daikon, crisp cucumber and fresh coriander. A creamy chilli spread and crunchy bread bring all the flavours together.

instructions.title: Pickle the vegetables
instructions.instruction: Combine the rice vinegar, sugar, 3 tablespoons of water and a pinch of salt. Add the carrot and daikon and leave to pickle for 15–20 minutes, stirring once or twice.
instructions.tip: Make sure the vegetables are cut thinly so they pickle quickly.

instructions.title: Marinate the tofu
instructions.instruction: Cut the pressed tofu into slabs. Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and garlic, then coat the tofu and leave for 10 minutes.
instructions.tip: Pat the tofu dry before marinating for better browning.

instructions.title: Pan-fry the tofu
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and lightly crisp. Slice into strips.
instructions.tip: Allow each side to brown before turning.

instructions.title: Make the chilli spread
instructions.instruction: Stir the vegan mayonnaise and chilli sauce together. Taste and adjust the heat to your preference.
instructions.tip: Add a little lime juice for extra tang.

instructions.title: Warm the bread
instructions.instruction: Split the baguettes lengthwise and warm them in a hot oven for 3–4 minutes until crisp outside but still soft inside.
instructions.tip: Choose baguettes without dairy or other non-vegan ingredients.

instructions.title: Build the sandwiches
instructions.instruction: Spread the chilli mayonnaise inside each baguette. Fill with tofu, drained pickled vegetables, cucumber, coriander and sliced chilli. Serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Add the pickled vegetables just before eating to keep the bread from becoming soggy.

tips: Press tofu for 15–20 minutes to improve its texture.
Add sliced jalapeños or extra chilli for more heat.
Keep the pickled vegetables refrigerated in a clean container for several days.

title: Vietnamese caramel trout
description: Trout fillets are glazed in a Vietnamese-inspired caramel fish sauce with garlic, ginger and a touch of chilli. The sauce reduces to a glossy, sweet-salty coating that pairs beautifully with steamed rice and fresh greens.

instructions.title: Prepare the caramel sauce
instructions.instruction: Mix the fish sauce, brown sugar and water in a small bowl until most of the sugar dissolves. Set aside near the stove.
instructions.tip: Measure the sauce ingredients before cooking because the caramel can darken quickly.

instructions.title: Sear the trout
instructions.instruction: Pat the trout dry and check for pin bones. Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the fillets skin-side down and cook for 3–4 minutes until the skin is crisp.
instructions.tip: Press gently for the first few seconds to help the skin make contact with the pan.

instructions.title: Turn and add aromatics
instructions.instruction: Turn the fillets carefully and cook for another 1–2 minutes. Add the shallot, garlic, ginger and chilli around the fish and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
instructions.tip: Keep the aromatics from sitting directly on the hottest part of the pan for too long.

instructions.title: Glaze the fish
instructions.instruction: Pour the prepared sauce into the pan. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 3–5 minutes, spooning the sauce over the trout as it thickens into a glossy glaze.
instructions.tip: Do not let the sugar burn; lower the heat if the sauce darkens too quickly.

instructions.title: Finish the sauce
instructions.instruction: Add the lime juice and turn the pan gently so the glaze coats the fillets. Cook until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, reaching 63°C at the thickest point.
instructions.tip: Trout cooks quickly, so check the centre before extending the cooking time.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Scatter spring onions over the trout and spoon the remaining caramel sauce over each fillet. Serve hot with jasmine rice and steamed vegetables.
instructions.tip: A squeeze of fresh lime at the table balances the sweet-savoury glaze.

tips: Use a non-stick pan to help keep the trout fillets intact.
Taste the sauce before reducing; add a little water if it seems too salty.
Serve with steamed pak choi, broccoli or green beans.

alternatives: soy sauce with a small amount of lime juice

title: Vietnamese chicken salad
description: A bright Vietnamese-style chicken salad combines shredded chicken, crunchy cabbage, carrot, cucumber and fresh herbs with a punchy lime, fish sauce and chilli dressing. It is light, refreshing and full of contrasting textures.

instructions.title: Cook the chicken
instructions.instruction: Place the chicken breasts in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the centre reaches 74°C. Remove and let cool slightly.
instructions.tip: Keep the water at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil to help the chicken stay tender.

instructions.title: Shred the chicken
instructions.instruction: When cool enough to handle, shred the chicken into bite-sized strips using two forks. Set aside while you prepare the vegetables.
instructions.tip: Shred along the grain for long strands that mix well into the salad.

instructions.title: Make the dressing
instructions.instruction: Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic, chilli and water until the sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust the balance of sourness, sweetness and saltiness.
instructions.tip: Add a little more lime juice if the dressing tastes too sweet.

instructions.title: Prepare the vegetables and herbs
instructions.instruction: Place the shredded cabbage, carrot, cucumber and red onion in a large bowl. Roughly tear the mint and coriander leaves and add them to the vegetables.
instructions.tip: Keep the vegetable strips thin for a pleasant texture.

instructions.title: Toss the salad
instructions.instruction: Add the shredded chicken and pour over most of the dressing. Toss thoroughly so the chicken and vegetables are evenly coated.
instructions.tip: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes to absorb the dressing.

instructions.title: Garnish and serve
instructions.instruction: Divide the salad among serving plates, sprinkle with chopped peanuts and drizzle over the remaining dressing to taste. Serve immediately.
instructions.tip: Add peanuts at the last moment to preserve their crunch.

tips: Use leftover roast or poached chicken to shorten preparation time.
Add sliced red bell pepper for extra colour and sweetness.
Keep the dressing separate if preparing the salad well in advance.

alternatives: soy sauce with extra lime juice

title: Turkish lahmacun
description: Turkish lahmacun is a thin, crisp flatbread topped with a finely minced mixture of beef, tomato, pepper, onion and fragrant spices. It is baked until the edges are crisp and commonly served rolled up with fresh parsley, lemon and salad.

ingredients.item: Aleppo pepper or mild chilli flakes

instructions.title: Make the dough
instructions.instruction: Combine the flour, yeast and salt in a bowl. Add the warm water and olive oil, then mix until a rough dough forms. Knead for 7–8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
instructions.tip: Add a teaspoon of water at a time if the dough feels too dry.

instructions.title: Let the dough rise
instructions.instruction: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and leave in a warm place for 45–60 minutes, until slightly risen. It does not need to double dramatically.
instructions.tip: Keep the dough covered to prevent the surface from drying.

instructions.title: Prepare the topping
instructions.instruction: Finely chop the onion, bell pepper and tomato. Combine with the ground beef, tomato paste, garlic, cumin, paprika, Aleppo pepper and parsley. Mix thoroughly until the topping is spreadable.
instructions.tip: Chop the vegetables finely so they cook quickly and do not make the topping too chunky.

instructions.title: Shape the flatbreads
instructions.instruction: Heat the oven to 240°C and place a heavy baking tray inside to heat. Divide the dough into 4 equal portions and roll each into a very thin round or oval on a lightly floured surface.
instructions.tip: Thin dough is key to the crisp texture of lahmacun.

instructions.title: Spread the meat mixture
instructions.instruction: Spread a thin, even layer of the raw meat topping over each dough round, pressing it gently across the surface and leaving only a narrow border.
instructions.tip: Keep the topping layer thin so the meat cooks through as the bread crisps.

instructions.title: Bake and serve
instructions.instruction: Carefully place each lahmacun on the hot tray and bake for 6–9 minutes, working in batches if needed, until the base is crisp and the meat is fully cooked with no pink remaining. Serve hot with lemon wedges and extra parsley.
instructions.tip: Check the centre of the topping is fully cooked before serving.

tips: Use a food processor to finely chop the topping vegetables, but avoid turning them into a watery puree.
Preheat the baking tray thoroughly to help the base crisp.
Serve with lemon, parsley, thinly sliced onion and a simple tomato salad.

alternatives: a mixture of beef and lamb
paprika with a pinch of cayenne
